en.name: Carpet
description:
From the second half of the 16th century, textiles were among the most frequently traded and most profitable goods introduced into Portugal through the Carreira da India, the route that from 1498 directly connected Europe to Asia. Despite Indian cloth having first constituted the majority of imported textiles, Persian textiles also arrived in Portugal during the first half of the 16th century in smaller quantities. Among these, knotted-pile carpets were in high demand within the upper classes of cosmopolitan Portuguese society, as elements of luxury and status that since the mid-16th century successfully displaced previous Spanish and Turkish imports.  
This small carpet, from the Santa Clara convent in Évora, embodies the Golden Age of importation, when the colourful and vivid Persian imaginary was proudly displayed in both sacred and profane European interiors. In its multicoloured decoration, we can see an elaborate ornamental network of “vine scrolls” interlaced with palmettes outlining the decorative geometry of the field. In addition, there are S-shaped cloud scrolls (*tchi*), rosettes and lotus flowers, arranged on a bright-red background, which contrasts with the dark-blue colour of the border, itself filled with palmettes and lotus flowers.
keywords: Carpet; Iran; 17th century; Portugal
materials: Cotton and wool; knotted; knot, 2Z; asymmetric knot, open to the left
tags: Asymmetric knot, Open to the left
partner: National Museum of Ancient Art ‒ MNAA

en.name: Stengelglas
description: In the complete course of art history, rarely has there been a movement in which the decorative arts played such an integral role as Art Nouveau. Among these arts, glass held the most important role by far. As a very flexible and mostly transparent material, glass provided an ideal medium in which artists of the movement could express their ideas that were inspired by nature and organic forms. The style, originating in England, spread throughout Europe; yet the most notable places it set its roots were Belgium, France, the Czech Republic, Germany and Austria. Known as Jugendstil in the German-speaking lands, the movement beared witness to divine glass creations from many, now world-famous, craftspeople who have truly earned honourable mentions in the history of the decorative and applied arts. An essential place for the birth and development of the Jugendstil in Vienna was the Wiener Werkstätte (Vienna Workshops), founded by Josef Hoffmann and Koloman Moser. The main aim of the workshops was to bring the artist or designer closer to the craftspeople and technicians entrusted with the execution of their designs, while also encouraging the designers to be their own crafters. The Wiener Werkstättewas host to a large number of Austrian craftspeople, such as Dagobert Peche, Otto Prutscher and Ludwig Heinrich Jungnickel. This drinking glass is the creation of Otto Prutscher, who produced his best works in the period between his graduation from the Kunstgewerbeschule in AD 1901 and the outbreak of World War I. Standing on a long stem, the bowl of the glass is decorated with silver-stained oval facets. This object is an excellent example of Prutscher’s early designs, which borrowed heavily from the rectilinear and modular language that Josef Hoffman and Koloman Moser worked out in the beginning of the century.
artist: Prutscher, Otto (design); Meyr's Neffe (manufacturer); Wiener Werkstätte (retailer)
materials: Crystal glass; glass cutting, silver stain, stained
partner: MAK – Austrian Museum of Applied Arts / Contemporary Art

en.name: Ponte dell'Ammiraglio
description: The Ponte dell’Ammiraglio (Bridge of the Admiral), so called because it was built in about the second quarter of the 12th century by Admiral Giorgio d’Antiochia in the service of King Ruggero II who was likewise founder of the Church of Santa Maria dell’Ammiraglio, now lies underground and is fenced in, lower by about three metres in relation to the level of the Corso dei Mille, with which it is aligned. The bridge, the passage across the River Oreto, was erected near the Porta Termini. It presents a configuration in “saddle- back” form, with two characteristic specula ramps and is composed of seven spans on flying buttresses with arches *a rincasso*, the height descending from the centre to the two ends. The six massive pillars have fornix openings above the level of the water so as to gear down the spray of the river in full spate. The whole structure is achieved with limestone ashlars cut in regular shapes, and on account of the technology and morphology, proposes once again a typology diffused throughout the area of the Maghreb. During the years, the course of the river underwent notable displacement in the area near its mouth and the modification of the configuration, itself of the riverbed, to the extent that in 1838 it was necessary to construct a new bridge, called Ponte delle Teste (Bridge of the Heads).

es.name: Puente del Almirante
description: El Puente del Almirante, llamado así porque lo hizo construir, alrededor del segundo cuarto del siglo XII (según algunos, en 1132), el almirante Giorgio de Antioquía —que estaba al servicio del rey Ruggero II, y fundador asimismo de la iglesia de Santa María del Almirante—, está actualmente desecado y circunscrito en un recinto tres metros por debajo del nivel del Corso dei Mille, al cual está unido. El puente, paso sobre el río Oreto, se levantó cerca de la Puerta Termini. Presenta una configuración en “lomo de asno”, con las dos características rampas simétricas, y está constituido por siete ojos de arco ojival rehundido y altura decreciente desde el centro a los extremos. Los seis gruesos pilones tienen aberturas en arco sobre el nivel del agua para aminorar el empuje del río en las crecidas. Toda la estructura está realizada con sillares de calcarenita de corte regular, y retoma, por técnica y forma, una tipología difundida en el área magrebí. En su tiempo, el curso del río sufrió en ese tramo, cerca de la desembocadura, un notable desplazamiento y la modificación de la propia configuración del lecho, tanto que, en 1838, fue necesaria la construcción de un nuevo puente, llamado Puente de las Cabezas (Ponte delle Teste).

de.name: Nördliche Seitenfassade
description: An den Seitenfassaden finden sich keine religiösen Motive mehr, sie sind rein der Schaulust des Betrachters überlassen. Während an der Südseite ein Scheinfenster mit einer herausblickenden Dame zu sehen ist, sind im Norden überwiegend exotische Tiere dargestellt, der damaligen Mode entsprechend. Auf dem Gesims sitzen drei Affen mit einem Früchtekorb, darüber ein Papagei auf einem Stab und eine Katze am anderen Ende des Gesimses.

en.name: Northern side façade
description: Religious motifs are no longer to be found on the side façades instead they are completely devoted to the amusement of the viewer. While the south side features a false window with a woman looking out, the north side is largely decorated with exotic animals in accordance with the fashion of the time. Three monkeys are sitting on the cornice with a basket of fruit, above them a parrot on a stick and a cat at the other end of the cornice.

en.name: *Izzedin Yusuf Effendi (1875–1916)*
short_description: Portrait of Izzedin Yusuf Effendi (1875–1916). He was the heir to the throne. In 1916 he committed suicide.
keywords: Izzedin Yusuf Effendi

ar.name: حقة
description: حقة كمثرية الشكل على الطراز الصيني، مكسوه ببطانة لونها أزرق كوبالتي، نفذت عليها زخارف باللون الأبيض ولون مؤكسد تحت طلاء تزجيج شفاف.

en.name: *Huqqa*
description: Pear-shaped *huqqa* pipe reservoir, in Chinese style, covered with a cobalt blue engobe, painted in white and ochre slips under a transparent colourless glaze.
keywords: Huqqa; China; Iran; Glaze

en.name: *Mokhfia* conical dish
description:
This conical plate, or *mokhfia*, is concave on a ring-shaped base. It has an arcade decoration called "turtle". In the centre of the dish a five-pointed star with green central point is inscribed in a double circle. Six blue dots are inside and five are outside of this star. From this central motif is a radiating design of five large green rounded forms, or scales, each with two dots on either side of a wide decorative stripe edged in yellow. The inside rim of the cup features a braided pattern enhanced with small blue strokes. This particular decoration and type of ceramic are characteristic of Moroccan work between the 17th and 19th centuries. They are widespread in Morocco and Spain. We note the Andalusian influence in certain motifs, such as the use of geometry.  
This piece cannot be attributed with certainty to a single production centre. However, Fes is the most important one of the period. The decoration with concentric arches called "turtle" is characteristic of these polychrome Moroccan ceramics. In the 19th century, the colours used were more assertive, the shapes heavier, and the designs less spontaneous than before.
holder: Museum of the Arab World Institute
materials: Ceramic with polychrome decoration enhanced with red lead
tags: Ceramic with polychrome decoration enhanced with red lead
partner: Museum of the Arab World Institute

fr.name: Plat conique *mokhfia*
description:
Ce plat conique dit mokhfia est très creux sur une base annulaire. Il présente un décor d'arcatures dit de "tortue". Au centre du plat, une étoile à cinq branches avec un point central vert s'inscrit dans un double cercle. Six points bleus occupent l'intérieur et cinq l'extérieur de cette étoile. A partir de ce motif central se développe un décor rayonnant de cinq grandes arcatures ou "écailles" contenant la même forme peinte en vert avec deux pastilles de part et d'autre d'une large bande décorative quadrillée et cernée de jaune. La bordure intérieure de la coupe comporte un motif tressé rehaussé de petits traits bleus.  
Ce décor et cette forme précise de céramique sont caractéristiques des productions marocaines élaborées entre le XVIIe et le XIXe siècle J.-C.. Elles sont très répandues, aussi bien au Maroc qu'en Espagne. D'ailleurs, on note l'influence andalouse dans certains motifs comme l'emploi de la géométrie.  
Cette pièce ne peut pas être attribuée avec certitude à un centre de production. Toutefois, Fès est le plus important de l'époque. Le décor aux arcatures concentriques dit de "tortue" est caractéristique de ces céramiques polychromes marocaines. Au XIXe siècle J.-C., les couleurs employées sont plus affirmées, les formes plus lourdes et les décors moins spontanés qu'avant.
holder: Musée de l'Institut du monde arabe
dates: XIIIe siècle de l'Hégire / XIXe siècle J.-C.

en.name: Jar fragments with incised décor
description:
This fragment, a kitchen ceramic, was excavated in 2007 by the French-Qatari Mission in one of the houses in Murwab. The water jar features a globular body and a high, straight neck with an unpreserved rim. Crafted from creamy white clay with inclusions of sand and basalt, the porous nature of the material makes it well-suited for keeping water cool.  
A vertical decoration, created with a comb, adorns the entire upper part of the body up to the midpoint of the globular section. Additionally, a rounded handle was attached to the neck of the water jar.
dates: AH late 2nd to late 3rd century / AD late 8th to late 9th century
keywords: earthenware, storage, transportation, jar

ar.name: دمية على هيئة راقصة.
description:
يظهر أن الدمية تمثل راقصة، يغلب على الظن أنها كانت تستخدم كلعبة. الشعر أسود اللون غير منتظم. الوجه مدور، ويبدو غير متناسق مقارنة مع باقي الجسد. العينان بارزتان، والأنف دقيق جداً. الرقبة طويلة نسبياً وحجمها ضخم. الثدييان كبيران نوعاً ما، بينما البطن الأهيف جداً مشار إليه بأخدودين متراصين فوق بعضهما. أعضاء الدمية العلوية مبتورة، أما أعضاؤها السفلية فينقصها القدمان، ويغطيها سروال من الطراز الشرقي.  
إن هيكل الدمية، الذي تم إدخال بنية خشبية إلى داخله بغية تأمين بعض الصلابة له، مصنوع من العاج المصمت. الدمية مجسمة بدقة كبيرة لكنها غير متناسقة. وسمات الوجه رافدية بشكل نموذجي، وتشبه عدة تصويرات مماثلة لها على أطباق من الخزفيات أو على قطع من الجبس .

يجسد هذا التمثال الصغير ذو الشكل الرافدي راقصة منحوتة بدقة من العاج المصمت؛ وتوفر بنية من الخشب بعض الصلابة لهيكله؛ ويمكن أن نقارنه بالعديد من التمثيلات المماثلة المزينة للصحون الفخارية أو للقطع المصنوعة من الجص.
keywords: العاج؛  نحت؛ زخرفة تصويرية؛ دمية؛ راقصة.

en.name: Figure of a dancer.
description:
The figure appears to be a dancer and was almost certainly a toy. The black hair is tousled. The round face with big eyes and a thin nose seems out of proportion with the body. The neck is very thick. The breasts are prominent but the abdomen, defined by two sets of grooves, is quite slim.  
The figure has lost its arms. The legs are covered by a type of Oriental trouser (*sirwal*) and the feet are missing.  
A wooden framework has been inserted inside the piece of ivory to give it rigidity.  
The figure is hardly harmonious but it is finely modelled. The facial features are typically Mesopotamian and they resemble those found on several contemporary pottery plates or stucco objects.

This finely carved figurine of a dancing girl of typically Mesopotamian physiognomy is made of solid ivory, with a wooden framework affording it a degree of stability. It is comparable to several similar images found on ceramic dishes and stucco objects.
keywords: Ivory; carving; figurative decoration

es.name: Figura de bailarina
description:
La estatuilla, que parece representar a una bailarina, debió de utilizarse como juguete. El negro cabello está despeinado. El rostro, redondo, con ojos intensamente marcados y afiliada nariz, no guarda proporción con el resto del cuerpo. El cuello es relativamente largo y bastante ancho. El pecho es bastante prominente, mientras que el vientre, marcado por dos estrías superpuestas, es de una gran esbeltez.  
La figura carece de miembros superiores; sus miembros inferiores, a los que les faltan los pies, están cubiertos con un pantalón de estilo oriental (*sirwal*).  
La figura es de marfil, pero tiene en su interior una estructura de madera a fin de dotarla de cierta rigidez. A pesar de no ser armoniosa, la estatuilla está modelada con elegancia. Los rasgos del rostro son típicamente mesopotámicos y se asemejan a varias representaciones análogas encontradas en platos de cerámica o en objetos de estuco.

Esta figurita de marfil representa a una bailarina con rasgos típicamente mesopotámicos y está modelada con elegancia. Una estructura de madera le proporciona una cierta rigidez. Se asemeja a varias representaciones análogas encontradas en platos de cerámica o en objetos de estuco.
dates: Siglo III de la Hégira / IX d. C.
keywords: Marfil; escultura; decoración figurativa

fr.name: Figurine d’une danseuse.
description: La figurine semble représenter une danseuse et servait très probablement de jouet. La chevelure noire est désordonnée. Le visage, arrondi avec des yeux bien marqués et un nez très fin, paraît disproportionné par rapport au reste du corps. Le cou, relativement long, est de gros calibre. Les seins sont assez développés alors que le ventre, très svelte, est marqué par deux rainures superposées. La figurine est amputée de ses membres supérieurs. Ses membres inférieurs, auxquels il manque les pieds, sont couverts d'un pantalon de type oriental (sirwal). La carcasse de la figurine, à l'intérieur de laquelle fut introduite une structure en bois pour lui assurer une certaine rigidité, est en ivoire massif. Sans être harmonieuse, la figurine est très finement modelée. Les traits du visage sont typiquement mésopotamiens et ressemblent à plusieurs représentations analogues sur des plats de céramique ou des objets en stuc.

Représentant une danseuse à la physionomie typiquement mésopotamienne, la figurine, finement modelée, est en ivoire massif. Une structure en bois assure une certaine rigidité à sa carcasse. Elle est comparable à plusieurs représentations analogues sur les plats de céramique ou des objets en stuc.
dates: IIIe siècle de l’Hégire (IXe siècle J.-C.).
keywords: Ivoire; sculpture; décoration figurative
partner: Musée des Arts islamiques de Monastir

en.name: Pendant necklace
description: This beautiful triangular pendant necklace shows a loop chain decorated with four little floral ornaments and the main pendant decorated small red and green mounted crystals. This also has a shared connection with the traditional Fátima Hand motif.
keywords: Silver; Protection; Personal attire; Women

en.name: A Tunisian decoration (on the right) and an Italian decoration (on the left) awarded to a member of the Moreno family
short_description:
Two members of the Moreno family, Raffaello (Tunis 1844-1913) and his brother Leone (Tunis, 1852-1940) were awarded honours both by the Italian King (Cavaliere dell’Ordine della Corona d’Italia) and by the Bey of Tunis (Nichan Iftikhar). The Morenos were Jews from Livorno (Italy), who had migrated to Tunisia in the early 19th century.  
Other Italians migrants in Tunisia were awarded both the title of Cavaliere dell’Ordine della Corona d’Italia by the Italian King and the title of Nichan Iftikhar by the Bey of Tunis, including Giuseppe Di Vittorio (a Sicilian who ran a construction company) and Luigi Rey (born in Tunis to an immigrant family from a village north of Turin, Piedmont, Italy, who also ran a construction company) and the Jewish Doctor Giacomo Castelnuovo.

ar.name: قلعة الشوبك.
description:
في عام 509 / 1115 قاد بلدوين الأول – مؤسس مملكة اللاتين في القدس - حملة عسكرية على المنطقة الواقعة جنوب شرق البحر الميت، فعبر وادي عربة حتى وصل إلى الشوبك الغنية بالأشجار الكثيفة والينابيع الطبيعية. هناك وعلى قمة جبل عالٍ يطل على الوديان التي تجري فيها المياه، شرع في بناء قلعة أطلق عليها اسم Crac de Montereal، وعيّن رومان لابوي والياً عليها وعلى الأراضي الواقعة شرقي نهر الأردن.  
  
ترتبط قلعة الشوبك مع قلعتين صغيرتين شيِّدتا حول البتراء وداخلها (الوعيرة والحبيس)، جميعها مكّنت الفرنجة من السيطرة على المنطقة الممتدة من البحر الميت إلى خليج العقبة، وفي نفس الوقت التحكم بقوافل الحج والتجارة بين سورية ومصر والحجاز. سقطت قلعة الشوبك سنة 584 / 1188 بيد جنود صلاح الدين الأيوبي، وأعيد تحصينها أكثر من مرة من قبل الأيوبيين (570 - 648 / 1174- 1250) والمماليك (648- 922 / 1250- 1517). في القرنين 12 - 13 / 18 - 19 في العصر العثماني سكن أهالي الشوبك القلعة، ولكنهم أجلوا عنها في القرن 20. لا يزال بإمكان الزائر مشاهدة بقايا أبنية تعود لكل هذه الفترات.  
  
تتخذ قلعة الشوبك شكلاً غير منتظم، أبعاده 175 X 90 م. يوجد داخل القلعة كنيسة ومصلى من زمن البناء الأصلي، بالإضافة إلى مجموعة من الأبنية السكنية التي شيِّدت بكتل حجرية نقلت من مواقع قريبة ومن محاجر تقع على بُعد 1 كم إلى الغرب من القلعة. كذلك يوجد في القلعة العديد من الكتابات العربية المنقوشة بخط النسخ والتي تساعد في التعرف على المراحل المتتابعة لإعادة بناء القلعة وتحصينها. تعتبر الجدران المحيطة والأبراج التي تبرز عنها، بالإضافة إلى السطوح المنحدرة المرصوفة بالحجارة الملساء لمنع الوصول إلى قواعد الأسوار، نموذجاً رائعاً للتحصينات المملوكية وأساليب الدفاع في حالة الحصار.

تمَّ بناء قلعة الشوبك في عام 509 هـ/1115م، بأمر من بالدوين الأول، مُؤسِّس مملكة القدس اللاتينية، الذي أُطلق عليها اسم قلعة مونتريال. وهي متَّصلة بقلعتين أصغر منها في البتراء، مما أدَّى إلى تمكين الفرنجة من فرض بعض السيطرة على المنطقة الممتدة بين البحر الميت وخليج العقبة، مع تعطيل الاتصال التجاري والعسكري بين سورية، ومصر، والحجاز. سقطت الشوبك بيد قوات صلاح الدين في عام 584هـ/1188م. ثمَّة نقوش عربية كثيرة، توثِّق لعمليات إعادة بناء وترميم مختلفة للقلعة، بما فيها أمثلة بديعة من أعمال التحصين المملوكية المبكرة، التي تبيِّن مراحل تطور دفاعات الحصار.
keywords: تحصينات؛ حصن؛ خربة مونريال؛ الصليبيون؛ قلعة.

en.name: Shawbak Castle.
description:
Shawbak is a Crusader, Ayyubid–Mamluk castle of the AH 6th–7th / AD 12th and 13th centuries. Located in southern Jordan, it is 120 km south of Kerak, and 35 km north of the fabulous Nabataean city of Petra. In AH 509 / AD 1115 Baldwin I, founder of the Latin kingdom of Jerusalem, led a major expedition into the region southeast of the Dead Sea. He crossed wadi Araba and marched to the fertile, wooded district of al-Shawbak. There atop a steep mountain, overlooking a well-watered valley, Baldwin erected a huge castle, which he named, 'le Crac de Montreal' and appointed Roman le Puy as lord of Montreal and the land of Oultre Jourdain.  
Shawbak (Montreal) is linked with two smaller fortresses built in and around Petra: al-Habis and al-Wu'ayra. The construction of these castles gave the Franks a loose control over the territory between the Dead Sea and the Gulf of Aqaba, and had the further advantage of hindering both the commercial and military connection between Syria, Egypt and the Hijaz. Shawbak fell to the soldiers of Salah al-Din (Saladin) in AH 584 / AD 1188 and was refortified several times by both the Ayyubids (AH 570–648 / AD 1174–1250) and the Mamluks (AH 648–923 / AD 1250–1517). The Castle was occupied by a village throughout the later Ottoman period (the 18th and 19th centuries AD) and was emptied of its inhabitants only in the 20th century. Considerable remains of all these periods fill the interior.  
Shawbak Castle, which has an irregular shape with maximum dimensions of 175 m x 90 m, possesses a Crusader church and a chapel as well as substantial secular buildings constructed out of stone taken from a nearby antique site and from quarries located one kilometre to the west of the castle. Numerous Arabic inscriptions in *naskhi* script record the various reconstructions of the castle. The impressive rusticated towers; curtain walls and a glacis (a paved slope) wrapped around the castle are fine examples of early Mamluk fortification showing the evolution of siege defences.

Shawbak Castle was built in AH 509 / AD 1115 by Baldwin I, founder of the Latin Kingdom of Jerusalem, who named it Le Crac de Montreal. It is linked with two smaller fortresses at Petra, which gave the Franks loose control over the area between the Dead Sea and the Gulf of Aqaba, and hindered the commercial and military connection between Syria, Egypt and the Hijaz. Shawbak fell to the forces of Salah al-Din in 584 / 1188. Numerous Arabic inscriptions record various reconstructions of the castle, including fine examples of early Mamluk fortification that show the evolution of siege defences.
keywords: Castle; Crac de Montreal; Crusaders; glacis
partner: Ministry of Tourism & Antiquities, Department of Antiquities

es.name: Castillo de Shawbak
description:
Shawbak es un castillo cruzado, ayyubí y mameluco de los siglos VI-VII / XII-XIII. En el año 509 / 1115, Balduino I, fundador del reino latino de Jerusalén, encabezó una importante expedición a la región del sureste del mar Muerto. Cruzó el valle de Araba y marchó hacia la fértil y arbolada zona de al-Shawbak. Allí, sobre una escarpada montaña, dominando un frondoso valle, construyó un enorme castillo que recibió el nombre de Krak de Montreal y nombró a Roman le Puy Señor de Montreal y de la Tierra de Outre-Jourdain.  
Shawbak está relacionado con dos alcázares menores construidos en Petra y alrededores: al-Habis y al Wuayra. La construcción de estos castillos otorgó a los francos un holgado control sobre el territorio que se extiende entre el mar Muerto y el golfo de Aqaba, con la ventaja añadida de que obstaculizaban las conexiones militares y comerciales entre Siria, Egipto y el Hiyaz. Shawbak se rindió a los soldados de Salah al-Din (Saladino) en 584-1188 y fue objeto de varios procesos de refortificación en tiempos de los ayyubíes (570-648 / 1174-1250) y los mamelucos (648-923 / 1250-1517). A finales del periodo otomano (en los siglos XVIII y XIX d. C.), una aldea ocupó todo el castillo, que no quedó deshabitado hasta el siglo XX. En el interior quedan cuantiosos restos de todas estas etapas.  
El castillo Shawbak es de forma irregular y sus dimensiones máximas son de 175 × 90 m; posee una iglesia y una capilla de los cruzados, además de edificios civiles construidos con piedras procedentes de un antiguo yacimiento cercano y de canteras situadas un kilómetro al oeste del castillo.  
Hay numerosas inscripciones en árabe, en letra *nasji*, que dejan constancia de las diversas reconstrucciones de la edificación. Las impresionantes torres de aspecto rústico, los muros de cierre y el glacis (suave pendiente enlosada) que rodean el castillo son ejemplos de los elementos de las primeras fortificaciones mamelucas y demuestran la evolución de las defensas desarrolladas contra los asedios.

El castillo de Shawbak se erigió en 509 / 1115 por orden de Balduino I, fundador del reino de Jerusalén, quien lo bautizó como Krak de Montreal. Está vinculado a dos fortalezas pequeñas de Petra que otorgaron a los francos un holgado control sobre la zona entre el mar Muerto y el golfo de Aqaba y dificultaron las conexiones comerciales y militares entre Siria, Egipto y el Hiyaz. Shawbak se rindió al ejército de Saladino en 584 / 1188. Muchas inscripciones registran las diversas reconstrucciones del castillo; algunas, de principios de la época mameluca, informan de la evolución de los elementos defensivos.
dates: Siglos VI-VII de la Hégira / XII-XIII d. C.
keywords: Castillo; Krak de Montreal; cruzados; glacis.

fr.name: Château de Shawbak.
description:
Shawbak est un château de style composite croisés-ayyoubide-mamelouk des VIe-VIIe siècles H (XIIe-XIIIe siècles J.-C.), situé dans le sud de la Jordanie, à 120 km au sud de Kerak et 35 km au nord de la cité nabatéenne de Pétra. En 509 H / 1115 J.-C., Baudouin Ier, fondateur du royaume latin de Jérusalem, prit la tête d'une grande expédition vers le sud-ouest de la mer Morte. Il franchit le *wadi* Araba et arriva dans la région fertile et boisée d'al-Shawbak. Au sommet d'une montagne escarpée dominant une vallée bien arrosée, il fit ériger un énorme château qu'il nomma le “Krak de Montréal”. Roman le Puy fut nommé seigneur de Montréal et de la terre d'outre-Jourdain.  
Shawbak est à rapprocher de deux forteresses de moindre importance construites dans et autour de Pétra : al-Habis et al-Wu'ayra. La construction de ces châteaux permettait aux Francs de mieux contrôler le territoire entre la mer Morte et le golfe d'Aqaba et de menacer les relations commerciales et militaires entre la Syrie, l'égypte et le Hedjaz. Le château tomba entre les mains de Salah al-Din (Saladin) en 584 H / 1188 J.-C. et ses fortifications furent renforcées à plusieurs reprises par les Ayyoubides (570-648 H / 1174-1250 J.-C.) et les Mamelouks (548-923 H / 1250-1517 J.-C.). Il fut occupé par un village à la fin de la période ottomane (XVIIIe et XIXe siècles) et vidé de ses habitants au XXe. L'intérieur de l'enceinte conserve de considérables vestiges de ces diverses occupations.  
De plan irrégulier de 175 x 90 m, Shawbak possède une église et une chapelle de l'époque croisée ainsi que d'importants bâtiments séculiers dont la pierre provient d'une ancienne carrière toute proche ou d'autres situées à un kilomètre à l'ouest. De nombreuses inscriptions arabes en *naskhi* permettent d'identifier les divers chantiers de reconstruction. Les impressionnantes tours en appareil rustique, les remparts et le glacis (pente pavée) entourant le château sont de remarquables exemples des fortifications du début de la période mamelouke et montrent l'évolution de l'architecture militaire de défense dans cette région.

Le château de Shawbak fut construit en 509 H /1115 J.-C. par Baudouin Ier, fondateur du royaume latin de Jérusalem, qui le nomma le Krak de Montréal. Il est à rapprocher de deux forteresses de moindre importance de Pétra, qui permettaient aux Francs de mieux contrôler le territoire entre la mer Morte et le golfe d'Aqaba, et de menacer les relations commerciales entre la Syrie, l'Égypte et le Hedjaz. Shawbak tomba entre les mains de Salah al-Din (Saladin) en 584 H /1188. De nombreuses inscriptions arabes documentent les différentes reconstructions du château, comme les remarquables exemples des fortifications du début de la période mamelouke qui montrent l'évolution de l'architecture défensive.
dates: VIe-VIIe siècle de l’Hégire (XIIe-XIIIe siècle J.-C.).
dynasty: Période des Croisés ; période ayyoubide ; période mamelouke.
keywords: châteaux ; krac de Montréal ; croisés ; glacis

en.name: Achir
description:
In 323/935, the Fatimide Caliphate al-Qaïm authorised his lieutenant, Ziri ibn Menad, as a result of his loyalty to the dynasty, to found a city. The lieutenant selected a protected site in the Tell Atlas mountains, on the slopes of the Djebel Lakhdar, about 150 km from Algiers. Achir, at first only a village on a mountain top, eventually covered 86 acres. Its ideal geographic location, between the steppes and the Tell Atlas mountains, provided a clear view of the tribes below while making the city unassailable. In effect, the city was used as a base of operations by Ziri, to the advantage of the Fatimides against the Zénata tribes (subjects of the Umayyads of Córdoba), and as a possible fallback position in the face of their frequent attacks.  
  
Ziri was encouraged by the caliphate, which sent him the materials and men necessary for the construction of Achir. His people were reassured by the arrival of many masons and carpenters from M’sila and Tobna who aided, through their knowledge and skill, in the building of homes, the palace, and the city wall. Achir’s urban character derived from the large immigration of people from Tahert and Tlemcen. Intellectual activity developed with the arrival of judges and scholars from these cities. Achir soon seemed to be a real capital, while Ziri, and later his son Bulughin, were considered to be the true rulers of central Maghreb. Historians have emphasised Achir’s impregnability, the abundance of its resources, and its economic and cultural importance. Ibn Hawqal highlights its “markets, agricultural lands, and gardens”, while Ibn Khaldoun states “the most distant countries sent their scholars and businessmen there”.  
  
The city, roughly rectangular in layout, grew in 361/972, and was surrounded by a wall in 366/977, even though, according to Ibn Khaldoun, its position on a steep mountain meant that “ten men would have been adequate to defend it”. Two major routes crossed it; the mosque’s ruins are located at their intersection, and at its highest point stands a watchtower, or manar. Excavations have also revealed the ruins of Ziri’s palace, a magnificent structure of 72 x 40 m. If its high architectural value links it to Abassid architecture of the same period, it also displays earlier Maghreb architectural traits that will be found in la Qal’at, its cousin city, and later in Béjaia or Algiers.  
  
The Ziri emirs regretfully left the city when they went to assume the Kairouan throne, which they inherited from the Fatimides, leaving their uncle Hammad ibn Bulughin to govern in Achir. He ruled so effectively, having increased his army and his territory, that he soon seceded and established his own capital, Al Qal’a of Beni Hammad. Soon it would replace Achir in becoming the capital of the Hammadid kingdom, of which Achir remained a major city until it was taken, in 496/1103, by the Almoravids.

fr.name: Achir
description:
En 323/935, le calife fatimide al-Qaïm autorise son lieutenant, Ziri ibn Menad, en raison de sa loyauté à la dynastie, à créer une ville. Celui-ci choisit un site protégé au coeur de l’Atlas tellien, sur les flancs du djebel Lakhdar, à environ 150 km d’Alger. D’abord village sur un sommet, Achir finit par couvrir 35 hectares. Sa position géographique idéale au contact des steppes et du Tell permettait une surveillance des tribus en même temps qu’elle en faisait une place inexpugnable. La ville servait en effet de base aux expéditions zirides au profit des Fatimides contre les tribus Zénata, vassales des Omeyyades de Cordoue, et de position de repli éventuel contre leurs fréquentes attaques.  
  
Ziri fut encouragé par le calife, qui lui envoya les matériaux et les hommes nécessaires à l’édification d’Achir. Son peuplement fut assuré par l’arrivée de nombreux maçons et charpentiers de M’sila et de Tobna qui aidèrent, par leur savoir-faire, à la construction des demeures, palais et muraille d’Achir, tandis que son caractère urbain lui vint de l’importante immigration des gens de Tahert et de Tlemcen. L’activité intellectuelle se développant avec l’arrivée de juristes et de savants originaires de ces villes, Achir fit bientôt figure de véritable capitale, tandis que Ziri puis son fils Bulughin passaient pour les véritables souverains du Maghreb central. Les historiens ont insisté sur son caractère inexpugnable, l’abondance de ses sources et son importance économique et culturelle. Ibn Hawqal met l’accent sur “ses marchés, ses terrains de culture et ses jardins”, tandis qu’Ibn Khaldoun déclare que “les pays les plus éloignés lui envoient leurs savants et négociants”.  
  
La ville, de plan à peu près rectangulaire, est agrandie en 361/972 et ceinturée d’une muraille en 366/977, même si, d’après Ibn Khaldoun, sa position sur une montagne escarpée faisait que “dix hommes auraient suffi à la défendre”. Deux voies principales la traversaient ; à leur intersection se trouvent les ruines de la mosquée et, sur le point le plus élevé, une tour de guet ou manar. Les fouilles ont aussi révélé les vestiges d’un grand palais, le palais de Ziri, magnifique édifice de 72 x 40 m. Si sa très haute valeur architecturale le rattache à l’architecture abbasside de la même époque, il présente également des traits précurseurs de l’architecture maghrébine qu’on retrouvera aussi bien à la Qalaa, sa cousine, que, plus tardivement, à Béjaia ou Alger.  
  
Les émirs zirides ne quittèrent la ville qu’à regret lorsqu’ils partirent s’installer sur le trône de Kairouan, qu’ils héritaient des Fatimides, laissant à leur oncle Hammad ibn Bulughin le gouvernement d’Achir. Celui-ci s’acquitta si bien de sa tâche qu’il ne tarda pas, ayant agrandi son armée et son domaine, à faire sécession en créant à son tour sa propre capitale, qu’il nomma la Qalaa des Beni Hammad. Celle-ci supplantera bientôt Achir en devenant la capitale du royaume hammadide, dont Achir restera un cheflieu de province avant d’être prise, en 496/1103, par les Almoravides.

en.name: Municipal Museum
names: Municipal Museum de São João de Alporão
description:
Work was begun on the church during the Romanesque period, and the lateral walls and lower part of the façade with one of the first *hood mould* Gothic portals in Portugal, undoubtedly date from this period. The upper part of the church was completed in the 14th and 15th centuries, when the chancel rotunda was built. Nothing remains of the changes made during the Manueline period.  
The contents of the museum are largely made up of archaeological finds and lapidary stones, many items coming from ruined or disaffected monasteries. There are Arab, Gothic and fine Manueline naturalistic capitals and others imported from Genoa at the beginning of the 16th century, as well as the tomb of Duarte de Meneses, Captain of Alcácer-Ceguer and two other 15th-century tombs of João and Martim Docem respectively.

ar.name: أسطرلاب
description: يعتبر هذا الإسطرلاب النادر أحد أقدم الإسطرلابات المعروفة من إسبانيا الإسلامية . ولقد صنع من قبل صانع الإسطرلابات الأندلسي الشهير محمد ابن صفر في قرطبة ويعود تاريخه لعام 411 هجري /1020 ميلادي كما ذكر في التوقيع ضمن الفراغ المربع في جزئه الخلفي. يلي التاريخ نظام الحروف والأرقام العربية المعروف بالأبجدية والسنة مشار لها بتشكيل من الأحرف طاء – ياء – ألف التي تقابل طاء (400) ، ياء (10) وألف (1) والتي يبلغ مجموعها 411 ويحتوي الإسطرلاب ستة لوحات / صفائح التي تقابل لجهتين لكل صفيحة ومن بينها اتجاه مكة ، دمشق ، القاهرة وقرطبة . إن الشبكة من ناحية أخرى هي إضافة جديدة من القرن السابع عشر تمت في تركيا العثمانية. وصانع هذا الإسطرلاب : محمد ابن صفر ( توفي عام 1029) صنع العديد من الإسطرلابات والأدوات العلمية الأخرى التي على الأقل يعرف بأن ثلاثة منها بقيت وهي اليوم مبعثرة في متاحف مختلفة .

en.name: Astrolabe
description: This rare astrolabe is considered to be one of the oldest known dated astrolabes from Muslim Spain. It was made by the celebrated Andalusi astrolabist, Muhammad ibn al-Saffar in Cordoba, dated 411 AH / 1020 AD as mentioned in the signature within a square space at the back of its mater. The date follows the Arabic alphanumeric system known as *abjad*. The year is marked by a combination of letters *ta-ya-alif*, that corresponds to *ta* (400), *ya* (10) and *alif* (1), which totals up to 411. The astrolabe contains six plates which correspond to two localities for each plate, among which are Makkah, Damascus, Cairo and Cordoba. The rete, on the other hand, is a new addition from the 17th-century Ottoman Turkey. The maker of this astrolabe, Muhammad ibn al-Saffar (d. 1029) made several astrolabes and other scientific instruments with at least three are known to survive and are today scattered in different museums.

en.name: The Cotton Museum at the Agricultural museum
short_description: This building is used as a display museum to show the types of cotton seeds and strains in Egypt next to the products that come from each type. Egyptian cotton is preferred around the world because of its long fibre, which make it softer and stronger at the same time. For many years, it was so valuable that most of the crop was exported to European countries, and Egyptians themselves could hardly buy items made from its cloth.
history:
King Fu\`ad I chose the palace of Fatma Ismail, the daughter of Khedive Ismail, ‎to host the displays of the Agricultural Museum. The ‎palace was chosen due to its location near the Egyptian Ministry of Agriculture in the ‎neighborhood of Dokki in Cairo. ‎  
The museum, which was first called "The Agricultural Museum of King Fu\`ad I", was officially opened for the public on the 16th of January 1938 in a big ceremony that the king himself attended.
keywords: Agricultural museum; cotton; agriculture; museum
partner: Centre for Documentation of Cultural and Natural Heritage (CULTNAT)

ar.name: مسجد الأندلسيين.
description:
غادرت المئات من عائلات الأشراف بلاد الأندلس في عام 202 هجري / 818 ميلادي، والتجأت إلى المغرب هرباً من عمليات القمع المتلاحقة والناجمة عن الاضطرابات التي شهدتها قرطبة؛ فحطوا رحالهم على الضفة اليمنى لوادي فاس؛ وسرعان ما انخرط هؤلاء السكان الجدد في بناء الجامع الواسع الذي سوف يحمل اسمهم.  
المعلمة الأصلية متواضعة. وفي القرن 5 الهجري / 11 الميلادي، يصف الجغرافي البكري مسجدا "مؤلفا من سبعة بلاطات ومن صحن صغير زرعت فيه أشجار الجوز وأشجار أخرى، وتصله مياه وفيرة من قناة تدعى وادي مصمودة".  
عرف المسجد منذ تأسيسه في عام 245 هجري / 859 ميلادي، عدداً من أعمال الترميم والتوسيع المتتالية. فقد أضاف إليه أمويو قرطبة، في القرن 4 الهجري / 10 الميلادي، المئذنة التي بقيت على حالها حتى الوقت الحالي. بنيت هذه الصومعة على قاعدة مربعة، وارتفاعها بسيط، وتشبه تلك الموجودة في مسجد القرويين المعاصرة لها. كما قام عبيد الله، حاكم فاس الفاطمي، لاحقاً ، بنقل خطبة يوم الجمعة من مسجد الأشياخ، الجامع الأول الذي تم تشييده على هذه الضفة، إلى مسجد الأندلسيين. ولدى وصول الموحدين، أمر الخليفة محمد الناصر (حكم في الفترة 600 إلى 604 هجري/ 1203 - 1207 ميلادي)، والذي أولى أهمية خاصة بمدينة فاس، ببناء الباب الضخم بدرجاته الأربعة عشر والمشرف على الواجهة الشمالية. تزين هذا الباب، الذي تعلوه قبتان، إحداهما من الجبس المنحوت والأخرى من خشب الأرز، تركيبات متناغمة من الزليج /القاشاني ومن الخشب، يُحتمل أنها رممت خلال الفترة العلوية. وقد كان المؤرخ والرائد الكبير في الفن الإسلامي، الباحث جورج مارسي، يرى في هذا المسجد واحداً من الإنتاجات الضخمة الأكثر روعة في الفن المغاربي.  
كما قام الخليفة الناصر بتجهيز المسجد بصهريج للمياه ( كان يغذيه وادي مصمودة) وبنافورة وبجناح للوضوء، مشابه لذلك المتواجد في مسجد القرويين. وفي الطابق العلوي، بنيت شقة من حجرتين للإمام فوق قاعة الصلاة الخاصة بالنساء.  
وأخيراً، يعود الفضل للمرينيين في ترميم بعض السقوف والدعامات وكذلك النافورة الموجودة في الواجهة الشمالية من البناية.  
جعلت كل هذه الترتيبات من جامع الأندلسيين البناية الدينية الثانية في المدينة، وضم، على غرار مسجد القرويين، سبعة كراسي للتعليم ومكتبتين.

عايش مسجد الأندلسيين الذي أسِّسَ عام 808 من طرف مريم، أخت فاطمة الفهرية، في العدوة التي تحمل نفس الاسم كل الثورات التي شهدتها مدينة فاس.  
جرى توسيع البناية المتواضعة الأصلية خلال القرن 10 من طرف أمويِّي قرطبة، ثم وُسع بعد ذلك من قبل المرينين. كما جُهز الجامع بمنارة مشابهة لتلك المتواجدة بالقرويين وباب ضخمة وقبتين؛ وبإمكانه أن يستقبل 4200 مصلي.  
يشكل الجامع مركزا ثقافيا حقيقيا بالمدينة، إذ تحيط به مدرستان، ويشتملُ على سبعة كراسي علمية للتدريس وخزانتين.
artist: مريم بنت محمد ابن عبد الله.
keywords: مسجد؛ جامع؛ بناية دينية؛ زليج / قاشاني؛ كراسي علمية؛ مكتبة علمية؛ مئذنة مربعة.
partner: Ministry of Culture,Directorate of Cultural Heritage

en.name: Andalusian Mosque.
description:
In AH 202 / AD 818, fleeing the reprisals that followed the riots of Córdoba, hundreds of respected families left al-Andalus and took refuge in Morocco. Having settled on the right bank of the Wadi Fez, these new inhabitants would soon participate in the construction of a huge mosque that would bear their name.  
The original building was a modest one. In the AH 4th / AD 10th century, the geographer al-Bakri described a mosque 'made up of seven rows of benches and a small courtyard planted with walnut and other trees that has an abundant supply of water from a canal known as the Wadi Masmuda'.  
Since its foundation in AH 245 / AD 859, the mosque has undergone a long succession of restorations and extensions. In the AH 4th / AD 10th century, the Umayyads of Córdoba added the minaret, which has survived to the present day. Constructed on a square base and of modest height, it is identical to its contemporary at the Qarawiyyin.  
Later, 'Ubayd Allah, the Fatimid governor of Fez, transferred the Friday *khutba* (sermon) from al-'Achyakh mosque, the first mosque built that side of the Wadi, to the Andalusian mosque.  
With the arrival of the Almohads, Caliph Muhammad al-Nasir (r. AH 595–610 / AD 1199–1213), who had a particular interest in the Fez Medina, had the 14-step monumental gateway that dominates the north façade built. Crowned with two domes, one in sculpted plaster and the other in cedarwood, this gateway is decorated with harmonious compositions in faience and wood, probably restored under the 'Alawids. The Muslim historian and great promoter of the arts Georges Marçais considered this to be one of the most impressive monuments of North African art.  
Al-Nasir also provided the mosque with a pool (which was fed by the Wadi Masmuda), a fountain and an ablutions pavilion similar to one at the Qarawiyyin Mosque in Fez. On the first floor, above the women's prayer room, a two-room apartment was built for the imam.  
Finally, the Marinids were responsible for the restoration of some of the ceilings and pillars, as well as the fountain situated on in north façade of the building.  
All of this work would make the Andalusian mosque the second largest religious building in the town. It provided seven teaching positions and two libraries.

Founded by Maryam, the sister of Fatima al-Fihriya, founder of the Qarawiyyin Mosque, the Andalusian Mosque, which stands in the quarter of the same name, has witnessed all of the revolts that have taken place in Fez. The modest original building was extended first in the AH 4th / AD 10th century by the Cordoban Umayyads and later by the Marinids. With a minaret identical to the one belonging to the Qarawiyyin, a monumental gateway and two cupolas, the mosque could accommodate up to 4,200 worshipers. Serving as a cultural centre for the town, it is flanked by two *madrasas* and has seven teaching chairs and two libraries.
artist: Maryam, a pious woman from Kairouan, daughter of Muhammad ibn ‘Abdallah.
keywords: Place of worship; minaret
partner: Ministry of Culture, Directorate of Cultural Heritage

es.name: Mezquita de los Andalusíes.
description:
La represión consecuencia de las revueltas de Córdoba de 202 / 818 provocó el exilio de al-Andalus y la emigración a Marruecos de cientos de familias importantes. Estos nuevos habitantes establecidos en la margen derecha del río Fez construyeron una amplia mezquita que lleva su nombre.  
El monumento original era modesto. En el siglo IV / X, el geógrafo al-Bakri describió una mezquita “compuesta por siete tramos y un pequeño patio plantado con nogales y otros árboles \[que\] obtiene abundante agua de un canal llamado río Masmuda”.  
Desde su fundación en 245 / 859, el santuario fue objeto de numerosas restauraciones y sucesivas ampliaciones. En el siglo IV / X, los omeyas de Córdoba añadieron el alminar, que aún hoy se conserva. De planta cuadrada y escasa altura, es idéntico a su contemporáneo de la mezquita Qarawiyin.  
Más adelante, Ubayd Allah, gobernador fatimí de Fez, transfirió la *jutba* (‘sermón’) del Viernes de la mezquita de al-Ashiaj, la primera construida en esta ribera, a la mezquita de los Andalusíes.  
Con la llegada de los almohades, el califa Mohamed al-Nasir (600-604 / 1203-1207), que tenía un particular interés en la medina de Fez, mandó levantar la puerta monumental de 14 escalones que domina la fachada norte. Dos cúpulas, una de estuco esculpido, la otra de madera de cedro, realzaban esta puerta adornada con armoniosas composiciones en cerámica y madera, restauradas probablemente en época alawí. El historiador y gran defensor del arte musulmán Georges Marçais la consideró como una de las obras monumentales más imponentes del arte magrebí. Al-Nasir, además, proveyó a la mezquita de una alberca (alimentada por el Masmuda), una fuente y un pabellón de abluciones semejante al de la Qarawiyin; en el primer piso, sobre el oratorio de las mujeres, se edificó una vivienda de dos estancias para el imam.  
Por último, los meriníes restauraron algunos techos y pilares, así como la fuente de la fachada norte.  
Gracias a dichas obras de restauración y ampliación, la mezquita de los Andalusíes se convirtió en el segundo mayor edifico religioso de la ciudad. A semejanza de la Qarawiyin, albergó siete cátedras de enseñanza y dos bibliotecas.

La mezquita de los Andalusíes, fundada por Maryam, hermana de Fatima al-Fihriya, en el barrio del mismo nombre, fue testigo de todas las revueltas de la ciudad de Fez.  
El modesto edificio original fue ampliado en el siglo IV / X por los omeyas de Córdoba y, después, por los meriníes.  
La mezquita podía acoger hasta 4.200 fieles. Posee un alminar idéntico al de la mezquita Qarawiyin, una puerta monumental y dos cúpulas. Auténtico centro cultural de la ciudad, está flanqueada por dos madrasas y cuenta con siete cátedras de enseñanza y dos bibliotecas.
artist: Maryam, hija de Mohamed ibn Abdallah.
keywords: Lugar de oración; alminar.
partner: Ministry of Culture,Directorate of Cultural Heritage

fr.name: Mosquée des Andalous.
description:
En 202 H / 818 J.-C., fuyant les répressions consécutives aux émeutes de Cordoue, des centaines de familles de notables quittèrent al-Andalus et trouvèrent refuge au Maroc. Accueillis sur la rive droite de l'oued Fès, ces nouveaux habitants allaient bientôt participer à la construction de la vaste mosquée qui porte leur nom.  
  
L'édifice d'origine était modeste. Au IVe siècle H (Xe siècle J.-C.), le géographe al-Bakri décrit une mosquée “composée de sept travées et d'un petit patio planté de noyers et d'autres arbres et \[qui\] reçoit une eau abondante d'un canal nommé oued Masmouda”.  
  
Depuis sa fondation en 245 H / 859 J.-C., la mosquée a connu nombre de restaurations et agrandissements successifs. Au IVe siècle H (Xe siècle J.-C.), les Omeyyades de Cordoue ajoutèrent le minaret qui est parvenu jusqu'à nous. Construit sur une base carrée, d'une hauteur modeste, il est identique à son contemporain de la Qaraouiyine.  
  
Plus tard, Obayd Allah, gouverneur fatimide de Fès, transféra la *khotba* (le prêche) du Vendredi de la mosquée al-Achiakh, la première mosquée érigée sur cette rive, à la mosquée des Andalous.  
  
à l'arrivé des Almohades, le calife Mohamed al-Nassir (600-604 H / 1203-1207 J.-C.), qui portait un intérêt particulier à la médina de Fès, fit construire la porte monumentale à 14 marches qui domine la façade nord. Rehaussée de deux coupoles, l'une en plâtre sculpté, l'autre en bois de cèdre, cette porte est décorée d'harmonieuses compositions en faïence et en bois, probablement restaurées à l'époque alaouite. L'historien et grand promoteur de l'art musulman Georges Marçais y voyait l'une des œuvres monumentales les plus impressionnantes de l'art maghrébin.  
  
C'est encore al-Nassir qui dota la mosquée d'un bassin (qui était alimenté par l'oued Masmouda), d'une fontaine et d'un pavillon à ablutions semblable à celui de la Qaraouiyine ; à l'étage, au-dessus de la salle de prière des femmes, un appartement de deux pièces fut construit pour l'imam.  
  
Enfin, on doit aux Mérinides la restauration de certains plafonds et piliers, ainsi que la fontaine située dans la façade nord de l'édifice.  
  
Tous ces aménagements allaient faire de la mosquée des Andalous le deuxième plus grand édifice religieux de la ville. à l'instar de la Qaraouiyine, elle a abrité sept chaires d'enseignement et deux bibliothèques.

Fondée en 808 par Meryem, sœur de Fatima al-Fihriya, la mosquée des Andalous, dans le quartier du même nom, a vécu toutes les révoltes de la ville de Fès.  
Le modeste édifice d'origine a été agrandi au Xe siècle par les Omeyyades de Cordoue, puis élargi par les Mérinides.  
Dotée d'un minaret identique à celui de la Qaraouiyine, d'une porte monumentale et de deux coupoles, la mosquée peut accueillir jusqu'à 4 200 fidèles.  
Véritable centre culturel de la ville, elle est flanquée de deux *madrasa* et possède sept chaires d'enseignement et deux bibliothèques.
dynasty: Idrisside, IIe-IVe siècle de l’Hégire (VIIIe-Xe siècle J.-C.).
artist: Meryem, fille de Mohamed Ben Abdallah.
keywords: lieu de prière ; minaret
partner: Ministry of Culture,Directorate of Cultural Heritage

en.name: Ring
short_description:
Thin silver ring with a squared black stone set in silver. Silver jewellery was the most common, because only rich people could afford gold jewellery. The dowry of silver and gold jewellery was given by the groom to the bride, reflecting the financial status of the groom.  
Jordan's economy in the late 19th and early 20th centuries relied on trades and crafts and new waves of people started to come to Jordan and began to settle for this purpose. This object is an example of how traditional fashion reflected the variegated population composition of Jordan in the late 19th and early 20th centuries. It is also an example of local personal attire, fashion, costumes and rites.
holder: Jordan Museum for Costumes and Jewellery, Department of Antiquities
keywords: Floral decoration; religious objects; waqf; Qur’an; Ottoman Baroque-Rococo
partner: Jordan Museum for Costumes and Jewellery

en.name: *Portrait of a Laughing Youth*
description:
The painting is mentioned for the first time as part of the collection in the 1693 inventory. It has been attributed variously to different artists in the past, but was confirmed as a “Carracci Caricature” in an 1833 *fideicommissum* (a deed forbidding the heirs to the Borghese estate from splitting up the collection). In the 20th century, it was deemed to be an early work of the Bolognese artist, at a time when Carracci made numerous attempts at “genre works”, leaving some superb examples, such as the famous canvas , *The Beaneater* in the Galleria Colonna, Rome (c. 1583–1584).  
The portrait of the jester has always been thought to be a character from the *Commedia dell'Arte*. This small sketch shows a smiling, mocking youth dressed in a dark suit, ruff and light hat, awkward and upside-down. The supposed jester, with his grotesque red nose, cannot be identified entirely with the theatrical comic tradition and, although the severe and sober clothes resemble the Bolognese mask of “Dottor Graziano”, the unusual hat is perhaps an invention of Carracci himself.  
The light comes from the right, creating a *chiaroscuro* effect on the folds of the hat, emphasising the satisfied look and ambiguous smile of the character, the focal point of the portrait.  
It is the complicit look and smile of a comic actor that, between fiction and reality, skilfully establishes a relationship with the viewer.  
The portrait stands against a simple yellow background, which helps to focus attention on the burlesque face, whose keen, realistic expression is rendered with a sombre palette of colours.  
Free charcoal lines quickly define the sketch, combined with fast, fluid brush strokes. Given the medium (paper on canvas) the use of these tools seems to suggest a desire to capture the immediacy of a live portrait, rather than a caricature, which has been suggested, although this area was of interest to the painter.  
The modernity of expression in the sketch anticipates by half a century the portraits of Velazquez and Bernini and appears to be the beginning of the study of emotions and character types that characterises 18th-century artistic innovation.  
The work is one of Carracci's “small portraits” painted after 1582, where his search for reality was based on simple lines and not precise reproductions of faces.

This piece is an interesting example of the artistic re-invention pursued by Carracci. In his sketchy *Portrait of a Laughing Youth*, dating to around1584, the young artist captures a moment of the youth's laughter. With its spontaneity, it is extraordinarily modern, anticipating the portraits by Bernini and Velázquez 50 years later. It may be the portrait of an actor, the Bolognese mask of the “Dottor Graziano”.
keywords: Portrait; Commedia dell'Arte; chiaroscuro; character types; genre painting

it.name: *Ritratto di giovane che ride*
description:
Il dipinto è citato per la prima volta in collezione nell'inventario del 1693; è stato variamente attribuito nel passato, ma è confermato come “Caricatura del Carracci” dal Fidecommesso del 1833 (atto che impediva agli eredi Borghese di disperdere la collezione). Nel '900 il ritratto viene considerato un'opera giovanile dell'artista bolognese, difatti il Carracci degli esordi si era avvicinato più volte alla cosiddetta “pittura di genere”, avendone lasciato superbi esempi, tra cui la famosa tela *Il Mangiafagioli* della Galleria Colonna di Roma (1583-1584 ca.).    
Il ritratto di buffone è stato sempre ritenuto un personaggio legato alla Commedia dell'Arte. Il piccolo schizzo ritrae un giovane sorridente e beffardo insieme, abbigliato in corsetto scuro, gorgiera e con un copricapo chiaro, goffamente riverso. L'ipotetico buffone, col naso grottescamente arrossato, non è del tutto identificabile nella tradizione comica teatrale e, sebbene i vestiti severi e sobri richiamino alla maschera bolognese del “Dottor Graziano”, il copricapo inusuale è forse un elemento d'invenzione carraccesca.  
La luce proviene da destra e crea con le pieghe del copricapo un gioco chiaroscurale che dà risalto allo sguardo compiaciuto e al sorriso ambiguo del personaggio, punto focale del ritratto.  
Sono lo sguardo ed il sorriso, ammiccanti e complici, di un attore comico che, tra finzione e realtà, stabilisce con mestiere la relazione d'intesa con il suo pubblico.  
La costruzione del ritratto risalta su un fondo giallo compendiario, che permette la concentrazione sul viso burlesco, la cui espressione arguta e realistica è resa con una tavolozza cromaticamente parca.  
I contorni a carboncino definiscono velocemente lo schizzo, il cui tratto libero si unisce alla rapida esecuzione delle pennellate fluide. Sembrano gli strumenti, insieme al supporto, carta applicata su tela, di una ricerca di immediatezza propria del ritratto dal vivo, piuttosto che la realizzazione di una caricatura, come talvolta ipotizzato, sebbene fosse un genere d'interesse del pittore.    
Lo schizzo è di tale modernità di espressione da anticipare di mezzo secolo la ritrattistica di Bernini e Velázquez e pare dare l'avvio allo studio dei moti dell'animo e della tipizzazione dei personaggi, che caratterizzeranno la ricerca artistica secentesca.  
L'opera s'inserisce nell'ambito dei “ritrattini” eseguiti da Carracci a partire dal 1582, dove la ricerca del dato reale avveniva attraverso tratti sintetici e non con riproduzioni puntuali delle fisionomie.

Quest'opera rappresenta un interessante esempio di rinnovamento artistico perseguito da Carracci. Il giovane artista coglie il momento del riso nel suo ritratto abbozzato del *Ragazzo che ride*, datato circa 1584.  
Con la sua spontaneità risulta straordinariamente moderno e anticipa i ritratti di Bernini e Velázquez di cinquata anni dopo. Forse è il ritratto di una attore, come si può vedere dal cappello, che era usato solitamente  per la maschera bolognese del “dottore”.
keywords: Ritratto; Commedia dell'Arte; chiaroscuro; tipizzazione dei caratter; pittura di genere

en.name: Altar panel with Mary Magdalene and John the Baptist
description: In the Middle Ages, lepers were segregated from the rest of society in lazarettos. In Zurich, these were located outside the city walls, close to running water, and had a chapel of their own. The St. Moritz lazaretto, which was built on the Spanweid in 1364, housed destitute lepers. The chapel received a new altarpiece in 1506. The inside of the panels depicts St. Mary Magdalene in costly fashionable clothing with a pouch and a cutlery holder. She is holding an open pot of ointment and promising the lepers hope of healing.
keywords: Painting; Chapel Spanweid; Zuerich; Mary Magdalene; John the Baptist; Zentralbibliothek;

en.name: Vase
description: In the complete course of art history, rarely has there been a movement in which the decorative arts played such an integral role as Art Nouveau. Among these arts, glass held the most important role by far. As a very flexible and mostly transparent material, glass provided an ideal medium in which artists of the movement could express their ideas that were inspired by nature and organic forms. The style, originating in England, spread throughout Europe; yet the most notable places it set its roots were Belgium, France, the Czech Republic, Germany and Austria. Known as Jugendstil in the German-speaking lands, the movement beared witness to divine glass creations from many, now world-famous, craftspeople who have truly earned honourable mentions in the history of the decorative and applied arts. An essential place for the birth and development of the Jugendstil in Vienna was the Wiener Werkstätte (Vienna Workshops), founded by Josef Hoffmann and Koloman Moser. The main aim of the workshops was to bring the artist or designer closer to the craftspeople and technicians entrusted with the execution of their designs, while also encouraging the designers to be their own crafters. The Wiener Werkstätte was host to a large number of Austrian craftspeople, such as Dagobert Peche, Otto Prutscher and Ludwig Heinrich Jungnickel. The Wiener Werkstätte was one of Hoffmann’s central projects throughout his long life. Therefore, his contribution to the art of the Austrian Jugendstil is a multi-faceted one, ranging from architecture to the decorative arts. Standing on a wide and small foot, this milky-blue glass bowl is covered with a green overlay in the form of triangles and continuing into stripes along the foot of the glass. In between there are isolated green leaves. This presents an ideal combination of Hoffmann’s inspirations from nature and rectilinear forms.
materials: Glass, cameo glass; flashing, glass cutting, blow molding, layered, etched (corroded)
tags: flashing, glass cutting, blow molding, layered, etched (corroded)
partner: MAK – Austrian Museum of Applied Arts / Contemporary Art

en.name: Azakhana-e-Zehra
description:
This magnificently built *azakhana* (Shia shrine) is located on the south bank of the river Musi, in the Darul Schifa area of historic Hyderabad. It is symbolic of the easy religious coexistence of Muslims and Hindus in the city. The shrine was built by the Sunni *Nizam* Mir Osman Ali Khan (1886 – 1967) in honour of his Shia mother Amtul Zehra Begum. Architect Zain Yar Jung was commissioned to design a monument representing the power and glory of the kingdom.  
  
The Shia shrine is a place of mourning for Shia Muslims. It houses *alams*, or battle standards, and is regularly visited by Shia devotees. In *Muharram*, the first month of the Islamic calendar, it also hosts religious gatherings called *majalis*. During this month the monument is transformed into a space for solemn meditation. Worshippers visit the shrine to commemorate the Prophet Muhammad, his daughter Fatima and son-in-law Ali, and his grandsons Hasan and Husain, the latter of whom died in the Battle of Karbala in 680 A.D. (10 *Muharram* in the year 61 A.H. of the Islamic calendar).  
  
Azakhana-e-Zehra was built in the Qutb Shahi architecture style. It has impressive outer elevations, and the interior of the structure is magnificent. The square building is topped by circular cupolas and divided into three sections by pillars. It also has two courtyards. The outer courtyard is overlooked by balconies and spans the distance from the entrance gate to the platform holding the main building.  
  
The interior of the monument is painted in a rich green accented with black and gold, and the names of the martyrs of the Battle of Karbala have been inscribed on the ceiling. The entrance can be unimposing, but leads to a vast open space with balconies and intricate decorations, with a platform directly across from the door.  
  
The teak ceiling of the shrine is an imposing 13 metres high, and stands without supporting pillars. The upper balconies have a *jaali*, or decorative screen, for women mourners attending gender-segregated religious gatherings. The walls are decorated with verses from the Quran and sayings of the Prophet Muhammad, written by master calligraphers. During the *hijra* or *hegira* that marks the Prophet Muhammad’s migration from Mecca to Medina, *alams* made of gold and precious stones are displayed here.

en.name: *Flügelaltar (Winged Altar)*
description: The creator of this triptych, which was intended as a small travel altar for private prayer, was Jan van Eyck, the most important representative of Old Netherlandish painting. Characteristic features of his new artistic style are the miniature-like, extremely realistic rendering of details and the use of brilliant colours. Enthroned in the centre of the Basilica is the Madonna with her son, the infant Christ. Stretched out at her feet is a precious woven carpet. It has a rhombic pattern featuring eight-pointed stars set in circles. Its intense colours contrast with the muted hues of the ingeniously patterned floor tiles.
holder: Gemäldegalerie Alte Meister (Old Masters Picture Gallery), Dresden State Art Collections
keywords: Painting; Christianity; Bibel; Carpet; Madonna

en.name: Goblet
description:
This particularly extravagant exhibition goblet in Renaissance style is a masterpiece by the Bohemia glass engraver Franz Paul Zach (1819–1881). It is made in two pieces, both of colourless, clear glass, with a thin, blue glass overlay. The bowl is attached to the stem with a cut glass screw thread.  
  
Zach has engraved through the blue overlay on the bowl, to reveal a lively, flowing mythological scene in the manner of the glass engraver Georg Schwanhardt the Elder (1601-67). We see Bacchus, the Roman god of wine, riding a goat, and wife Ariadne, a Cretan princess, riding a panther. Bacchus’s followers, including a goat-hooved satyr, are carrying a type of staff topped with a pine cone which is called a thyrsus, a symbol of fertility.

en.name: *Traitor*
short_description: During his frequent travels across the Balkans in the 1880s, Paja Jovanović acquainted himself with the ethnic makeup of the population, particularly in Lower Zeta (present-day Podgorica and the surrounding area), in the neighbourhood of Bar and in the border-lying area with Albania. It was here that Albanian, Serbian and Montenegrin inhabitants intermingled, so their characters, physiognomies, customs and vivid national costumes were entwined and fused into a whole in the paintings of Paja Jovanović. The image of capturing or trying a traitor, who, according to tribal custom, awaited sentencing, is certainly a noteworthy genre subject among those he selected to depict the life and customs of peoples in the Balkans. Unlike the first version, painted by Jovanović in 1885, this replica of The Traitor from the mid-1920s was painted in a more free-handed manner, in broad brush strokes and without insistence on details.
keywords: Genre Painting

en.name: Blue-and-white bottle with partridges
description: This bottle, painted with confident black strokes in reserve against a blue background, combines a Chinese shape and colour scheme with a Persian interpretation of Eastern motifs – three fat partridges alternating with large, fleshy lotus flowers. Such wares were designed to compete with Chinese porcelain in markets at home and abroad.
dates: Hegira second half of the 11th century / AD second half of the 17th century

ar.name: جبهية باب.
description:
تتخذ هذه الجبهيّة هيئةَ نصف مضلع له تسعة أضلاع، مؤلفٍ من أربع لوحات؛ زخرفت الأولى بتزاويق نباتية؛ فيما زُينت اللوحات الثلاث الأخريات بنقيشة كتابية من تسعة أسطر منحوتة نحتاً بارزاً، ومكتوبة بأحرف نسخية باستثناء السطر الأخير المكتوب بخط كوفي مربّع الزوايا. قُسمت الأسطر الستّة الأخيرة من النقيشة في المنتصف بزخرفة زهريّة وهندسيّة. تحتوي هذه النقيشة على النص التالي: "أعوذ بالله من الشيطان الرجيم / في بيوت أذن الله أن ترفع / ويذكر فيها اسمه يسبّح له فيها بالغدو والآصال (القرآن، سورة 21، آية 36-37) / بيت مرفوعة بالذكر عامرة بالله قائمة يغفر لمن فيها / وللذي أنشأها وأقام لها البنا يحيى ابن محجوبة لله مهديها / اغفر له مامضى وقِه حرّ اللظى وأدخله دار السلام / امنحه فيها هبة الرضا والأمان من هول يوم الزحام وامنحه أعلى الجنان يفوز من فيها / في عام شج كمل منها البنا وأتمّ الله بناها يا قارئ ادع للذي بناها / وبعفو ومغفرة الله وشفاعة خير الناس / اجعل منها مكانا لقراءة السنة للعامة".  
هذه النقيشة هي الوحيدة في الجزائر التي تحمل تاريخاً مُعبَّراً عنه بطريقة حساب الجمل (بإضافة القيم الرقميّة لكل حرف أبجدي يؤلّف الجملة نحصل على التأريخ المستتر وراءها). كانت هذه الجبهيّة مثبّتةً فوق باب زاوية تُعرف باسم "زاوية ابن محجوبة" متاخمة لمقبرة. وقد تمّ هدم هذا البناء عند شقّ الشارع الوطني حوالي عام 1865.  
والشخص المذكور في نص الجبهيّة هو الشيخ أبو زكريّا يحيى ابن محجوبة (المتوفّى عام 1017 هجري / 1608 ميلادي)، الذي كان مفتياً، والذي ورد ذكره أيضاً في مخطوط يعود إلى تلك الفترة.

تتكون هذه الجبهية التي كانت تعلو مدخل الزاوية من أربع لوحات؛ زخرفت اللوحة الأولى بزخرفة نباتية، وتحمل اللوحات الثلاث الأخرى نقيشة كتابية منقوشة بأحرف نسخية، أو كوفية في السطر الأخير تمجد الله وتمدح مشيد البناية، والتي جرى تأريخها بحساب الجمل.
keywords: أحرف كوفيّة ؛ أحرف نسخية؛ خشب؛ زخرفة زهريّة؛ زخرفة هندسيّة؛ العثمانيّون؛ علم الكتابات والخطوط؛ عمارة دينيّة؛ زاوية.
materials: خشب الأرز المنحوت نحتاً بارزاً، تطعيم.
tags: خشب الأرز المنحوت نحتاً بارزاً، تطعيم.

en.name: Pediment of a door.
description:
This pediment takes the form of a half-polygon of nine sides, consisting of four panels; the first is ornamented with vegetal decoration; the remaining three are decorated with a nine-line inscription, sculpted in relief and in cursive lettering, except for the last line, which is in quadrangular *kufic*. The final six lines of the inscription are centrally divided by floral and geometric decoration. This inscription features the following text: 'May God protect us from Satan the abuser / In houses that God allowed us to build / in which men invoke his Name and glorify Him, morning and night (Qur'an, XXI, 36–37) / raised house, full of invocations, erected for the worship of God. He will pardon those who find themselves there / and the one who founded and built it, Yahyia ibn Mahdjuba, who offered it to God / Forgive him his past! Protect him from the heat of hell! Enable him to enter paradise where he will experience well-being! / Grant him Your assurance and Your protection against the terrors of the day of resurrection! Offer him a place at the top of paradise! What success for those who are there! / In the year *chin*, *djim*, the construction was finished and completed with the help of God. Oh reader, make wishes in favour of he who built this / Through the forgiveness and indulgence of God, through the intercession of the best of men! Do it so that one can always read the tradition to the people.'  
This inscription is the only one in Algeria that features a date written in the form of a chronogram (in adding together the numeric values of each letter that it consists of, one obtains the date it conceals). This pediment was previously situated above the entrance to a *zawiya* known under the name of Zawiya Ibn Mahdjuba, adjacent to a cemetery. The building was demolished around 1865, during the widening/opening of the rue Nationale.  
The person mentioned is the sheik Abu-Zakariya Yahyia ibn Mahdjuba (d. AH 1017 / AD 1608), who was a *mufti* and who is mentioned in a manuscript contemporary to the era.

This pediment stood above the entrance to a *zawiya* and consists of four panels. The first is decorated with plant motifs and the other three bear an inscription carved in cursive characters (*kufic* in the last line) that glorify God and the patron of the work. It is dated by a chronogram included in the inscription.
holder: National Museum of Antiquities and Islamic Arts
keywords: Floral decoration; geometric decoration; epigraphy; religious architecture; kufic; cursive characters; Ottoman; wood
materials: Cedar wood, carved in relief, marquetry.
tags: Cedar wood, carved in relief, marquetry.
partner: National Museum of Antiquities and Islamic Art

es.name: Tímpano de puerta.
description:
Este tímpano, cuya forma se amolda a un semipolígono de nueve lados, está compuesto de cuatro paneles; el primero está adornado con decoración vegetal y los otros tres, con una inscripción distribuida en nueve líneas y esculpida en relieve en caracteres cursivos, excepto la última línea, que presenta caracteres cúficos cuadrangulares. Las últimas seis líneas de esta inscripción están divididas por la mitad con una decoración floral y geométrica vertical. El texto es el siguiente: “Que Dios nos proteja de Satán el Apedreado / En casas que Dios ha permitido erigir / y que se mencione en ellas Su nombre. En ellas Le glorifican, mañana y tarde (Corán, XXIV, 36) / casa levantada, llena de invocaciones, alzada para el culto de Dios. Serán perdonados quienes se encuentren en ella / y quien la ha fundado y construido, Yahya ben Mahdyuba, que la ha ofrecido a Dios / ¡Perdónale el pasado! ¡Protégelo del calor del infierno! ¡Hazle entrar en el paraíso, donde encontrará el bienestar! / ¡Concédele Tu beneplácito y Tu protección contra los pavores del día de la resurrección! ¡Dale un sitio en lo alto del paraíso! ¡Qué éxito para los que allí se encuentran! / En el año *shin yim* la construcción ha sido terminada y rematada con la ayuda de Dios. Oh lector, formula votos a favor de quien la ha levantado. / ¡Por el perdón y la indulgencia de Dios, por la intercesión del mejor de los hombres! Haz que en ella siempre se lea la tradición al pueblo”.  
Esta inscripción es la única en Argelia que lleva una fecha formulada por medio de un cronograma (sumando los valores numéricos de cada letra que lo compone se obtiene la fecha). Este tímpano estaba antaño situado sobre la puerta de una *zawiya* conocida como “*zawiya* de Ben Mahyuba”, adyacente a un cementerio. El edificio fue destruido en 1865, cuando se abrió la calle Nacional.  
El personaje mencionado es el jeque Abu Zakariya Ben Mahdyuba (m. 1017 / 1608), muftí cuyo nombre aparece en un manuscrito de la época.

Este tímpano, antaño situado sobre la entrada a la *zawiya*, consta de cuatro paneles. El primero está adornado con decoración vegetal y los otros tres tienen esculpida una inscripción en caracteres cursivos –cúficos en la última línea– que glorifica a Dios y al mecenas de la obra, y que está fechada con un cronograma.

fr.name: Fronton de porte.
description:
Ce fronton épousela forme d'un demi-polygone de neuf côtés, composé de quatre panneaux ; le premier est orné d'un décor végétal ; les trois autres sont décorés d'une inscription de neuf lignes, sculptées en relief et en caractères cursifs, à l'exception de la dernière ligne qui est en coufique quadrangulaire. Les six dernières lignes de l'inscription sont divisées, au milieu, par un décor floral et géométrique. Cette inscription comporte le texte suivant : “Que Dieu nous garde de Satan le lapidé / Dans des maisons que Dieu a permis d'élever / dans lesquelles des hommes invoquent son Nom et Le glorifient, matin et soir (Coran, XXI, 36-37) / maison élevée, pleine d'invocations, dressée pour le culte de Dieu. Il sera pardonné à ceux qui s'y trouvent / et à celui qui l'a fondée et construite, Yahyia ben Mahdjouba, qui l'a offerte à Dieu / Pardonne-lui le passé ! Protège-le de la chaleur de l'enfer ! Fais-le entrer au paradis où il connaîtra le bien-être ! / Accorde-lui Ton agrément et Ta protection contre les terreurs du jour de la résurrection ! Donne-lui une place au haut du paradis ! Quel succès pour ceux qui y sont ! / En l'an *chin*, *djim*, la construction en a été terminée et achevée avec l'aide de Dieu. ô lecteur, forme des vœux en faveur de celui qui l'a élevée / Par le pardon et l'indulgence de Dieu, par l'intercession du meilleur des hommes ! Fais qu'on y lise toujours la tradition au peuple.”  
  
Cette inscription est la seule en Algérie portant une date exprimée au moyen d'un chronogramme (en additionnant les valeurs numériques de chaque lettre qui le compose, on obtient le millésime qui s'y dissimule). Ce fronton était autrefois placé au-dessus de la porte d'une *zaouïa* connue sous le nom de “*zaouïa* Ben Mahdjouba” adjacente à un cimetière. L'édifice a été démoli vers 1865, lors de l'ouverture de la rue Nationale.  
  
Le personnage qui y est mentionné est le *cheikh* Abou-Zakariya Yahyia ben Mahdjouba (m. 1017 H / 1608 J.-C.), qui était *mufti* et qui est mentionné dans un manuscrit de l'époque.

Ce fronton qui surmontait l'entrée de la *zaouïa* est composé de quatre panneaux. Le premier est orné d'un décor végétal, les trois autres portent une inscription sculptée en caractères cursifs ou coufiques pour la dernière ligne, qui glorifie Dieu et le commanditaire de l'ouvrage et qui est datée par chronographe.

ar.name: قطعتان من القاشاني.
description: قطعتان من القاشاني من عجينة الكوارتز (فريت) المزجج. تحمل القطعة (159) تركيباً أفقياً من أغصان الكرمة المرسومة بشكل طبيعي مع أوراق خضراء وعناقيد حمراء تحيط بغصن مركزي تنمو عليه أزهار صغيرة زرقاء وحمراء. يظهر على القطعة (160) تصميم زهري كثيف من الأوراق المعروفة باسم الساز متراكبة في الوسط ويحيط بها أربعة أنصاف أزهار تخيلية، أما الأرضية فقد تم ملؤها بأشرطة متموجة حمراء اللون وأغصان متقنة باللون الأزرق.

منذ خمسينيات القرن العاشر الهجري/ السادس عشر الميلادي، باتت ألواح آجرّ شبيهة بهذين، وكان البلاط العثماني يُوصي بإنتاجها، لتغطية حاجة برامج البناء المّوسَّعة في استنبول، وغيرها، هاجساً رئيسياً على ما يبدو، بالنسبة إلى جملة المشاغل الازنيقية، وثمة أعداد كبيرة منها باقية على حالها.

en.name: Two tiles.
description: Two stone-paste (fritware) glazed tiles, tile no. 159 a horizontal composition of naturalistically drawn vines with green leaves and fleshy red grapes that flank a central branch that has small blue and red flowers growing on it. Tile no. 160 shows a dense floral design, with two curved so-called *saz* leaves superposed in the centre and surrounded by four fantastical half-flowers. The background is filled with sinuous red cloud-bands and delicate blue scrolling.

Since the late AH 950s / AD 1550s tiles like these, commissioned by the Ottoman court for their extensive building programmes in Istanbul and elsewhere, are known to have become the major concern for the Iznik workshops and a large number of examples remain *in situ*.
dates: Hegira, late 10th century / AD late 16th century.
keywords: Iznik; stone-paste (fritware); vine scrolls; tilework; grape
materials: Stone-paste (fritware), blue, green and black underglaze with a bole-red underglaze slip, over which a clear glaze.
tags: Stone-paste (fritware), blue, green and black underglaze with a bole-red underglaze slip, over which a clear glaze.

es.name: Dos azulejos
description: Dos azulejos de pasta de piedra vidriada. El núm. 159 está decorado con una composición horizontal de dibujo naturalista que representa una rama central con pequeñas flores azules de botón rojo y flanqueada por vides con hojas verdes y carnosas uvas rojas. El núm. 160 presenta un denso diseño floral con dos hojas de *saz* curvas en el centro, rodeadas por cuatro flores imaginarias. El fondo se decora con sinuosas nubes encadenadas y finos tallos azules.

Gracias al extenso plan constructivo que el Imperio Otomano llevó a cabo en Estambul y otras partes, es bien conocido que los azulejos pasaron a constituir el principal producto de los talleres de Iznik desde finales de la década de 950 / 1550. Gran parte de estos azulejos aún se conservan *in situ*.
dates: Finales del siglo X de la Hégira / XVI d. C.
keywords: Iznik; pasta cerámica (frita)
materials: Pasta de piedra (frita) pintada en azul, verde, negro y engobe de bol rojo bajo vidriado claro.
tags: Pasta de piedra (frita) pintada en azul, verde, negro y engobe de bol rojo bajo vidriado claro.

fr.name: Deux carreaux.
description: Deux carreaux en céramique frittée. Le carreau n° 159 présente une composition horizontale de vigne à feuilles vertes et grappes charnues de couleur rouge disposées de chaque côté d'une branche centrale à petites fleurs rouges et bleues. Le carreau n° 160 est orné d'une composition florale chargée, à deux feuilles *saz* superposées au centre, entourées de quatre demi-fleurs de fantaisie. Le fond est occupé par des bandeaux de nuages sinueux et d'enroulements de délicates tiges végétales bleues.

Depuis  la fin des années 950 H / 1550 J.-C, des carreaux  comme ceux-là furent commandés par la cour ottomane pour ses importants programmes de construction à Istanbul et ailleurs. Ils finirent par représenter  l’essentiel de la production des ateliers d’Iznik et un grand nombre d’entre eux sont encore en place aujourd’hui.
dates: Fin Xe siècle de l’Hégire (fin XVIe siècle J.-C.).
materials: Céramique frittée, sous-glaçure bleue, verte et noire, barbotine rouge en sous-glaçure, glaçure transparente.

en.name: Cathedral
description: Lamego Cathedral dates back to the 11th century, but everything to be seen nowadays is from a later date, the oldest part being the base of the tower. The new façade with its three beautiful Late Gothic portals dates from the Manueline period, in 1508, and the following years. João Lopes was the Master Craftsman and Juan de Vargas and Juan de Pamenes, Spaniards from Cantabria, assisted him. Part of the cloister is also Manueline, begun at the end of 1524 by Duarte Coelho.
