en.name: Mosque of Aqsunqur
description:
Amir Aqsunqur was one of al-Nasir Muhammad’s *amirs*, he was also one of his sons-in-law and later became governor of Tripoli, Lebanon. Among the many buildings commissioned by Amir Aqsunqur, in this same street, we find his house, several public drinking fountains and a watering trough for animals. With his interest in architecture, he personally took charge of the supervision for the building work on the mosque. Built in 747/1347, it follows the traditional hypostyle plan; a central courtyard surrounded by four porticoes, the largest of which is the prayer hall with two aisles.  
Its name derives from its east wall, tiled from floor to ceiling in beautifully coloured majolica, the predominant shade being blue. This tile work is a later addition from one of the renovations carried out by the Ottoman Ibrahim Agha Mustahfazan, in 1062/1652.  
Another notable feature of this mosque is its marble *minbar*, decorated with an unusual design of bunches of grapes and vine leaves and inlaid with coloured stones. It is one of the few *minbars* ever built with this costly material and one of the oldest in Cairo.

es.name: Mezquita de Aqsunqur (opción)
description:
El emir Aqsunqur fue uno de los emires de al-Nasir Muhammad, uno de sus yernos y luego gobernador de Trípoli, ciudad del norte del Líbano. Entre las numerosas edificaciones de este emir, en la misma calle Bab al-Wazir se encuentran su casa, varias fuentes públicas y un abrevadero. Interesado en la construcción, se encargó personalmente de supervisar las obras de edificación de su mezquita que, construida en 747/1347, sigue el modelo de la planta hipóstila tradicional: un patio central rodeado por cuatro pórticos, el mayor de los cuales es el de la *qibla* con dos naves.  
Su nombre de mezquita azul se debe al revestimiento de su pared este —desde el suelo hasta el techo— con mayólica de bellos colores entre los que predomina el azul, resultado de una de las reformas emprendidas por el otomano Ibrahim Aga Mustahfazan, en 1062/1652.  
Lo más destacable de esta mezquita radica en su *mimbar* de mármol, tallado con una original decoración de racimos de uva y hojas de parra con incrustaciones de piedras de colores, uno de los pocos realizados en este material tan costoso y uno de los más antiguos conservados en El Cairo.

fr.name: Mosquée de Aqsunqur (option)
description:
L’émir Aqsunqur fut l’un des émirs de al-Nasir Muhammad, un de ses gendres et plus tard gouverneur de Tripoli, une ville du nord du Liban. Parmi les nombreuses édifications dues à cet émir, dans la même rue Bab al-Wazir se trouvent sa maison, plusieurs fontaines publiques et un abreuvoir. Intéressé par la construction, l’émir se chargea lui-même de superviser les travaux d’édification de sa mosquée, laquelle, construite en 747/1347, obéit au modèle à plan hypostyle traditionnel avec une cour centrale entourée de quatre portiques, dont le plus grand, à deux nefs, est celui du mur de la *qibla*.  
Elle doit son nom de mosquée bleue au revêtement qui, du sol au plafond, orne la paroi est de majoliques de belles couleurs – parmi lesquelles prédomine le bleu –, résultat de l’une des réformes entreprises par l’Ottoman Ibrahim Agha Mustahfazan en 1062/1652.  
L’élément le plus remarquable de cette mosquée réside dans son *minbar* de marbre sculpté, dont l’originale décoration de grappes de raisin et de feuilles de vigne est incrustée de pierres de couleur; il fait partie des rares exemples réalisés dans ce matériau si coûteux, et des plus anciens qui soient conservés au Caire.

It depicts one of the episodes which preceded the Treaty of Bardo and took place on the Algerian-Tunisian border near the town of Kef. Zouave troops can be seen at the front of the French troops.

ar.name: إبريق.
description: ربما يكون شكل هذا الإبريق تقليداً لنموذج أصلي مصنوع من الزجاج، وهو احتمال يعززه النسق المتراصف على شكل دوائر مماثلة لتلك التي وُجدت على الأواني الزجاجية الإيرانية المعاصرة. الإبريق مقولب ومصبوغ بلون الخزامى الأزرق الشاحب، لكن قاعدته تنقصها الدقة، كما أنه تُرك دون أي تزجيج. يبيِّن شكل هذا الإناء تأثير الصناعة الخزفية في إيران على مثيلتها في الرقة. كانت الرقة أحد مركزين رئيسيين لإنتاج الخزف في سوريا العصر الأيوبي، بينما كانت الرصافة ثانيهما. ففي الرقة كان هنالك عدد من الورش المصنِّعة للخزف، وقد أنتجت مجموعة كبيرة من الأواني الفخارية؛ منها ذات البريق المعدني، والمفرَّغ في قوالب منقوشة، والمزيَّن برسوم تحت طبقة مزجَّجة.

كثيراً ما درج خزَّافو الشرق الأوسط على النظر إلى صناعات أخرى، التماساً للإلهام الفني. وشَكْلُ هذا الإبريق مقولبٌ تقليداً لأنموذج أصلي من الزجاج. والهوامش المثلَّمة الدائرية التي تُزيِّن بطن الإبريق، موجودة أيضاً على أوانٍ زجاجية إيرانية معاصرة.
keywords: آنية منزلية؛ حرفة.
materials: عجينة بيضاء كوارتزية مع تزجيج بلون أزرق غير شفاف.
tags: عجينة بيضاء كوارتزية مع تزجيج بلون أزرق غير شفاف.

en.name: Jug.
description: The shape of this jug probably copies a glass prototype, a probability further endorsed by the indentations that are arranged in a circular pattern similar to that found on contemporary Iranian glassware. The jug is moulded and glazed with an interesting opaque lavender-blue colour, but falling short of the foot, which has been left unglazed. The shape of this vessel shows the influence of Iranian ceramics on Raqqa's pottery industry. Raqqa was one of two major pottery-production centres in Ayyubid Syria, the other being Rusafah. Raqqa had a number of pottery workshops, which produced a range of ceramics including lustre-painted, relief-moulded and underglaze-painted vessels.

The potters of the Middle East were frequently looking at other industries for artistic inspiration. The shape of this jug is moulded, copying a glass prototype. The circular indentations that decorate the belly of the jug are also found on contemporary Iranian glassware.
keywords: Domestic wares; crafts

es.name: Jarro.
description:
La forma de este jarro recuerda modelos en vidrio, impresión que confirma el diseño circular de los rehundimientos, similar al de objetos de vidrio iraníes contemporáneos. Tras moldearlo, el jarro se vidrió en un peculiar azul lavanda opaco que no cubrió por completo el pie.  
La forma es una muestra de la influencia de la cerámicas iraníe en la industria y alfarería de Raqqa. Raqqa y Rusafah eran los dos mayores centros productores de alfarería en la Siria Ayubbí. En Raqqa había un gran número de talleres que producían varios tipos de cerámica: vasijas de reflejo metálico, moldeadas en relieve y pintadas bajo vidriado.

Los alfareros de Oriente Próximo buscaban frecuentemente inspiración en otras artes. Este jarro está moldeado siguiendo un prototipo en vidrio. Encontramos el mismo diseño circular de rehundimientos que decora esta pieza en objetos de vidrio iraníes de la misma época.
dates: Siglo VI de la Hégira / XII d. C.
keywords: objetos de uso doméstico; artesanía.

fr.name: Cruche.
description: La forme de cette cruche s'inspire probablement d'un prototype en verre, ce que confirment les indentations disposées en motif circulaire, similaires à celles trouvées sur des pièces de verrerie iranienne contemporaines. La cruche moulée est vernie d'une intéressante couleur bleu lavande opaque, qui ne couvre pas le pied. Cette forme montre l'influence de la céramique iranienne sur la poterie de Raqqa. Cette ville était l'un des deux grands centre de production de poterie dans la Syrie des Ayyoubides, l'autre étant Rusafa. La ville possédait un certain nombre d'ateliers de potiers qui produisaient une gamme de céramiques dont des récipients à décor lustré, moulés en relief ou peints sous glaçure.

Les potiers du Moyen-Orient puisaient souvent leur inspiration artistique dans les autres corps de métier. La forme de cette cruche moulée copie un prototype en verre. Les indentations circulaires qui décorent le ventre du pichet se trouvent également sur des pièces de verrerie iranienne de la même époque.
dates: VIe siècle de l’Hégire (XIIe siècle J.-C.).
keywords: récipients domestiques ; artisanat
materials: Céramique frittée à glaçure opaque bleue.
tags: Céramique frittée à glaçure opaque bleue.

de.name: Deckengemälde *Verehrung der hl. Dreifaltigkeit*
description: Der sonst wenig bekannte Freskant Franz Joseph Haller hat in der westlichen Kuppel mit der Thematik eines Heiligenhimmels fast vollständig auf gemalte Architektur verzichtet, von ein paar überleitenden Treppenstufen am unteren Rand abgesehen. Stattdessen bleibt hier die Wirkung der ganz in Augsburger Tradition leuchtenden Farbigkeit überlassen, die hier lichtdurchflutete Wolken darstellt, vor denen sich die prachtvollen Gewänder der Heiligen effektvoll abheben. Die Komposition ist weniger auf das Rund angelegt, als vom östlichen Rand zur Mitte hin gestaffelt, ausgerichtet auf dem in die Kirche eintretenden Besucher.

en.name: Ceiling painting *Veneration of the Holy Trinity*
description: In his rendering of a heaven of the saints in the western cupola, the otherwise little known fresco artist Franz Joseph Haller has largely dispensed with painted architecture, with the exception of a few transitionary steps at the bottom edge. Instead, its effect is achieved through the luminous colours used to depict clouds suffused with light, against which the magnificent robes of the saints stand out dramatically. The composition is designed less with reference to the circular form than staggered from the eastern edge to the centre, thus oriented towards the entering visitor.

en.name: *Strike fund*
short_description: "Strike funds" were established during strikes, collecting money which they received from donations and subscription fees. These funds are able to financially support strikers, who no longer received their salaries and therefore had no means of survival. This drawing emphasises the anxiety on the faces of the workers and their families, who relied wholly on this solidarity for their food and lodgings. It also mocks the role of the Minister of the Interior, who was sending in military troops instead of funds. Indeed, many strikes were interrupted by the arrival of military forces between 1899 and 1901.
keywords: Strikes; solidarity; France; cartoon; caricature

fr.name: *Caisse de grève*
short_description: Lors des grèves, peuvent être constituées des « caisses de grève » alimentées par des dons et les cotisations syndicales. L’argent ainsi récolté permet de soutenir financièrement les grévistes qui ne touchent plus leur paie et n’ont donc plus de moyens de subsistance. Sur ce dessin, on voit les expressions inquiètes des grévistes et de leurs familles qui ne peuvent compter pour se nourrir et se loger, que sur l’éventuelle solidarité. Ce dessin d’humour ironise sur le rôle du ministre de l’Intérieur qui n’envoie pas de dons mais les troupes. En effet, plusieurs grèves entre 1899 et 1901 viennent d’être interrompues par l’envoi de troupes militaires.
keywords: Grèves; Solidarité; France

description: A vase in lost-wax moulded clear glass with a grey patina, decorated with four groups of doves in high relief which form the handles of the vase.

ar.name: 'سجادة لوتو
description:
هذه السجادة صغيرة الحجم يهيمن عليها شكل صليب يشكل عادة جزءًا من نمط أكثر اتساعًا مصنوع من الصلبان والأشكال المعينيَة. ومع ذلك، بفضل هذه الزخارف يمكن التعرف على هذه السجادة على أنها من نوع يسمى بالسجادة "لوتو"، سُمية على اسم فنان عصر النهضة لورينزو لوتو (885-963 هجري / 1480-1557 م)، الذي خلد مثل هذه السجادة على لوحة المذبح التي تصور محبة القديس أنطونيوس.  
  
الحدود غير نمطية تمامًا، مما يشير إلى تاريخ محتمل لهذه السجادة تحديدًا في أواخر القرن السابع عشر.
dates: أواخر القرن 11 الهجري / أواخر القرن 17 الميلادي

en.name: *Lotto* carpet
description:
This small-sized carpet is dominated by a cross-shaped motif that normally forms a part of a more extensive pattern made of crosses and diamonds. However, it is thanks to this motif that this carpet can be identified as of the so-called Lotto type, named after the Renaissance artist Lorenzo Lotto (Hegira 885-963 / AD 1480-1556-57), who immortalised such a carpet on an altarpiece depicting the charity of Saint Anthony.  
  
The border is quite untypical, pointing to a probable date of the late 17th century for this particular carpet.
dates: Hegira late 11th century / AD late 17th century

en.name: *Der heilige Sebastian (Saint Sebastian)*
description: Antonello da Messina set the martyrdom of Saint Sebastian in Venice, as is evident from the waterways in the background or from the typical chimneys. As one of the largest European trading cities, Venice was a key hub for the exchange of exotic luxury goods. The two carpets depicted here would also have come to the lagoon city via trading routes. According to information provided by Stefano Carboni (2015), these were carpets from the Ottoman Empire. They were highly sought after as decorative items throughout Europe. Antonello da Messina painted this picture for the first altar of the Brotherhood of Saint Roch in the Church of San Giuliano in Venice. With its extremely steep perspective, the lifelike rendering of the flesh and the three-dimensional modelling of the nude figure, this work is a tour de force of early Renaissance painting.
holder: Gemäldegalerie Alte Meister (Old Masters Picture Gallery), Dresden State Art Collections
keywords: Painting; Christianity; Bibel; Venice; Anatolia; Carpet; Renaissance
materials: Oil on wood, transferred to canvas
tags: Oil on wood, transferred to canvas
partner: Dresden State Art Collections, Gemäldegalerie Alte Meister (Old Masters Picture Gallery)

en.name: Darracq 12HP Open Tourer
description: Alexandre Darracq began his storied career in the late 19th century with the manufacture of the successful Gladiator bicycles, which competed well in the French market of the 1890s. Dating from 1902, this car, sporting an Open Tourer bodywork, is one of the most important units of the Darracq brand. It was with this exact model that the French manufacturer launched himself properly into the automobile manufacturing scene. This extraordinary car is unique in the world: Its engine architecture has two separate cylinders which are connected in such a way that it appears as two single-cylinder engines.

ar.name: لوحة تخطيط
description: اعتبارا من القرن السادس عشر فإن اللوحات التخطيطية كانت منتشرة جدا في الإمبراطورية العثمانية .وهذه اللوحة كتبت من قبل حسني في عام 1877. وإن طراز الكتابة المستخدم هو خط السيلي ثلث أو الثلث. وكان هذا الطراز مستخدما بشكل واسع في نقوش الأبنية والقطع الأخرى وعدد من الصفائح المنفردة ولوحات التخطيط الكبيرة كانت أيضا تكتب باستخدام هذا الطراز. والاقتباسات الدينية المذهبة بشكل جميل المكتوبة على لوحات كبيرة كانت تستخدم لتزيين المساجد . وبعض هذه اللوحات كان يراد أن ترسم على بلاطات وكانت ترسم كمسودات في البداية قبل أن يعاد تشكيل التصاميم على البلاطات.والمخطوطة هي داخل إطار ذهبي مزين بالأزهار الذي يساعد على موازنة التشكيل. وباللغة العربية تقول :"" استسلم لأمر الله ورغبته واخضع  للقدر الذي قدره"".
dates: القرن الثالث عشر الهجري /  القرن التاسع عشر الميلادي
keywords: تخطيط

en.name: Calligraphic Panel (*Levha*)
description:
From the 16th century, calligraphic panels were highly popular in the Ottoman Empire. This one was written by Hüsni in 1877. The style of writing used is *celi sülüs*, or *thuluth*. This style was widely used for inscriptions on buildings and other objects, and a number of individual sheets and large calligraphic panels were also written using this style. Beautifully illuminated religious quotations, written on large panels, were used to decorate mosques. Some of these panels were intended to be painted on tile and were first drafts before the designs were recreated on the tiles.  
The manuscript is inside a golden frame decorated with flowers, which help balance the composition. In Arabic, it reads, "surrender to the command and desire of God and submit to the fate determined by him."
keywords: Calligraphy

en.name: Bab al-Maqam
description: The initial construction of Bab al-Maqam was under the auspices of al-Zahir Ghazi, but completed by his son, Muhammad, in around 627/1230; extensive alterations took place during the Mamluk period. Far less impressive than other Ayyubid gates, it differs from them by its lack of towers and by the fact that its original design was one of a triple gate with a large central opening flanked by two smaller ones, the traces of which are still visible in the masonry. Such tripartite gates were practically unknown in medieval Syria as they only had minimal defensive capabilities. Bab al-Maqam was most likely a ceremonial gate that stood on the road linking the Ayyubid monuments in the Maqamat with the citadel.

ar.name: مصحف
description: هذه الصفحات هي جزء من مجموعة مكونة من 201 صفحة لأحد أقدم المصاحف الموجودة وهي مخطوطة التي تعتبرعموما أنها أنتجت في بداية القرن الثامن وبالتالي هذا لا يزيد عن قرن بعد وفاة النبي محمد في السنة الحادية عشرة من العصر الإسلامي (632 ميلادي). إن نص القرآن يكون دائما بالعربية وهذه الصفحات مكتوبة بالخط الكوفي على رق. والعصابات الملونة للتزيين الهندسي هي بمجموعة ألوان مكونة بشكل أساسي من أصبغة بالأحمر، الأزرق ، الأخضر و الأصفر والتي تحدد بداية السورة الجديدة من القرآن.

en.name: Qur'an
description: These folios are part of a 201-folio fragment of one of the oldest Qur’ans in existence, a manuscript that is generally accepted as having been produced in the early eighth century, and therefore no more than a century after the death of the Prophet Muhammad in the eleventh year of the Islamic era (AD 632). The text of the Qur’an is always in Arabic and on these folios it is written in *kufic* script on vellum. Colourful bands of mainly geometrical decoration in a palette consisting primarily of red, blue, green and yellow pigments mark the start of each new *sura* (chapter) of the Qur’an.

ar.name: صحن.
description: صحن سميك غير مزخرف، مزجَّج بلون كثيف من الفيروزي الداكن: إنه نموذج نمطي، من حيث طريقة الصنع والشكل، عن المنتجات الخزفية في الرقة. وعلى الرغم من التآكل الشديد الذي أصابه، فإن الطلاء ما يزال يدلُّ على الروعة التي كانت لهذا الصحن البسيط في عصره. فاللون الفيروزي كان محطَّ إعجاب من الناحية الجمالية، فضلاً عن الاعتقاد بتوافره على خصائص حمائية، الأمر الذي جعله شائعاً في الصناعة الخزفية في طول مناطق الشرق الأوسط الإسلامية وعرضها. كانت الرقة أحد مركزين رئيسيين لإنتاج الخزف في سوريا العصر الأيوبي، بينما كانت الرصافة ثانيهما. ففي الرقة كان هنالك عدد من المشاغل لتصنيع الخزف، وقد أنتجت مجموعة كبيرة من الأواني الفخارية؛ منها ذات البريق المعدني، والمفرَّغ في قوالب منقوشة، والمزيَّن برسوم تحت طبقة مزجَّجة. وقد توقف إنتاج الخزف عندما خرَّب المغول المدينة تماماً في عام 657 / 1259.

رغم زخرفه الرديء، يبدو أن هذا الصحن الفيروزي كان أزرق اللون، أخاذاً، حين كان لا يزال جديداً. والرقّة في سورية كانت أحد المراكز المهمة لإنتاج الخزفيات خلال الفترة الأيوبية، حيث كان يتمّ إنتاج العديد من القطع ذوات اللمعة الفيروزية، التي كانت بشارة خير شعبية، في الشرق الأوسط.
keywords: آنية منزلية.
materials: عجينة بيضاء كوارتزية مع تزجيج بلون فيروزي داكن.
tags: عجينة بيضاء كوارتزية مع تزجيج بلون فيروزي داكن.

en.name: Dish.
description:
An undecorated, thickly potted dish with a heavily applied deep-turquoise glaze that is typical of Raqqa ware in both its manufacture and shape. Though badly deteriorating, the glaze still indicates how beautiful this plain dish would have been in its time. The colour turquoise was appreciated aesthetically, and was thought to have protective qualities, rendering it popular in ceramics throughout the Islamic Middle East.  
  
Raqqa was one of two major pottery-production centres in Ayyubid Syria, the other being Rusafah. In Raqqa there were a number of pottery workshops that produced a range of ceramics including lustre-painted, relief-moulded and underglaze-painted vessels. The pottery production ceased when the Mongols razed the city to the ground in AH 657 / AD 1259.

Though badly deteriorated, this turquoise dish would have looked strikingly blue when still new. Raqqa in Syria was an important centre for the production of ceramics during the Ayyubid period, generating many pieces with turquoise glazing, which was a popular auspicious colour in the Middle East.
keywords: Domestic vessels.

es.name: Plato.
description: Plato de cerámica gruesa sin decorar, con un espeso vidriado en color turquesa fuerte. Se trata de un modelo típico de Raqqa, tanto en su fabricación como en su forma. El vidriado, aunque muy deteriorado, aún da idea de la belleza original del plato. El color turquesa era muy popular en la cerámica islámica de Oriente Medio por su belleza y sus supuestas cualidades protectoras. Raqqa y Rusafah eran los dos mayores centros productores de alfarería en la Siria ayyubí. En Raqqa había un gran número de talleres que producían varios tipos de cerámicas vasijas de reflejo metálico, moldeadas en relieve y pintadas bajo vidriado. La producción cesó cuando los mongoles arrasaron la ciudad en 657 / 1259.

El azul de este plato, ahora muy deteriorado, sería bastante llamativo en el momento de su fabricación. El azul era un color muy popular en Oriente Medio, ya que se creía que portaba buenos augurios. En el periodo ayyubí se produjeron en Raqqa, importante centro productor de cerámica de la época, muchas piezas con este vidriado turquesa.
dates: Siglo VII de la Hégira / XIII d. C.
keywords: vasijas de uso doméstico.
materials: Pasta de piedra vidriada en color turquesa fuerte.
tags: Pasta de piedra vidriada en color turquesa fuerte.

fr.name: Plat.
description:
Lourd plat sans décor à épaisse glaçure turquoise foncé, typique de la production de Raqqa aussi bien par sa forme que son style de fabrication. Bien que gravement détériorée, la glaçure conserve une idée de la beauté que pouvait revêtir ce simple plat à son époque. La couleur turquoise, appréciée pour ses qualités esthétiques, était censée offrir une protection, ce qui rendit son usage très populaire en céramique dans tout le Moyen-Orient islamique.  
Raqqa fut l'un des deux grands centres de production de poterie de la Syrie ayyoubide, l'autre étant Rusafa. On y trouvait un certain nombre d'ateliers qui produisaient différentes céramiques, dont des pièces décorées au lustre, moulées en relief ou peintes sous glaçure. La production cessa lorsque les Mongols rasèrent la ville en 657 H / 1259 J.-C.

Bien que très détérioré, ce plat turquoise devait être d’un bleu saisissant quand il était neuf. Raqqa en Syrie était un important centre de production de céramique pendant la période ayyoubide, avec de nombreuses pièces à glaçure turquoise, qui était une couleur populaire de bon augure dans le Moyen-Orient.
dates: VIIe siècle de l’Hégire (XIIIe siècle J.-C.).
keywords: récipients domestiques
materials: Céramique frittée à glaçure turquoise foncé.
tags: Céramique frittée à glaçure turquoise foncé.

ar.name: مرآة.
description:
هذه القطعة هي قطعة الأشغال الفولاذية الوحيدة المتبقية من أشغال المعدن في عهد سلاجقة الأناضول. القطعة عبارة عن مرآة مسبوكة منزَّلة بالذهب تحمل زخرفة تصويرية بنقش بارز قليلاً. الزخرفة مشابهة إلى حد بعيد لتلك التي تزين المرايا الأرتقية، فهي تتألف من رصيعة مدوَّرة عليها صياد يمتطي جواداً، ويحيط به إطار يشتمل على صور حيوانات تطارد بعضها بعضاً. يُستدل من الهالة المحيطة برأس الصياد الفارس أنه شخصية ذات شأن. فوجهه وعيناه المائلتان وشعره الطويل وزيّه تمثل جميعها نمط النبيل السلجوقي. التفاصيل الزخرفية على القطعة مثل الصقر الذي يحمله الفارس على رسغه الأيسر، والذيل المعقود للحصان، وكذلك قائمة الحصان اليمنى المرفوعة، تبين تأثير فن آسيا الوسطى على فن سلاجقة الأناضول.  
  
المثال الأول على تشكيل كهذا في الفن الإسلامي وُجد على صحن خزفي يعود إلى القرن 4 / 10. اللافت للانتباه أن طوق كلب الصيد مربوط إلى السرج، فقد جرت العادة أن تكون كلاب الصيد طليقة في تشكيلات مماثلة تعود لهذه الفترة. إن الطير الجارح في الزاوية العلوية اليسرى والثعلب في الزاوية العلوية اليمنى يمثلان الطريدة. كما أن صورة التنين الواقع تحت القائمتين الأماميتين للحصان تعيد إلى الذهن تماثيل مشابهة في التصوير الجصِّي لآسيا الوسطى وفن الأيقونات المسيحي في الأناضول.  
  
في وسط الجزء العلوي من إفريز الإطار يوجد تنينان متشابكا الجسدين يتصارعان ويعضُّ كل منهما الآخر. المحور المتشكل بواسطة القبضة والتنينين محاط على التوالي بكل من: عنقاء برأس طائر وجسد أسد، ودب، ومخلوق خيالي نصفه العلوي إنسان ونصفه السفلي أسد، وغزلان. وثمة صورة للمخلوق الخرافي القنطور الذي يرمز إلى برج القوس، ولكن هذا المخلوق الذي يتخذ عادة جزؤه العلوي شكل إنسان والسفلي شكل فرس مُثل جزؤه السفلي في هذه الصورة بشكل أسد.

لاشك أن أدوات الاستعمال اليومي تُقدِّم بيانات بالغة الأهمية عن الحياة الاجتماعية. وهذه المرآة، وهي الوحيدة الباقية من تلك المصنوعة من الفولاذ، تُوفِّر شاهداً على الحياة الاجتماعية، والأيقونات النافرة، للحقبة السلجوقية في الأناضول.
keywords: زخرفة تصويرية؛ شغل بالمعدن؛ فولاذ؛ مشهد صيد.

tags: فولاذ مصبوب، تقنيات التنزيل والنقش ضئيل البروز.

en.name: Mirror.
description:
This is the only surviving work of steel among the metalwork from the Anatolian Seljuq period. The mirror cast and inlaid with gold, bears figurative decoration in low relief. The decoration, which closely resembles that on Artuqid mirrors, comprises a medallion with a mounted hunter encircled by a border of animal figures chasing each other.  
  
The hunter on horseback is inferred to be an important figure for he has a halo around his head. His round face, slanting eyes, long hair and costume represent a typical Seljuq nobleman. Details such as the falcon he carries on his left wrist, the knotted tail of the horse, and its raised right foreleg are traces of the Central Asian influence found in the art of the Anatolian Seljuqs.  
  
The first example of such a composition in Islamic art is found on a ceramic plate of the AH 4th / AD 10th century. The greyhound with its collar tied to the horseman's saddle is interesting because in similar compositions of this period the greyhound is always loose. A bird of prey in the upper left corner and a fox in the upper right represent the hunt. The dragon motif under the forelegs of the horse recalls similar imagery in Central Asian frescoes and Christian iconography in Anatolia.  
  
In the centre of the upper part of the border frieze is a pair of confronted dragons with knotted bodies biting each other. The axis formed by the handle and the pair of dragons is flanked with, respectively, a griffin with a bird's head and a lion's body, a bear, a fantastic creature with the upper body of a man and the lower body of a lion, and gazelles. The figure of a centaur, symbolising the zodiac sign of Sagittarius, normally has the upper body of a man and the lower body of a horse, but here it is depicted with the lower body of a lion.

Items of daily use no doubt provide the most important data on social life. This mirror, the only surviving example in steel, provides evidence regarding the social life and iconographic beliefs of the Anatolian Seljuq period.
keywords: Figurative decoration; hunting scene; metalwork; steel
materials: Cast steel, low relief and inlay techniques.
tags: Cast steel, low relief and inlay techniques.

es.name: Espejo.
description:
Este es el único objeto de acero que se conserva de toda la metalistería del periodo selyuquí de Anatolia. Se trata de un espejo de fundición con incrustaciones de oro y decoración figurativa en bajorrelieve. La ornamentación, muy parecida a la de los espejos artuquíes, incluye un medallón con un cazador a caballo rodeado por un borde de figuras de animales persiguiéndose unos a otros.  
El jinete tiene un halo alrededor de la cabeza, por lo que se infiere que fue un personaje importante. Sus facciones redondeadas, sus ojos rasgados, su larga cabellera y sus ropajes son típicos de los nobles selyuquíes.  
Detalles como el halcón posado en su muñeca izquierda y el caballo, con la cola anudada y la pata delantera derecha levantada, son muestras de la influencia centroasiática en el arte de los selyuquíes anatolios.  
El primer ejemplo de este tipo de composiciones en el arte islámico se halló en un plato de cerámica del siglo IV / X. Resulta llamativo que el galgo vaya atado por el collar a la silla de montar del jinete, porque en imágenes similares del mismo periodo el perro aparece siempre suelto. El ave de rapiña del ángulo superior izquierdo y el zorro de la parte superior derecha simbolizan la caza. El motivo del dragón bajo las patas delanteras del caballo recuerda la imaginería de los frescos del centro de Asia y la iconografía cristiana de Anatolia.  
En el centro de la parte superior del borde hay dos dragones enfrentados con los cuerpos entrelazados, mordiéndose mutuamente. El eje formado por la agarradera del espejo y los dragones está flanqueado por un grifo con cabeza de pájaro y cuerpo de león, un oso, gacelas y un ser fantástico con la parte superior del cuerpo de hombre y la inferior de león. La figura del centauro, que simboliza el signo zodiacal de sagitario, normalmente es hombre en su parte superior y caballo en la inferior, pero aquí está representada con cuerpo de león.

Los artículos de uso cotidiano aportan la información más importante sobre la vida social. Este espejo, único ejemplar en acero que se conserva, aporta información sobre la vida y la imaginería durante el periodo selyuquí de Anatolia.
dates: Siglo VII Hégira / XIII d. C.
keywords: Decoración figurativa; escena de caza; metalistería, acero.

fr.name: Miroir.
description:
Ce miroir incrusté d'or à décoration figurative en bas relief est le seul objet en acier parvenu de la période des Seldjoukides d'Anatolie. Le décor qui ressemble étroitement à celui des miroirs de la période artukide est essentiellement constitué d'un médaillon orné d'un chasseur à cheval, entouré d'une bordure d'animaux se pourchassant.  
Ce chasseur doit être un personnage important puisque sa tête est cerclée d'une auréole. Son visage rond, ses yeux bridés, sa longue chevelure et son costume présentent tous les traits caractéristiques des nobles seldjoukides. Des détails comme le faucon sur son poignet droit, la queue tressée du cheval et la patte avant relevée de celui-ci sont des traces d'une influence d'Asie centrale que l'on retrouve dans l'art seldjoukide anatolien. Le premier exemple d'une telle composition en art islamique figure sur une assiette de céramique du IVe siècle H (Xe siècle J.-C.). Le lévrier à collier attaché à la selle du cavalier est intéressant car dans certaines compositions de cette époque, le chien est généralement libre de ses mouvements. Un oiseau de proie, dans le coin supérieur gauche, et un renard, dans le coin inférieur droit, symbolisent la chasse. Le motif du dragon sous les pattes avant du cheval rappelle des images semblables observées dans des fresques d'Asie centrale et dans l'iconographie chrétienne d'Anatolie. Au centre de la partie supérieure de la frise de bordure se trouve un couple de dragons affrontés aux corps entrenoués se mordant l'un l'autre. L'axe formé par le manche et le couple de dragons est flanqué par un griffon à tête d'oiseau et corps de lion, un ours, une créature fantastique dont le haut du corps est humain et la partie basse appartient à un lion, et des gazelles. La figure du centaure, symbole du signe zodiacal du sagittaire, est généralement mi-homme mi-cheval, mais ici la partie inférieure est celle d'un corps de lion.

Les objets d’usage quotidien procurent sans aucun doute de précieux renseignements sur la vie sociale. Ce miroir, unique exemple en acier de cette époque, nous informe sur la vie sociale et les croyances iconographiques de la période des Seldjoukides d’Anatolie.
dates: VIIe siècle de l’Hégire (XIIIe siècle J.-C.).
keywords: travail du métal ; acier ; décoration figurative ; scènes de chasse
materials: Fonte d’acier, décor en bas relief et incrustations.
tags: Fonte d’acier, décor en bas relief et incrustations.

tr.name: Ayna.
description:
Anadolu Selçuklu Dönemi'nden bugüne kalmış madeni eserler arasında çelik malzemeli tek örnek olan alçak kabartma tekniği ile oluşturulmuş figürlü bezemeye sahip ayna, döküm tekniği ile yapılmış ve altın malzeme ile kakma tekniği kullanılarak süslenmiştir. Artuklu dönemi aynalarıyla yakın benzerliklere sahip örneğin ortasında atlı avcı tasvirli bir madalyon ve onun etrafında birbirini kovalayan hayvan figürleri ile doldurulmuş friz bulunmaktadır.  
  
Madalyonun içinde, başındaki hale nedeniyle önemli bir insan olduğunu anladığımız atlı avcı; yuvarlak yüz hattı, çekik gözleri, uzun saçları ve kıyafetiyle tipik bir Selçuklu soylusunu canlandırmaktadır. Avcının sol el bileğinde taşıdığı avcı doğan kuşu, atın kuyruğunun düğümlü ve ön sağ ayağının kalkık tasviri gibi bazı özellikler Anadolu'da Selçuklu Dönemi'nde görülen Orta Asya sanatının etkileridir. Böyle bir kompozisyonun İslam Sanatındaki ilk örneği ise 10. yüzyıla tarihlendirilen bir seramik tabak üzerinde görülmektedir. Madalyonun içindeki atlı avcı sahnesinde, boynundaki tasma ile atın eyerine bağlanmış tazı figürü, aynı döneme ait benzer uygulamalarda serbest halde tasvir edilmesi nedeniyle ilginç bir uygulamadır. Sol üst köşede uçan bir av hayvanı, sağ alt köşede kaçan bir tilki tasviri av'ı temsil etmektedir. Atın ön ayakları altında bulunan ejder figürü ise Orta Asya fresklerinde ve Anadolu'da Hıristiyan ikonografisinde görülen benzer sahneleri hatırlatmaktadır. Aynanın kenarını dolanan frizin üst kısmının ortasında, gövdeleri kıvrım yapan, birbirilerini ısırır pozisyonda tasvir edilmiş karşılıklı iki ejder figürü bulunmaktadır. Sap ve çifte ejderlerin oluşturduğu eksenin her iki tarafında sırasıyla; kuş başlı aslan gövdeli grifon, ayı, belden yukarısı insan belden aşağısı aslan olarak tasvir edilen efsanevi bir yaratık ve ardından da ceylan figürleri sıralanmaktadır. Belden üstü insan, gövdesi at şeklinde tasvir edilen ve yay burcunun simgesi olan kentavros, burada aslan gövdeli olarak tasvir edilmiştir.

Sosyal hayatın en önemli verileri, kuşkusuz günlük yaşamın bir parçası olan kullanım eşyalarıdır. Anadolu Selçuklu Dönemi sosyal hayatı ve ikonografik inanışları hakkında önemli ipuçları veren çelik ayna, malzemesi bakımından da tek örnek olma özelliğine sahiptir.
keywords: Maden sanatı; çelik; figürlü tezyinat; av sahnesi
materials: Çelik. Döküm, alçak kabartma ve kakma tekniği.

ar.name: قطعة خشبية.
description: وُجِد في منطقة الرقة مجموعات من القطع الخشبية التي كانت تزين القاعات الرسمية الملكية في القصور. ويمكن تصنيف هذه المجموعات إلى ثلاث فئات، وذلك حسب أسلوب الصنع والزخرفة. المجموعة الأولى زخارفها محفورة وملونة ومذهّبة، وهي تشبه الواقع بحيث تظهر التصميمات مثل الأوراق والأزهار بأشكال شبه واقعية. المجموعة الثانية منفذة بأسلوب الحفر المائل بحيث تبدو أطراف وسطوح هذه الأشكال منحنية وليست حادة، ومثل هذا الطراز ظهر أيضاً في سامراء/3/ ويُنسَب إليها. المجموعة الثالثة زخارفها محفورة بشكل عمودي، بحيث يبدو السطحان العلوي والسفلي مسطحين، أما الزخارف فحوافها حادة. تنتمي هذه القطعة إلى المجموعة الأخيرة، إذ أن زخارفها محفورة بأسلوب الحفر العمودي. وقد زينت بزخارف كتابية بالخط الكوفي نصها "أمير المؤمنـ] ـين[". ويبدو على القطعة آثار حريق.
لوحة خشبية، ذات رسومات مُصوَّرة, تمَّت زخرفتها بالحفر على شكل زوايا قائمة، ودوائر عميقة، والتي اشتهرت في العصر العباسي، وانتشرت من هناك إلى المناطق المحيطة كافة.
keywords: أسلوب سامرّاء C؛ خشب محفور؛ خط كوفي؛ الرقة.

en.name: Fragment from a carved wooden piece.
description: In the Raqqa region one can find fragments of wood that once decorated the formal halls of its Abbasid royal palaces. It is possible to classify these fragments into three types according to their techniques of decoration. The first group is adorned with relatively realistic coloured and gilded carved ornamentation that includes floral and calligraphic motifs. The second group is carved in a slanted manner so that the edges of the carved objects appear curved and not sharp. The examples of this group are influenced by the Abbasid Samarra motifs identified as "Samarra Style C". The third group, to which this piece belongs, has decorative motifs carved in a vertical manner so that the panel appears to have an upper surface and a lower background. The decorative carving is flat with sharp edges and the groove to the background is deep, as can be seen in the small deep holes indicating the circular part of the calligraphic letters. The piece is decorated with Arabic *kufic* script that reads “Commander of the Faithful.” It seems to have been partially burned in a fire.

This calligraphic wooden panel with its sharp vertically carved angles and deep circular grooves is one example of the many carving styles that were developed in the Abbasid period and spread throughout the region.
keywords: Wood; carved; Raqqa; Samarra; kufic script

es.name: Fragmento de madera tallada.
description:
En la región de al-Raqqa se han encontrado fragmentos de madera que, en su día, decoraron los salones oficiales de los palacios reales abbasíes. Estos fragmentos se han clasificado en tres tipos en función de la técnica con que se decoraron.  
El primer grupo está adornado con motivos florales y caligráficos tallados, relativamente realistas, coloreados y dorados.  
El segundo grupo está tallado oblicuamente para que los bordes parezcan curvados y no angulosos. Las piezas de este grupo tienen reminiscencias de los motivos de la Samarra abbasí, conocidos como “estilo C de Samarra”.  
El tercer grupo, al que pertenece esta pieza, presenta motivos decorativos tallados verticalmente, de manera que el panel parece tener una superficie elevada y un fondo más profundo. La talla es plana con bordes afilados y surcos profundos, como se aprecia en los pequeños hoyos que marcan la parte circular de las letras. La inscripción decorativa, en letra cúfica, reza: “Comandante de los creyebtes”. Parece haberse quemado parcialmente.

Este fragmento de madera con caligrafía, en el que se aprecian marcados ángulos verticales y profundos surcos, es un ejemplo de uno de los varios estilos de talla que se desarrollaron en la época abbasí y se extendieron por toda la zona.
dates: Siglo IV o V de la Hégira / X o XI d. C. aproximadamente.
keywords: Madera; talla; al-Raqqa; estilo C de Samarra; escritura cúfica.

fr.name: Fragment d'élément en bois sculpté.
description: On peut encore trouver dans la région de Raqqa des fragments d'éléments en bois qui décoraient jadis les salles d'apparat des palais royaux abbassides. Ils sont classés en trois types, selon leur technique de sculpture. Le premier groupe contient des éléments ornementaux sculptés colorés et dorés relativement réalistes, dont des motifs floraux et calligraphiques. Le second réunit des éléments sculptés en biseau pour donner une impression de contours arrondis. Les exemples de ce groupe ont été influencés par les motifs abbassides de Samarra dit “style Samarra C”. Le troisième groupe, auquel appartient cette pièce, présente des motifs décoratifs sculptés à la verticale de telle façon que le panneau semble posséder deux plans parallèles, celui de la surface de la sculpture et celui du fond. La sculpture est donc traitée en à-plat avec des bords vifs et un relief très marqué, comme on le voit dans les petits trous pratiqués dans les lettres. Le texte en arabe de style coufique se lit : “Commandeur des Fidèles”. Le bois semble avoir été partiellement brûlé.

Ce panneau calligraphique à caractères se détachant verticalement et rainures circulaires en profondeur est un exemple des nombreux styles de sculpture mis au point pendant la période abbasside et diffusés dans la région.
dates: Vers le IVe-Ve siècle de l'Hégire (Xe-XIe siècle J.-C.).
keywords: Bois ; bois sculpté ; Raqqa ; style C de Samarra ; écriture coufique

en.name: al-Ghuta ash-Sharqiyya
description: The apricots are pressed using a press installed in the orchard or in the sheltered part of the facility. This press is equipped with two superimposed sieves, one with large holes to remove the stones and another with a much finer mesh to remove the fibres, leaving only the juice to pass through. The juice is collected in a large-capacity basin of more meticulous construction; the interior is tiled and surmounted by a fixed metal structure. The model of press dates from the 1970s. This operation takes place when the heat dies down at the end of the afternoon.

en.name: *Concerto Grosso*
description:
Following the widespread international acceptance and recognition of the Portalegre Tapestry Manufacture in 1952, their tapestries began to be internationalized, attracting many foreign artists. One of the aims of the manufacturer has been to translate famous contemporary paintings into tapestries. The piece in question is a wool, handwoven wall tapestry after a painting (of the same name) by English practitioner Tom Phillips (1937), himself a multidisciplinary artist whose creative activities include writing, photography and music (both as a musician and composer).  
Several of Philips’ music-themed paintings have been transposed into tapestries. *Concerto Grosso* is one such example, a representation of the dialogue between a set of soloists (*concertino*), usually two violins and a cello, and the remainder of the orchestra.  
The complexity of its formal language is owed to the multiplicity and accuracy of the draughtsmanship, as well as to the infinity of nuances present in its rich chromatic composition, itself enhanced by the Portalegre technique. The wider colour palette (with over 7,000 tones available) allows for high definition of small details and for the creation of very precise forms. *Concerto Grosso* was part of Tom Phillips’ solo exhibition *Tom Phillips – Woven Music*, held at the Galeria Tapeçarias de Portalegre, in Lisbon, in 2002.
artist: Tapestry based on an original painting by Tom Phillips (1937)
Manufactura de Tapeçarias de Portalegre, Portugal
keywords: Manufactura de Tapeçarias de Portalegre; Portalegre tapestries; Tom Phillips; *Concerto Grosso*

en.name: A life insurance policy for military officers offered by the Italian company Istituto Nazionale delle Assicurazioni (INA)
Molar Flask
description: One of the first techniques that were used to shape glass was casting. Molten glass was poured into a mould, producing a solid block or a thick-walled vessel. When cooled, it was then drilled and deeply carved. This small moulded transparent blueish green colour molar flask made using that glass technique. Its body has a narrow shoulder, a cylindrical neck and a flat top. At the midpoint of each side of its body, triangle motifs with diamond-shaped knobs can be identified. It has four pointed feet, one at each corner resembling the roots of a molar tooth, a shape which gave these objects their name, molar flasks. They were most commonly produced as small flasks for valuable cosmetic liquids such as oils or perfume.
keywords: Glass; Moulded; Drilled; Cut; Tulunid; Fatimid

en.name: *Geometrical Elevation of the Building of the Chemical Laboratory* Azulejos
description:
In 1772, under the educational reforms of King Jose I's Prime Minister the Marquis of Pombal, a new statute for Coimbra University emerged. The views of the Marquis and other Enlightenment figures replaced the Aristotelian school of thought previously taught by the Jesuits, who were expelled in 1759. The aim was to modernise teaching by basing it on practical experience and observation.  
In addition to hiring foreign teachers, buying new textbooks and the acquisition of specialised didactic teaching aids, the university replaced the Jesuit-built college with new buildings, one where the former College of the Jesus Society had been and another where the Paço das Escolas (School Hall) once stood.  
The buildings followed the designs of the English Engineer William Elsden, who was also responsible for the construction. The tile panel *Geometrical Elevation of the Building of the Chemical Laboratory* is one of nine panels decorating the Bishop’s palace.  
The building shown here was used by the science department, which had been newly created through Pombaline reform. Today the building hosts the Museum of Science, part of the University of Coimbra.  
The decoration of the Bishop's palace (today the Museu Nacional de Machado de Castro) was commissioned by the Bishop, formerly the Rector of the University. The panels were designed to celebrate the Pombaline reform of the University of Coimbra (1772–1777), and to mark the important role played by D. Francisco de Lemos de Faria Pereira Coutinho, known as “Reformer and Rector of the University of Coimbra”. He was picked out to lead local reform by the Marquis of Pombal.  
The panels were made at Nova Fábrica da Telha Vidrada, a factory founded in 1773 to meet the demands of (*azulejos*) required for the construction and renovation of the University buildings.  
The production of *azulejos* with repetitive patterns, single figures and ornamental and figurative panels are part of the second phase of the Rococo period (or Pombaline style) that occurred after the earthquake of 1755. In Coimbra this period was extended until the end of the century, whereas in Lisbon, *azulejos* from 1790 onwards had been designed in the Neo-classical style leaving the Rococo for the minor panels.  
The frames of bulky shell forms, similar to those present in some paintings of the period, probably belong to Salvador de Sousa Carvalho (1727–1810), who alternated with Manuel da Costa Brioso (1752–1776) as the director of the Nova Fábrica da Telha Vidrada.

The panel is an excellent example of 18th-century quality ceramics produced in Coimbra. It represents a memorial of Pombaline reforms at the University of Coimbra depicting the façade of the Chemical Laboratory.
holder: Museu Nacional de Machado de Castro
place: Nova Fábrica da Telha Vidrada, Rua João Cabreira, Coimbra
keywords: Tile panel; *azulejo*; glazed earthenware; Pombaline reform; University of Coimbra; Enlightenment; tilework; science; education

pt.name: *Painel de azulejo representando o Laboratório Químico da Universidade de Coimbra*
description:
No contexto da reforma do ensino proposta pelo Marquês de Pombal, que pretendia substituir a escolástica aristotélica, seguida pelos Jesuítas, expulsos em 1759, pelo ensino baseado na experiência e na observação prática, procedeu-se à adaptação dos edifícios antigos pertencentes aos Jesuítas mas também à edificação de novos.  
Os projectos são da autoria do engenheiro inglês William Eldsen, responsável pelas obras, e o edifício representado neste painel é o único dos novos departamentos científicos projectados de raiz cujo projecto foi concretizado, albergando actualmente o Museu da Ciência da Universidade de Coimbra.  
O painel representando a *Elevação Geométrica Do Edifício Do Laboratório Chimico* integra um conjunto de nove, encomendados pelo reitor, depois bispo, para decorar o paço episcopal, hoje Museu Nacional de Machado de Castro. A encomenda dos painéis pretendeu comemorar a reforma pombalina da Universidade de Coimbra (1772-1777) e o papel nela desempenhado por D. Francisco de Lemos de Faria Pereira Coutinho, nomeado *Reformador e Reitor da Universidade de Coimbra.*  
Estes painéis terão sido encomendados à Nova Fábrica da Telha Vidrada, propositadamente fundada em Coimbra, em 1773, para satisfazer as encomendas de azulejos, telha e tijolos necessários às obras decorrentes da construção e da renovação dos edifícios universitários.  
A sua produção de azulejos de padrão, figura avulsa, painéis ornamentais e figurativos, integra-se na segunda fase do período rococó ou pombalino, posterior ao terramoto de 1755, que, em Coimbra, se prolongou até ao fim do século. Os concheados volumosos das molduras, similares a outros presentes em encomendas documentadas, remetem a pintura do painel para Salvador de Sousa Carvalho (1727-1810), que, em alternância com Manuel da Costa Brioso (act.1752-1776), dirigiu a Nova Fábrica da Telha Vidrada no período em questão.

O painel representa a qualidade da cerâmica coimbrã do século XVIII, sendo também um memorial da tentativa de reformar o ensino universitário em Portugal à luz do que melhor se fazia nos países mais evoluídos da época.
holder: Museu Nacional de Machado de Castro

en.name: Church of Worship and Basilian Monastery of Máriapócs
names: Greek Catholic Church of Worship and Monastery
description:
The Church of Worship of Máriapócs has a transept and two towers on the west façade; the sanctuary is oriented east. It has three ridged turrets on the roof and the vestry is on the south side.  
The date of construction and the names of the builders are commemorated on a chronosticon above the main gate, above which there is a mosaic representing the Madonna (*Theotokosz*). Beside bishops, many of the church’s patrons are lying in the crypt.  
The main red marble altar was a gift from Count Pál Forgách Bishop of Nagyvárad (Oradea) in 1750; the two preparation altars (in the sanctuary with the main altar); its pulpit (carved and gilded with the statue of St. Michael the archangel above); the painting of the Apostle Paul below the baldachin, with paintings, *Christ and the Samaritan Woman* and the *Seed-Sower*, and the structure of its iconostasis (with a Rococo balustrade and crowned with a cross; the pictures of which date to 1896) are also 18th century.  
There are two side altars: on the north side, the Altar of the Virgin Mary (1943–1944) designed by the Franciscan monks of Pécs, now houses the the miraculous “Weeping Mary of Máriapócs”. The south altar, known as the Altar of the Heart of Jesus, holds a cross relic. The Great Altar of St. Basil is at the same side of the church.  
The sanctuary wall paintings, by Manó Petrasovszky, depict King St. Stephen (Szent István) I offering Hungary to the Virgin Mary with the first martyr St. Stephen, patron saint of the Diocese of Hajdúdorog, and Hungarian saints and pilgrims. The stained-glass windows were made after designs by Petrasovszky between 1944 and 1945. Other wall paintings are by József Boksay (1943).  
The two-storey rectangular Baroque monastery is connected to the church via a suspended corridor.

The Church of Worship in Máriapócs is one of Hungary's most important places of worship particularly for the Greek Catholic community living mostly in eastern Hungary. Up until 1950, the church was maintained by monks from the next-door Basilian Monastery, which was consecrated in 1756. The interior of the church along with the furnishing, much of which dates to the 1780s, has been renovated several times during the 19th and 20th centuries. A copy of the miraculous “Weeping Mary of Máriapócs” was placed in the church in 1707. Since then, this miraculous image has wept twice, attracting numerous other miraculous events to Máriapócs.
artist: László Csigri judge of Máriapócs; Lőrinc Hurta and his family; Count Ferenc Károlyi; Bishop and Apostolic Vicar György Bizáncy Gennadius (d. 1733); István Simon Olsavszky; Gábor Blazsovszky; Bishop Mihály Mánuel Olsavszky (d. 1767); Basilian Monks of Máriapócs; Baroness Zsigmond Palocsay *née* Countess Rozália Gersei Petheő; Count Pál Forgách Bishop of Nagyvárad; István Telekessy Bishop of Eger (1633–1715).

Painters: Mihály Spalinszky (2nd half of the 18th century), Tádé Spalinszky (?–1809), István Papp (brother of the local Greek Catholic pastor), József Boksay; unknown wood carvers from Eperjes; stained glass: Manó Petrasovszky (active middle of the 20th century)
history:
The Church of Worship and Monastery of Máriapócs is a highly significant place for the Greek Catholic Church. Pócs first gained significance in 1696 when in a small, wooden Greek Catholic church in Pócs a group of soldiers witnessed a devotional image, painted in 1676, weeping.  
The original “Weeping Mary of Máriapócs” was commissioned by László Csigri judge of Máriapócs as a votive painting in gratitude for his release from Turkish captivity. István Papp, the younger brother of the local Greek Catholic pastor Dániel Papp, painted the picture but the judge could not pay him on completion. Lőrinc Hurta and his family subsequently purchased the painting and donated it to the church. Following the first act of weeping, Emperor Leopold I had the painting transferred to Vienna, where it was finally placed in St. Stephen's Dome on 11 September 1697, the day the troops of Prince Eugene of Savoy defeated the Turkish armies at Zenta (Senta). The people of Vienna related the triumph to the miraculous power of the “Mary of Pócs”, which Leopold I confirmed in his bull issued to Pócs in 1701.  
Belief in the power of the painting led Leopold I to support the people of Pócs in their fundraising efforts to erect a new church in 1701. Later, Charles VI Emperor gave permission for construction of a church, and the settlement of Greek Catholic Basilian monks in Pócs; Count Ferenc Károlyi donated a large sum of money towards construction as well as his entire Pócs estate.  
Construction began in 1731 at the personal expense of Bishop and Apostolic Vicar György Bizáncy Gennadius, but was halted when the bishop died in 1733.  
István Simon Olsavszky and Gábor Blazsovszky renovated the deteriorating walls before Bishop Mihály Mánuel Olsavszky continued the building programme and consecrated the church in 1749. The foundations were laid and the sanctuary walls erected by 1748.  
In 1749, Bishop Olsavszky received permission from Queen Maria Theresia to establish the Basilian Monastery and the independent bishopric of Munkács (Mukachevo). By 1751, the foundation stone was laid and part of the monastery was complete, so the monks from Munkács (Mukachevo) moved in. The whole building was consecrated in 1753.  
By 1756, the church was complete.  
The Greek Catholic Vicar of Pócs addressed a petition to the emperor requesting that the “Weeping Mary of Máriapócs” be returned. Leopold I promised that a replica would be donated to the church in his written transcript addressed to István Telekessy Bishop of Eger, but in the end, Telekessy commissioned an Austrian artist to paint the copy in 1707, which arrived to Pócs in the same year.  
The paintings of the iconostasis (replaced in 1896) are by Mihály and Tádé Spalinszky (Tádé was also a Basilian monk) of Polish origin between 1785 and 1788. Its gold-plated wooden structure was probably made by a craftsman from Eperjes (Prešov).  
In 1943, the miraculous “Weeping Mary of Máriapócs”, which hung above the Royal Door of the iconostasis, was moved to a side altar in the north wing, then in 1946, on the 250th anniversary of the first weeping, it   was moved to its present location.  
The marble main altar was made in the 18th century; the towers of the church in 1856, and the new bronze gate of the church completed in 1991 for the visit and mass of Pope John Paul II. Pope Pius XII gave the Church of Worship of Máriapócs the title Basilica Minor in 1948.  
The church was cared for by Basilian monks until the dissolution of the order in 1950. The monastery then became a care home, and 10,000 volumes from the library were removed, along with valuable furnishings and items of worship from the church and monastery, which were scattered among various locations. Renovation of the church and monastery began in 2008.

en.name: Tabla
short_description: The *tabla*, also known as the *durbakke*, is a small hand drum very common in traditional Arabic music. It is shaped like a vase, and is covered at the top with goat skin. *Tabla*s are often beautifully decorated, with metal, bone inlay, or paint.

en.name: Monumental staircase
description:
Around 1688 Annibale Ranuzzi commissioned the construction of a monumental staircase for his residential palace in Bologna. The presence of a monumental staircase was a very important element in the baroque ceremonies connected with Bolognese senatorial class political and social activities.  
It is not possible to identify the creator of the staircase. Some believe he must be identified with Giovanni Battista Torri, who paid for the wood model of the work. Others believe he must be identified with the famous Carlo Fontana, who was contacted by the patron together with other architects.  
The work was finished around 1695.
artist: Giovanni Battista Torri (?), Carlo Fontana (?), Ercole Graziani; Filippo Balugani
partner: Musei Civici d’Arte Antica di Bologna in cooperation with the Province of Bologna

it.name: Scalone monumentale
description:
Attorno al 1688 Annibale Ranuzzi decise di far costruire uno scalone monumentale nel suo palazzo di  Bologna. Uno scalone monumentale era un elemento molto importante nelle cerimonie barocche legate alla vita politica e sociale della classe senatoria bolognese.  
Non è possibile identificare il vero ideatore dello scalone. Alcuni lo identificano con  Giovanni Battista Torri, pagato per il modello in legno dell'opera; altri credono che possa essere identificato con il celebre Carlo Fontana, contattato assieme ad altri architetti dai committenti.  
I lavori terminarono attorno al  1695.
artist: Giovanni Battista Torri ?; Carlo Fontana?; Ercole Graziani; Filippo Balugani

en.name: Gradual
description: Some things are made to last forever. One of them is the Gradual from the St. Katharinental Abbey in what is today the canton of Thurgau. The late Gothic hymnal was created in 1312 and was used in the abbey for approximately 500 years. Because it was kept locked away between uses, the Gradual is in excellent condition and the colours of the precious miniatures adorning the pages have lost none of their brilliance. The book was opened only while the nuns sang from it during Mass. They would stand on the choir steps so that they could all read from the book at the same time. The name «Gradual» derives from the Latin word gradus meaning «step». The book is almost half a metre tall to enable all the nuns to read the liturgical chants. This Gradual is one of the most valuable manuscripts in Switzerland. Weighing thirteen kilograms, it is also a true heavyweight of cultural history.
holder: Swiss Confederation, Canton of Thurgau, Gottfried Keller Foundation
place: St. Katharinental Abbey in Diessenhofen, Canton of Thurgau, Switzerland
keywords: Gradual; Illuminated; Manuscript; St. Katharinental Abbey; Parchment; Illuminated; Diessenhofen; Canton of Thurgau; Switzerland

en.name: Ring ‘Potiential Diamond’
description: For his conceptual jewellery, Hans Stofer looks to everyday objects or nature – be it a light bulb, tinfoil, or a piece of coal. He combines them with precious stones or encloses them in wire mesh. There is always a hint of irony and humour about his pieces: his oversized ring made of a piece of coal in wire mesh, for instance, is called “Potential Diamond”. From 1972 to 1976, Hans Stofer was apprenticed as a precision instrument maker. Between 1981 and 1984, he attended the specialist jewellery and instrument-making class at the Zurich School of Design where, in 1985-86, he ran his own workshop before leaving for London in 1987. First, he taught metalwork at Camberwell College of Arts; in September 2006, he was appointed professor and head of Goldsmithing, Silversmithing, Metalwork, and Jewellery at the Royal College of Art.
keywords: Ring; Steel; Coal; Potential Diamond; Hans Stofer

en.name: Large Jar
description: The origins of this object are from Southern Mesopotamia; it’s a complete pottery jar with rolled edges, a short-straight neck, and a globular body. This piece is considered rare, made from fine clay with opaque white glaze and copper, blue, and black manganese splashes on the sides. Archaeologists were able to find many different pottery pieces from different historical periods, and this piece dates back to the 9th century AD. A vessel like this is usually used as a goblet. Typically, it’s a multi-use jar which could have been used for storage and cooking or storing water to keep it cold or to drink from directly.
place: Sohar Fort (al-Batinah North Governorate). Origin: Southern Mesopotamia

en.name: Woman’s court robe (*conteş*)
description: This *seraser* silk was discovered in the latter half of the nineteenth century in a monastery located in the historical region of Oltenia (southwestern Romania), probably at Bistriţa, where it was preserved as an ecclesiastical cope. A hundred years later, following ample restoration undertaken at the Museum, it regained its original form, namely that of a woman’s court robe. It can be assumed that the robe had been donated to the monastery by a boyar’s family, which testifies to the wealth and refinement of the Romanian aristocracy in the sixteenth century, given the fact that *seraser* silk was by far the most precious Ottoman textile, covered ‘from end to end’ with silver and silver-gilt thread. The robe features a design of large palmette garlands, outlined with green silk, each of which encloses a circular motif and a crescent. Between the garlands, circular motifs surrounding a star.
holder: The National Museum of Art of Romania
keywords: Seraser

en.name: Islamic City of Ayla
description:
The modern port resort of Aqaba (the name given to the ancient site in the 7th/13th century)lies in the northeastern corner of the Gulf of Aqaba and is situated within the region of the Great Rift Valley in close proximity to the southern end of Wadi Araba. Subterranean waters run down this *wadi* and enter the sea beneath the modern town; thus fresh water is made available through tapping underground water, a few metres below the surface of the earth. The town is surrounded by desert and high mountains: Sinai to the west, Negev to the north, Hisma and Wadi Ramm to the northeast. When the soldiers of the Great Arab Revolt marched with Lawrence of Arabia from Wadi Ramm to the shores of the Gulf in 1917, Aqaba was a primitive village with a few mud-brick huts and palm groves. Beneath its soil, however, was concealed a long history that stretched back to the 4th millennium BC. The spelling of the name of the site varies in historical sources as Aila, Ailana, Elana, Haila, Ailath, Elath, Ayla and Wayla. A procession of biblical peoples, Edomites, Israelites, Nabataeans, Romans and Arabs inhabited the town. Recent archaeological research has shown that the focus of settlement through the numerous historical periods tended to shift from north to south. The Iron Age II and III (8th-5th centuries BC) site was located at *Tell* al-Kaliefeh, some 500 m. north of the shoreline inside the Jordanian border with Elath.  
The site was identified initially with the biblical Ezion-Geber, where King Solomon built a fleet that sailed to Ophir (Somalia) and returned with 420 talents of gold. Recent excavations cast doubt on this identification and have shown that the site was not founded prior to the 8th century BC. The site, instead, served both commercial and industrial purposes as a trading post for caravans and for smelting copper from Wadi Faynan. In the 1st century BC, Ayla and its region were inhabited by the Nabataeans who raised livestock and also engaged in piracy, attacking merchant ships in the Red Sea. In the same period, merchants from “Ailana” were found in southern Arabia (Yemen) buying frankincense, myrrh and other aromatics. In 106 Trajan, the Roman emperor, annexed the Nabataean kingdom to the newly created *Provincia Arabia*, hence bringing Ayla under direct Roman rule. The *Via Nova Traiana*, which extended from Bostra in southern Syria to Ayla, was completed between 111 and 114. The administrative and military reforms of Diocletian (r. 284-305) partitioned *Provincia Arabia* into two parts, with the southern part (the area east of the Dead Sea) being transferred to *Palestina Tertia*. At the turn of the 3rd century, the *Legio Fretensis* was transferred from Jerusalem to Ayla where it remained at least until the end of the 5th century. During the reign of the Byzantine emperor Leo I (457-474), an Arab chief by the name of “Amorkesos” (Imru’ al-Qays) occupied the island of Iotabe (identified with the Isle de Graye and presently known as Jazirat Fir‘aun or with Tiran at the mouth of the Gulf of Aqaba) from which he had evicted the Byzantine customs officers. Later, Amorkesos visited the emperor in Constantinople, received gifts and was officially recognised as a *phylarch* over *Arabia Petraea*. How this could have happened while the Tenth Legion was still in Ayla is difficult to explain. It is likely, however, that Amorkesos was won over to the Byzantine side and entrusted with the duty of securing the trade routes that led from southern Arabia to the Mediterranean world. Several bishops were attested at Ayla beginning in 325 when its bishop attended the Council of Nicaea. Excavations, begun in 1994, located the Nabataean-Roman City of Ayla at a distance of 2 km. from *Tell* al-Khaliefeh, in the circular area of modern Aqaba. In the course of excavation, a massive mudbrick basilica structure, dated from the early 4th century and identified by the excavators as a church, was discovered. If this identification proves correct, it is then the earliest church building yet known in Jordan and Palestine. In 8/630, Ayla surrendered peacefully to the Prophet Muhammad who guaranteed security for the city’s ships and caravans. In the mid-1st/7th century the Muslims founded a new walled-in settlement, to the south of the Roman-Byzantine town. This town, a rare example of early Islamic urban planning, was discovered in the course of excavations, begun in 1986. The plan of the Islamic city (165 x 140 m.) is laid out in axial streets leading to four gates, the intersection in the middle marked by a tetrapod. This central building was later transformed into a luxurious residence decorated with frescoes. To the northeast of this residence and occupying a large portion of the northeastern quadrant was a mosque. Its plan shows a wide courtyard with colonnades around the sides, the southwestern side being two columns deep. In the centre of this side was a deep niche, the *mihrab*.  
The whole city was surrounded by substantial walls and U-shaped towers. The regular plan follows closely that of Roman legionary camps as those of nearby Udhruh and Lejjun, and may have been inspired by the Byzantine camp in Ayla itself, which has yet to be discovered (see Roman Legionary Camps and City Planning). In addition to serving as a transhipment point for goods, Islamic Ayla benefited from the annual pilgrimage to Mecca and continued to prosper until the end of the 6th/12th century. Soon after, the city suffered from a series of disasters in the form of earthquakes, Bedouin raids and attacks by Crusaders. The process of site migration from north to south continued in the late medieval period when a new settlement around the Mamluk fortress was established about 1 km. to the south of early Islamic Ayla.

es.name: Ciudad islámica de Ayla
description:
El moderno puerto de Aqaba (nombre otorgado al antiguo lugar en el siglo VII/XIII) se encuentra en la esquina noreste del Golfo de Aqaba, dentro de la región del Gran Valle del Rift y en estrecha proximidad con el extremo meridional del Wad Araba. Este wad está recorrido por aguas subterráneas que entran en el mar por debajo de la ciudad moderna, de modo que se obtiene agua potable derivando este acuífero unos pocos metros por debajo de la superficie del suelo. La ciudad está rodeada por el desierto y por altas montañas: el Sinaí al oeste, el Negveb al norte y el Hisma y el Wad Ramm al noreste.  
Cuando los soldados de la Gran Revuelta Árabe avanzaron con Lawrence de Arabia desde el Wad Ramm hasta las orillas del Golfo en 1917, Aqaba era un pueblo primitivo con unas pocas casas de tierra y algunas palmeras. Bajo su suelo, sin embargo, se ocultaba una larga historia que se remontaba al milenio IV a. C. El nombre del lugar aparece bajo las más diversas formas según las fuentes históricas: Aila, Ailana, Elana, Haila, Ailath, Elath, Ayla y Wayla. Una verdadera procesión de pueblos bíblicos habitó la ciudad: edomitas, israelitas, nabateos, romanos y árabes. Las excavaciones arqueológicas más recientes han revelado que el foco de asentamiento ha tendido a desplazarse de norte a sur, a través de los diversos periodos históricos. Así, en las Edades del Hierro II y III (siglos VIII-V a. C.), el emplazamiento estaba localizado en el *tell* al-Kaliefe, unos 500 m al norte de la línea de costa y hacia el interior de la frontera jordana con Elat.  
En un principio se identificó el lugar con la bíblica Esyón-Gvéber, donde el rey Salomón construyó una flota que zarpó hacia Ofir (Somalia) y regresó con 420 talentos de oro. Recientes excavaciones han arrojado dudas sobre esta identificación, al demostrar que no fue fundado antes del siglo VIII a.C. En cambio, parece claro que el lugar sirvió para fines a la vez comerciales, como estación de caravanas, e industriales, como centro de fundición del cobre extraído del Wad Faynan. En el siglo I a.C., Ayla y su región estaban habitadas por los nabateos, quienes, aparte de criar ganado, se dedicaban a ejercer la piratería contra los barcos mercantes del Mar Rojo. En el mismo periodo, había mercaderes de Ayla en Arabia del Sur (Yemen), donde compraban incienso, mirra y otros productos aromáticos. En el año 106, el emperador romano Trajano anexionó el reino nabateo a la recién creada *Provincia Arabia*, de modo que Ayla quedó sometida directamente a la jurisdicción romana. Entre el 111 y el 114 se completó la *Vía Nova Traiana*, que se extendía desde Bostra, en el sur de Siria, hasta Ayla. Las reformas administrativas y militares de Diocleciano (r. 284-305) dividieron la *Provincia Arabia* en dos partes, y la parte sur (la zona al este del Mar Muerto) fue transferida a la *Palestina Tertia*. A principios del siglo III, la *Legio Fretensis* fue trasladada de Jerusalén a Ayla, donde permaneció estacionada al menos hasta finales del siglo V. Durante el reinado del emperador bizantino Leo I (457-474), un jefe árabe de nombre Amorkesos (Imru’ al-Qays) ocupó la isla de Iotabe (identificada con la isla de Graye, conocida actualmente como Yazira Fir‘awn, o con Tiran, situada en la boca del Golfo de Aqaba), de la que expulsó a los funcionarios de aduanas bizantinos. A continuación, Amorkesos visitó al emperador en Constantinopla, recibió presentes y fue reconocido como *filarca* de *Arabia Petraea*. El que esto pudiera ocurrir hallándose la Décima Legión estacionada en Ayla es algo difícil de explicar. Es probable, sin embargo, que se convenciera a Amorkesos de ponerse de parte de los bizantinos y que se le confiara la responsabilidad de garantizar la navegación comercial entre el sur de Arabia y el mundo mediterráneo. Existen pruebas de que, a principios del 325, había varios obispos en Ayla cuando su obispo asistió al Concilio de Nicea. Las excavaciones iniciadas en 1994 localizaron la ciudad nabateo-romana de Ayla a una distancia de 2 km del *Tell* al-Jaliefe, dentro del radio de la actual Aqaba. En el transcurso de la excavación, se descubrió una construcción basilical de grandes dimensiones, fechada a principios del siglo IV e identificada por los arqueólogos como una iglesia. Si esta identificación demuestra ser acertada, se trataría del edificio eclesiástico más antiguo hallado hasta el momento en Jordania y Palestina. En el año 8/630, Ayla se rindió pacíficamente al Profeta Muhammad, quien garantizó la seguridad de los barcos y caravanas de la ciudad. A mediados del siglo I/VII, los musulmanes fundaron un nuevo asentamiento amurallado al sur de la ciudad romano-bizantina. Esta nueva ciudad, un ejemplo singular de planificación urbana islámica de primera hora, fue descubierta en el curso de las excavaciones iniciadas en 1986. La planta de la ciudad islámica (165 x 140 m) se ordena en torno a dos ejes que conducen a las cuatro puertas, y en la intersección de ambos se encuentra un *tetrapilon* o edificio con cuatro entradas.  
Este edificio central fue reconvertido posteriormente en una lujosa residencia, decorada con frescos. Hacia el noreste de esta residencia y ocupando una gran porción del cuadrante nororiental había una mezquita. Su planta muestra un amplio patio rodeado por galerías de columnas, y la del lado suroeste es de doble columnata. En el centro de este lado se abría un nicho profundo, el *mihrab*. Toda la ciudad estaba rodeada de potentes murallas y torres en forma de U. La planta regular responde estrechamente al modelo de los campamentos romanos de legionarios como los de las cercanas Udhruh y Leyyun, y pudo haberse inspirado en el campamento bizantino de la propia Ayla, que aún está por descubrir (ref. Campamentos romanos de legionarios y planificación urbana). Además de servir como punto de transbordo de mercancías, la Ayla islámica se beneficiaba de la peregrinación anual a La Meca y siguió prosperando hasta finales del siglo VI/XII. Poco después, sin embargo, la ciudad sufrió una serie de desastres en forma de terremotos, incursiones beduinas y ataques de los cruzados. El proceso de desplazamiento del lugar desde el norte hacia el sur continuó a lo largo del periodo medieval tardío, cuando se estableció un nuevo asentamiento en torno a la fortaleza mameluca, a una distancia aproximada de 1 km al sur de la primera Ayla islámica.

fr.name: La ville islamique d’Ayla
description:
Le port moderne d’Aqaba (ce sera le nom du site à partir du VIIe/XIIIe siècle) est situé à l’extrémité nord-est du golfe d’Aqaba, dans la région de la vallée du Grand Rift, au sud de Oued Araba. Les eaux souterraines qui coulent sous ce *oued* vont se jeter en mer en dessous de la ville moderne. Elles fournissent l’eau potable, qui est simplement captée à quelques mètres sous la surface du sol. La ville est cernée par le désert et les montagnes: le Sinaï à l’ouest, le Néguev au nord, le Hisma et le Oued Ramm au nord-est.  
Quand, en 1917, les soldats de la grande révolte arabe marchent avec Lawrence d’Arabie de Oued Ramm jusqu’aux rives du golfe, Aqaba est encore un village primitif avec quelques huttes en briques crues et des palmeraies. Mais dans son sous-sol se trouve cachée une histoire qui remonte au quatrième millénaire av. J.-C. Le nom du site varie en fonction des sources historiques locales: Aila, Ailana, Elana, Haila, Ailath, Elath, Ayla et Wayla. La ville a vu se succéder les peuples bibliques: Édomites, Israélites, Nabatéens, Romains et Arabes. Des recherches archéologiques récentes ont bien établi que les populations de la région tendent à se déplacer du nord au sud au cours de l’histoire. Ainsi, le *Tell* al-Kaliefeh, qui correspond au peuplement du deuxième au troisième âge du fer (VIIIe-Ve siècle av. J.-C.), est-il situé à 500 m au nord de la côte, à l’intérieur de la frontière entre la Jordanie et Eilat.  
On a d’abord cru qu’Ayla était l’Ezion- Geber biblique, où le roi Salomon aurait fait construire une flotte qui appareille pour Ophir (Somalie) et en revient chargée de 420 talents d’or. Les fouilles récentes récusent cette hypothèse et tendent à prouver que la fondation du site ne remonte pas au-delà du VIIIe siècle av. J.-C. Par contre, il sera très tôt un centre de commerce et d’industrie, une halte commerciale pour les caravanes, et on y fond le cuivre de Oued Faynan. Au Ier siècle av. J.-C., Ayla et sa région sont habitées par les Nabatéens, qui y élèvent du bétail et s’adonnent quelque peu à la piraterie aux dépens des navires marchands de la mer Rouge. À cette époque, on trouve des marchands en provenance “d’Ailana” jusqu’en Arabie du sud (Yémen), où ils vont acheter de l’encens, de la myrrhe et d’autres aromates. En 106, l’empereur romain Trajan annexe le royaume nabatéen à la *Provincia Arabia*, nouvellement créée, mettant ainsi Ayla sous l’autorité directe de Rome. La *Via Nova Traiana*, qui va de Bostra en Syrie du sud à Ayla, sera terminée entre 111 et 114. Avec les réformes administratives et militaires de Dioclétien (r. 284-305), la *Provincia Arabia* est divisée en deux parties; sa partie sud (la région à l’est de la mer Morte) étant rattachée à la *Palestina Tertia*. Au début du IIIe siècle, la *Legio Fretensis* est déplacée de Jérusalem à Ayla, où elle va rester jusqu’à la fin du Ve siècle. Pendant le règne de l’empereur byzantin Léon Ier (457-474), un chef arabe nommé Amorkesos (Imrou al-Qays) occupe l’île d’Iotabe (identifiée soit comme l’île de Graye –connue aujourd’hui sous le nom de Jazirat Fir‘aoun– soit comme Tiran, à l’embouchure du golfe d’Aqaba). Il en expulse les officiers des douanes byzantines. Un peu plus tard, Amorkesos se rend à Constantinople où l’empereur lui offre des présents et le nomme *phylarque d’Arabia Petraea*. On s’explique mal cette délégation de pouvoirs, alors que la Xe Légion romaine est toujours cantonnée à Ayla. Mais il est probable qu’Amorkesos s’est rangé du côté des Byzantins et qu’on lui a confié la charge d’assurer la sécurité des routes commerciales du sud de l’Arabie au monde méditerranéen. À partir de 335, date à laquelle l’évêque d’Ayla participe au concile de Nicée, les évêques vont se succéder. Grâce à des fouilles commencées en 1994, on a pu découvrir la cité nabatéenne et romaine d’Ayla qui se trouvait à 2 km du *Tell* al- Khaliefeh, dans la zone périphérique de la ville moderne. Au cours des fouilles, un grand ensemble basilical en brique crue a été mis au jour. Les chercheurs l’ont identifié comme étant une église construite au début du IVe siècle. Si cette attribution était confirmée, il s’agirait de la plus ancienne église connue de Jordanie et de Palestine. En 8/630, Ayla se soumet sans combat au prophète Muhammad, qui garantit à la ville la sécurité pour ses bateaux et ses caravanes. Au milieu du Ier/VIIe siècle, les musulmans vont fonder une nouvelle ville avec son enceinte, au sud de la ville romaine et byzantine. Cette cité, découverte au cours des fouilles entreprises à partir de 1986, est un des rares témoignages de l’organisation urbaine du début de l’islam. La cité islamique (165 m sur 140 m) se développe autour de deux axes perpendiculaires débouchant aux quatre portes. Au centre, à leur intersection, est érigé un tétrapyle. Cet édifice central sera transformé plus tard en une luxueuse résidence décorée de fresques. La mosquée occupe une grande partie du secteur nord-est. Sa large cour centrale était entourée de colonnades, avec une double colonnade au sudouest; au centre de ce côté se trouvait une niche profonde, le *mihrab*. Toute la ville est entourée d’une solide muraille avec des tours en forme de U. Son plan régulier est une reproduction fidèle de celui des camps romains, exactement comme à Edroh et à Lejjoun, tout proches. Cependant, il n’est pas exclu qu’il ait été repris du modèle du camp byzantin d’Ayla même, mais les recherches n’ont toujours pas permis de redécouvrir ce camp. La ville va continuer de prospérer jusqu’à la fin du VIe/XIIe siècle, essentiellement grâce à sa situation sur le chemin du pèlerinage annuel de La Mecque et à son rôle de port de transbordement de marchandises. Mais elle subit à cette époque une série de désastres: tremblements de terre, razzias de Bédouins, attaques des croisés. Le proprocessus de migration du site, du nord vers le sud, se confirme jusqu’au bas Moyen Âge où une nouvelle agglomération sera établie autour de la forteresse mamelouke, à environ 1 km au sud de la première Ayla islamique.

en.name: Costume for Cleopatra in the Ballets Russes production of *Cléopâtre*, 1918
short_description: The sets and many costumes for the 1909 *Cleopatre* were destroyed in a fire during the company’s 1917 South American tour, so painter Sonia Delaunay was commissioned to fashion new costumes for the principals. The artist’s palette of brilliant color, graphic design, and combination of textures resulted in costumes markedly different from the originals. Cleopatra’s luminous dress, reflecting the abstract forms in Sonia Delaunay’s paintings, as well as aspects of fashionable dress of the period, remains one of her most significant creations for the theatre.
