en.name: *Silsile-name* ('Chain book' or Genealogy)
description: This *Silsile-name*, meaning chain book or genealogy, was completed by the scribe and painter Huseyin in 1104 AH / 1692 AD in Istanbul, according to the colophon. It was acquired in Turkish Ottoman territory soon after by Count Luigi Ferdinando Marsili (died 1730 AD) and listed in the printed catalogue of his personal library in 1702, his coat of arms appearing as embossed stamps on two folios (fol. 2a, 36a). However, it was acquired by the Austrian National Library in the early 18th century and restored in 1921, as an inscription on fol. 1a indicates. Family trees and their graphical representation in the form of linked circular medallions - hence the name - have had a long tradition in Islam since the early 14th century. The literary form of such genealogies referring to ancestors, however, originated under Suleyman the Magnificent in the 16th century. Starting with Adam and Eve, these manuscripts develop from the great biblical prophets and legendary rulers of Iran to the most important Arabic, Mongol, Persian, and Turkish dynasties, concluding with the contemporaneous Ottoman rulers. The genealogies were often conceived as scrolls, and here this appearance is even reflected in book form with the connecting lines between profiles continuing horizontally across the page from right to left. These family trees are of great cultural and art-historical interest as they exist in large numbers and reveal manifold artistic source material that even draw on European models. Moreover, their political objective to legitimise the Ottoman rule based on past history reveals the manner of self-representation of Ottomans as well as their visual evaluation regarding specific ancestral figures. As these genealogies are traced back to pagan or biblical times, the names of saints become part of a dynastic claim of legitimacy and historical awareness. Genealogies with paintings in medallion form can be divided into two categories: one creating manuscripts of the highest quality in an Istanbul studio working for the court, and the other one of slightly lower quality produced by workshops of the Mevleviye Order, which were either located in Istanbul or in various places in the Ottoman province such as Baghdad at the turn of the 16th and 17th centuries. This particular copy was likely made by a workshop close to the court, stylistically relating to a similar manuscript located in Warsaw, Poland (Biblioteka Narodowa, BOZ 183). Its 36 folios are in horizontal landscape format, with inscriptions accompanying the tondo-shaped miniatures that were carefully crafted by the otherwise unknown painter Huseyin in the Ottoman court style from the end of the 17th century. Depending on the importance of the person depicted, the diameter of the circular medallions varies; moreover, the flame aureoles of saintly figures stand out amongst their mortal counterparts. While the biblical ancestors and the Turkish tribal fathers are depicted in small roundels, the medallions increase in size starting with the Prophet Muhammad, his successors, the Abbasid caliphs, and the Mongol rulers, reaching its biggest form in the depiction of the first Ottoman sultan (fol. 30a). The great variety of the elaborate robes and of the headdresses adorned with numerous decorative elements point to the luxury of the commission. European painting conventions are reflected in the shading, the colour scape, and the modelling of the skin, masterfully combined with Ottoman artistic traditions. However, while the prophets and past rulers are shown as ideal portraits following traditional models in a uniform scheme, the depictions of later Ottoman sultans have individual, portrait-like features. This reveals that the painter may have had access to portrait miniatures from the sultan’s collection at court.
keywords: Adam; Eve; genealogy; Mehmet; medaillon; Muhammad; painting; prophet; Suleyman; sultan; turban; Zahhak

ar.name: قطعة من قماش.
description:
إن هذه القطعة ذات تلوين متنوع جداً ومتناسق ورائق. يغلب على الأرضية بشكل عام اللونان الكستنائي والأحمر، وتزينها شرائط مشكلة من عناصر زخرفية هندسية ومكونة بشكل رئيسي من الرصيعات. تتناوب هذه الأخيرة مع زخارف نباتية مكونة من زخارف غصينات تتفتح منها أوراق جد مبسطة. في حين، تصور الزخرفة الحيوانية عصافير منمنمة جداً ولا يمكن التعرف عليها.  
وعموماً، فإن العناصر الزخرفية ملونة بالأزرق المركب أساساً من شجرة النيلة (الأنديكو)، وبالأصفر الذي مصدر لونه من الزعفران، وباللون الأحمر المركب أساساً من لون دودة القز أو من مادة البريق الصيني، إلى جانب اللون الأخضر الكستنائي وغيرها من الألوان. التقنية المستخدمة هي تقنية التوشية التي خلدها النساجون الأقباط منذ عدة قرون. ويبدو أن مصدر هذه القطعة من أعالي مصر التي اشتهرت منذ القدم بنسج الصوف.

قطعة من قماش كثيرة التلوين حيث تشترك الأشكال الهندسية والزخارف النباتية. تقنيات النسج والأشكال الزخرفية مشابهة لتلك التي تم العثور عليها على بعض التيرازات المصرية التي ترجع إلى الفترة الطولونية. ويبدو أن هذه القطعة قد حُصل عليها من مصر العليا، التي اشتهرت منذ العهد القديم بحياكة الصوف.
keywords: تيراز؛ قماش؛ زخرفة هندسية ؛ زخرفة نباتية؛ زخرفة تصويرية.

en.name: Cloth fragment.
description:
The many different colours of the fragment combine serenely and harmoniously. The mainly red of beige background is decorated with strips containing geometric motifs (mostly medallions) alternating with floral patterns (stylised scrolled stalks and leaves) and highly stylised birds.  
The motifs are mainly in blue (indigo), yellow (saffron), and red (cochineal dye or lacquer). Beige-green and other colours accompany these.  
The cloth is woven in the manner used by Coptic weavers over several centuries. This fragment appears to come from high Egypt, well-known since ancient times for its weaving of wool.

Fragment of a heavily dyed fabric combining geometric and plant motifs. The needlework techniques and decorative motifs are similar to those found in Egyptian *tiraz* from the Tulunid era. This fragment is thought to come from Upper Egypt, famed since Antiquity for its wool weaving.
keywords: Tiraz; geometric decoration; figurative decoration; textile

es.name: Fragmento de tejido.
description:
Este fragmento presenta una amplia, armoniosa y serena gama cromática. El fondo, donde predominan los tonos beige y rojo, está ornamentado con franjas de motivos geométricos compuestos, esencialmente, por medallones que alternan con ornamentos florales, sobre todo follajes de los que surgen hojas muy estilizadas. El diseño zoomórfico está representado por unos pájaros muy estilizados e irreconocibles.  
Los motivos están teñidos predominantemente en tres colores: azul, a base de índigo; amarillo, cuyo tinte procede del azafrán; rojo, a base de tintura de cochinilla o de laca. El verde, el beige y otros colores completan la composición.  
En la fabricación se utilizó la técnica de la confección mantenida desde varios siglos antes por los tejedores coptos. Este fragmento de tela pudiera tener su origen en el Alto Egipto, afamado, desde la Antigüedad, por el tejido de la lana.

Fragmento de un tejido muy colorido, donde alternan motivos geométricos y ornamentos vegetales. Las técnicas de confección y los motivos decorativos se asemejan a los hallados en unos *tiraz* egipcios del período tuluní. Este fragmento de tela pudiera tener su origen en el Alto Egipto, afamado, desde la Antigüedad, por el tejido de la lana.
dates: Siglo III de la Hégira / IX d. C.
keywords: Tiraz; decoración geométrica; decoración figurativa

fr.name: Fragment de tissu.
description: Le fragment est d'une coloration très variée, harmonieuse et sereine. La plate-forme, généralement de couleur beige ou rouge, est ornée de bandes à motifs géométriques formés essentiellement de médaillons qui alternent avec des décors végétaux, composés de rinceaux d'où émanent des feuillets très stylisés. Le décor animalier est représenté par des oiseaux très stylisés et méconnaissables. Généralement, les motifs sont colorés de bleu, à base d'indigo, de jaune dont la teinte provient du safran, du rouge à base de teinte de cochenille ou de laque, à côté du vert beige et d'autres. La technique utilisée est celle de la tapisserie perpétuée par les tisserands coptes depuis plusieurs siècles. Ce fragment semble provenir de la haute égypte réputée depuis l'antiquité pour le tissage de la laine.

Fragment d'un tissu fortement coloré où les motifs géométriques s'associent aux décors végétaux. Les techniques de tapisserie et les motifs décoratifs sont analogues à ceux retrouvés sur des *tiraz* égyptiens de l'époque toulounide. Ce fragment semble provenir de Haute égypte, réputée depuis l'Antiquité pour le tissage de la laine.
dates: IIIe siècle de l’Hégire (IXe siècle J.-C.).
keywords: Tiraz; décoration géométrique; décoration figurative
partner: Musée des Arts islamiques de Monastir

en.name: Khan al-‘Arus
description:
It is impossible to miss this attractive building, which survives as a very important example of a medieval *caravanserai*. The 6th-/12th-century traveller Ibn Jubayr, as well as other visitors of the 13th/19th century, noted the existence of an inscription panel located above the entrance lintel which has since gone missing. A record exists of the following words:  
*“The construction of this blessed hotel was ordered by our leader al-Malik al-Nasir, the righteousness of the world and the religion, the Sultan of Islam and all Muslims, Abu al-Muzaffar Yusuf bin Ayyub, the reviver of the nation of the prince of the faithful, and that is in the year 577.”*  
The date corresponds to AD 1181, the patron is Salah al-Din, and the style of this building is very much like a fortress – clear evidence of the militarization of Islamic architecture during this period. Ibn Jubair (d. 614/1217) passed by this building less than two years after its construction and calls it “Khan al-Sultan” in reference to its ruling patron. In his travel memoirs, he describes it as “… the zenith of strength and handsomeness, with iron doors after the fashion in the building of khanat in this part of the world …”, and he refers to many similar constructions along the travel-routes, as beautiful and well fortified.  
The khan is nearly  
square; all four of its sides are about 40 m long. The entry, framed by two arches, is on the southern wall. It leads into a corridor that has a staircase on the left-hand side leading to the roof.  
The open courtyard with its central water basin is about 29.55 m x 24.75 m, is surrounded by arched porticos, known in Arabic as *riwaq*.  
The upper storey consists of a single  
room built on top of the entrance as a protective measure. This room is rectangular, 6.40 m x 3.85 m, with a barrel-vaulted roof. It has two windows, used for surveillance, one overlooking the  
courtyard and the other overlooking the entrance. Originally endowed with merlons and arrow loops on all sides the room has two doors to facilitate access to the roof.

en.name: *Pulpit on the Platform of the Mosque of Omar*
short_description: This image, etched after having been originally drawn by Samuel Prout after a sketch made on the spot by F. Catherwood, shows the ‘Minbar al-Saif’ of the Al-Aqsa mosque precinct, on the southern side of the Dome of the Rock in Jerusalem, right next to the south gateway to its raised platform.  Originally built by Saladin in the 12th century, it was later restored in the 14th century by Burhan al-Din, whose name is also used to refer to the structure.  It forms an important part of the Haram al-Sharif revered by Muslims. The third-most sacred site in Islam, it marks Islam’s first qibla and the spot from which the Prophet undertook his night journey to heaven. The image was first published in 'Landscape Illustrations of the Bible', consisting of Views of the most remarkable places mentioned in the Old and New Testaments. From original sketches taken on the spot and engraved by W. And E. Finden. With descriptiions by the Rev. Rhomas Hartwell Horne, B.D. In 2 Vols, Vol 1, John Murray and Charles Tilt, London 1836.
holder: Sharjah Art Museum / Sharjah Museums Department
keywords: Minbar al-Saif; al-Aqsa Mosque; Dome of the Rock; Haram al-Sharif; Jerusalem; Saladin; Burhan al-Din

en.name: Stag aquamanile
description:
This aquamanile in the shape of a standing stag illustrates that animal motifs were considered suitable for handwashing vessels in Fatimid Egypt in the 10th and 11th century. The object is characterized by a cup-shaped opening, through which it can be filled with water, and spouts located in the snout and nostrils. The front of the snout is closed, instead water flows out from openings located on either side of the mouth. The handle is shaped like a slender and highly stylized quadruped standing on the stag’s back; it leans its front legs against the neck, where the cup is positioned, and stretches its head upwards, as if trying to reach the water source. Notably, aside from several folds in its skin, the stag’s body is not ornamented. This makes it one of the few Fatimid aquamaniles, and indeed one of the few Islamic animal figures, with an unadorned body surface.  
  
The work is primarily compared with the only other known stag aquamanile, now located in Munich (Museum Five Continents, Inv.-Nr. 26-N-1). The motif of the drinking stag was transmitted into Islamic culture through the translations of the Physiologus, a didactic Christian text written in Greek by an unknown author in Alexandria during the 2nd century AD. It describes animals and fantastic creatures and provides accompanying moral commentary. Thus, both Christian and Islamic stag iconography refer back to the same source. In addition to stags and deer, there are other aquamanilia surviving today that originate from regions under the control of the Sasanian as well as the Umayyad, Abbasid, and Fatimid rule. These can be dated between the 6th/7th century and the early 13th century.  
  
The handle and the spout reveal the function of the object; it allowed for the pouring of two streams of water onto two outstretched hands, so they may be washed. Its material made it unsuitable for holding wine and its large size prevented its use as a drinking vessel. Aquamanilia were most likely used in a courtly context for lavish festivities and private events with wine, singing, riddles, games, and friendly competition between poets. This would also explain the iconography of the aquamanilia, which refers to courtly culture. The imagery of the falcon, for example, was usually intended as a representation of sovereign power and a sign of authority.
holder: Museo e Real Bosco di Capodimonte
place: Santangelo Collection, until 1967 in the Archaeological Museum, subsequently in the National Museum of Capodimonte
keywords: Aquamanile, stag, Fatimid, Egypt, Museo e Real Bosco di Capodimonte
tags: Aquamanile, stag, Fatimid, Egypt, Museo e Real Bosco di Capodimonte
partner: MIC | Museo e Real Bosco di Capodimonte

en.name: Villa Zanchini-Garagnani
description:
The villa is formed by the superimposition of eighteenth-century elements on the original nucleus of the building, once crowned by a small covered terrace (altana) on the top of the roof.  
The scenographic solution of the front with lateral arcades forms an aedicule that covers the curved stairs. This elegant feature was used as an entrance for coaches. The two hexagonal aedicules can be dated to the seventeenth-century and were attributed to the local architect Giovan Giacomo Monti. The curved flight of stairs is similar to solutions employed in Bolognese buildings of the same age, so that this part of the villa can be considered the first to be built.  
Distributed around the central hall are several different rooms. The elegant and measured interiors can be dated to the latest transformation that involved the building, at the end of the nineteenth-century. The rooms are decorated with stucco in Neo-classic style and in some case they still hold their original “Venetian style” floors.

The originality of this villa is the scenographic structure of its front formed by different arcades that hide and, at he same time, introduce to the two-curved stair flights, bringing to the first floor.  
The dynamism and elegance of the space and the changing views that can be enjoyed through the arcades and columns from the small loggia on the top of the stairs, are typical of the local baroque architecture that owns most of its devices to the theatre tradition.
dates: 1679; 1786; 1881 restoration of the building and decoration of the interiors in Neo-classic style
artist: Edoardo Zanchini; Vincenzo Zambeccari; Raffaele Garagnani
history:
Not much is known about this villa and its architect remains unidentified. A Latin inscription, still visible on the building, tells us that it was built in 1679 by Edoardo Zanchini. At the beginning of the eighteenth-century the villa passed to the Zambeccari family and in 1786 it was restyled and enlarged by Marquis Vincenzo Zambeccari. In 1878 it was sold in a public auction to Raffaele Garagnani who promoted some restoration work and took the villa back to its original splendour.  
The whole building was seriously damaged during the Second World War. The private chapel next to the villa was destroyed and the roof was completely rebuilt by the Garagnani Family. They still own the villa and the surrounding land with vineyards and orchards.
keywords: Residential architecture; Scenography; Villa; Monumental staircase; Loggia
partner: Musei Civici d’Arte Antica di Bologna in cooperation with the Province of Bologna

it.name: Villa Zanchini-Garagani
description:
La villa è formata da una sovrapposizione di elementi del XVIII secolo su un nucleo originario un tempo coronato da una piccola terrazza coperta (altana) posta al vertice del tetto.  
La scenografica soluzione della fronte con portici laterali che formano un'edicola che copre le scale curve è elegante ed era utilizzata per le carrozze. Le due edicole esagonali possono essere datate al XVII secolo e sono attribuite all'architetto locale Gian Giacomo Monti. Anche le rampe di scale curve richiamano soluzioni analoghe utilizzate in edifici bolognesi dello stesso periodo, tanto che si ritiene che questa parte della villa sia stata costruita per prima.  
Attorno al salone centrale sono distribuite le diverse stanze. Gli interni, eleganti e equilibrati, si possono dare all'ultima trasformazione che ha riguardato l'edificio, alla fine del XIX secolo. Le stanze sono decorate in stucco in stile neoclassico e in alcuni casi mantengono ancora i loro pavimenti a palladiana.

L'originalità di questa villa è la struttura scenografica della sua facciata, costituita da diversi portici che nascondono e allo stesso tempo introducono le due rampe di scale curve che conducono al primo piano.  
Il dinamismo e l'eleganza della spazio e le vedute che cambiano e si apprezzano attraverso le arcate e le colonne della piccola loggia al vertice delle scale, sono tipiche della architettura barocca locale che deve molti dei suoi effetti alla tradizione della scenografia teatrale.
dates: 1679; 1786; 1881 restauro dell'edificio e decorazione dell'interno in stile neoclassico
artist: Edoardo Zanchini; Vincenzo Zambeccari; Raffaele Garagnani
history:
Non si sa molto di questa villa e finora non è stato possibile individuarne l'autore. Un'iscrizione latina ancora visibile sull'edificio ci dice che fu costruita nel 1679 da Edoardo Zanchini; all'inizio del XVIII secolo la villa passò alla famiglia Zambeccari e nel 1786 fu ristrutturata e ampliata dal marchese Vincenzo Zambeccari. Nel 1878 venne venduta all'asta a Raffaele Garagnani, che promosse alcuni lavori di restauro e la riportò al suo primitivo splendore.  
L'intero edificio fu gravemente danneggiato durante la Seconda Guerra Mondiale: la cappella privata vicino alla villa fu distrutta e il tetto fu interamente ricostruito dalla famiglia Garagnani, che è l'attuale proprietaria della villa e del terreno circostante con I suoi vigneti e frutteti.
keywords: Architettura residenziale; scenografia; Villa; scalone monumentale; Loggia;

en.name: Sidi Brahim Mosque
description:
The mosque inherited the name of the tomb of Sheikh Sidi Brahim, next to which it was built. It is located in one of the oldest cemeteries of the valley, below the southern slope of the *ksar* (fortified castle) of el-Ateuf. It is a funerary mosque for families of the same lineage, and includes a small, round, partly-underground room formerly used for teaching the Koran.  
  
Directly above this room, at mid-height, is a room used by the mosque’s sheikh, who spent most of his time there. These two spaces are accessible from the prayer room, whose form and spatial proportions inspired several eminent architects, in particular Le Corbusier in his design for the Ronchamp Chapel in France.  
  
The mosque opens onto the interior prayer area or *sahn* via arcades of various dimensions, and onto the cemetery by a large openwork wall adjacent to the tomb of Sidi Brahim.  
  
This monument was built with stone bound with lime mortar for load-bearing walls and pillars; palm tree trunks for beams and girders; and palm trees as temporary framework for arches, which gave each arch a unique shape. The whole is covered with lime mortar plaster applied variously by hand, trowel, with palm-leaf clusters and by other methods. The building is periodically whitewashed, which protects it from the effects of bad weather and maintains its bright whiteness in contrast to the ochre environment.

ar.name: ثوب امرأة ( إنتاري)
description: المعطف الخارجي الطويل حتى الأرض  له فتحة عنق بيضوية ودقة الصنعة تشير لإنتاج مخصص للبلاط. والأكمام هي  زائدة الطول ويوجد شق من الأسفل ومبطن بقماش علوي مطرز. والثوب يزرّ في الوسط  على نحو كثير أو قليل مع الخصر بواسطة اثني عشر زرا مزخرفة وتطريز الطارة يشمل لفات مزهرة وحزم من الأزهار وأيضا أشكال منممنة معمارية وطيور.
dates: القرن الثامن عشر - القرن التاسع عشر
partner: المتحف التمساوي للفنون التطبيقية / الفنون المعاصرة

de.name: Frauenkleid (*entari*)
description: Die bodenlange, unten ausgestellte Überjacke verfügt über einen tiefen, spitzovalen Brustausschnitt. Die Feinheit der Ausführung verweist auf eine Produktion im höfischen Kontext. Die Ärmel weisen eine Überlänge auf, sind im unteren Teil geschlitzt und mit besticktem Oberstoff gefüttert. Das Kleid wird mittig, etwa bis zur Taille durch zwölf Posamentenknöpfe geschlossen. Die Tambourstickerei weist neben Blütenranken und Blumengebinden kleine Architekturdarstellungen und Vögel auf.
holder: MAK – Österreichisches Museum für angewandte Kunst / Gegenwartskunst
partner: MAK – Österreichisches Museum für angewandte Kunst

en.name: Woman’s dress (*entari*)
description: The floor-length overcoat, flaring below, has a low, lancet-oval décolleté. The fineness of workmanship indicates a production in the context of the Court. The sleeves are overlong, slit below and lined with embroidered top fabric. The dress is fastened in the middle more or less to the waist with twelve ornamentally trimmed buttons. The tambour embroidery includes floral scrolls and bunches of flowers as well as miniature architectural motifs and birds.
type: Ottoman dress, silk, cotton, embroidery, garment
keywords: women; costume; Ottoman costume; dress; workshop; Floral decoration
partner: MAK – Austrian Museum of Applied Arts / Contemporary Art

ar.name: البرج الشمالي.
description:
بني هذا الصرح الضخم من الطابية على تصميم مربع الشكل تقريباً، وشيد برج في كل زاوية من زواياه الأربعة، وتحيط أروقة بهيكل البناء من الداخل. شكلت السقوف من قبب مكورة على شكل قوس دائرة. وتحتفظ المعلمة ببعض الزخارف البسيطة، لكنها غطيت جزئياً بعد العديد من عمليات الترميم، ويصعب تأريخها لعدم توفر الوثائق. كما يفضي سلم عريض يتكون من أكثر من 60 درجة إلى السطح.  
يستخدم البرج حالياً كمتحف للأسلحة.

يقع البرج الشمالي (حاليا متحف الأسلحة) فوق تل شمال مدينة فاس العتيقة، خارج الأسوار؛ وهو عبارة عن موقع محصن شُيد خلال القرن 16 من طرف السلطان السعدي، أحمد المنصور الذهبي. استُعملت هذه البناية العسكرية الضخمة المبنية بالطابية والمحاطة بأربعة أبراج، لحماية مدينة فاس من الحصارات المتعددة للقبائل والمطالبين بالعرش.  
تحيطُ بداخل البناية ممرات؛ بينما غُطيت الأسقفُ بقبوات مكورة على شكل قوس دائرة، مع زخارف بسيطة؛ غُطيت جزئيا بعد ترميمات عديدة.
dates: القرن 10 الهجري / 16 الميلادي؛ عام 995 هجري / 1588 ميلادي.
keywords: برج؛ بستيون؛ قلعة؛ بناية عسكرية؛ متحف الأسلحة.
partner: Ministry of Culture,Directorate of Cultural Heritage

en.name: North Burj.
description:
This massive military construction, built of adobe, is approximately square plan. A tower stands at each of its four corners and corridors run around its interior. The ceilings consist of semi-circular barrel vaults. Some simple decoration has survived, but it has been partially covered by repeated restoration work and a lack of relevant documentation makes dating difficult. A wide staircase with more than 60 steps leads to the terrace.  
Today, the *burj* is used as an armaments museum.

Located on a hill to the north of the Fez *medina*, outside the ramparts, the North Burj (now a museum of armaments) is a bastion built in the AH 10th / AD 16th century by the Sa'did Sultan Ahmad al-Mansur. This massive military structure, built with adobe and flanked by four towers, helped to protect the town against several sieges at the hands of various tribes and pretenders to the throne.  
Corridors run around the inside the building. Its semi-circular vaulted ceilings are adorned with simple decorations, some of which have been covered up by repeated restorations.
keywords: Burj; bastion; military building; museum
partner: Ministry of Culture, Directorate of Cultural Heritage

es.name: *Bury* norte.
description:
Maciza construcción militar en adobe y de planta prácticamente cuadrada, en cada una de cuyas esquinas se alza una torre. Unos pasillos recorren el perímetro interior del edificio. Los techos tienen forma de bóvedas de cañón. Se conserva parte de la sencilla decoración, parcialmente tapada tras las múltiples restauraciones, por lo que, a falta de documentación, es difícil de datar. Una amplia escalera de más de 60 peldaños conduce a la terraza.  
En la actualidad, el *bury* alberga el Museo de Armas.

Situado sobre una colina al norte de la medina de Fez, fuera de su recinto, el *bury* Norte (hoy Museo de Armas) es un bastión construido en el siglo X / XVI por el sultán saadí Ahmad al-Mansur. Este macizo edificio militar de adobe, flanqueado por cuatro torres, sirvió para defender la ciudad de Fez de los constantes asaltos de tribus y de aspirantes al trono.  
Unos pasillos recorren el perímetro interior del bastión. Los techos tienen forma de bóveda de cañón, con sencilla decoración tapada en parte tras múltiples restauraciones.
keywords: Bury ; bastión ; edificio militar ; museo
partner: Ministry of Culture,Directorate of Cultural Heritage

fr.name: Borj nord.
description:
Ce massif édifice militaire construit en pisé s'élève sur un plan sensiblement carré ; une tour se dresse à chacun des quatre coins, et des couloirs font le tour à l'intérieur de la bâtisse. Les plafonds sont en forme de voûte arrondie en arc de cercle. Quelques décorations subsistent, simples, mais partiellement recouvertes après de multiples restaurations, qu'il est difficile de dater faute de documents. Un large escalier de plus de 60 marches livre accès à la terrasse.  
  
Aujourd'hui le *borj* est utilisé comme musée des Armes.

Situé sur une colline au nord de la médina de Fès, à l'extérieur des remparts, le Borj nord (aujourd'hui musée des Armes) est un bastion construit au XVIe siècle par le sultan saadien Ahmed al-Mansour. Cet édifice militaire massif, en pisé, flanqué de quatre tours, a servi à protéger la ville de Fès contre les nombreux sièges des tribus et des prétendants au trône.  
Des couloirs font le tour à l'intérieur de la bâtisse. Les plafonds sont en forme de voûte arrondie en arc de cercle, avec des décorations simples, partiellement recouvertes après de multiples restaurations.
dynasty: Saadienne, Xe siècle de l’Hégire (XVIe siècle J.-C.).
keywords: borj ; bastion ; édifice militaire ; musée
partner: Ministry of Culture,Directorate of Cultural Heritage

en.name: Vila Palace
description: Surrounded by the houses of the presentday town of Sintra and occupying the whole of the top of a small hill overlooking one of the region’s most luxuriant valleys, the palace stands out by virtue of the extraordinary interplay between its different volumes and shapes. In more remote times, this was a small, fortified settlement where the inhabitants of the surrounding region would seek refuge in the event of danger. In the Islamic period, although it continued to perform this same role for a brief period, this small fortification was almost certainly rebuilt at the end of the 5th/11th century to adapt the area between the walls for recreational purposes and to serve as a country residence. Although there is no actual archaeological evidence of this, such a conclusion is suggested by its systematic use by the queens of the first Portuguese Dynasty. Major rebuilding work was undertaken to transform the area into a palace in the 15th and 16th centuries, and Moorish taste is echoed in a whole series of additional volumes that have been interlaced and juxtaposed to achieve an architectural synthesis of rare harmony. Small courtyards with babbling water and the gentle polychrome effect created by the use of glazed tiles have given the palace’s interior one of the most beautiful atmospheres in Mudejar art and in the whole of Portuguese architecture.

es.name: Palacio da Vila
description: Rodeado por las casas de la actual villa de Sintra y ocupando todo un pequeño cerro que se alza en uno de los valles más exuberantes de la sierra, el Palacio da Vila se destaca por lo insólito de su juego de volúmenes. Antiguamente, el lugar era un pequeño poblado fortificado donde se refugiaban en caso de peligro los habitantes de los alrededores. En época islámica, esta pequeña fortificación, que en un primer momento siguió desempeñando la misma función, debió de sufrir, a finales del siglo V/f. XI, algunas obras para adaptar el área de intramuros a funciones de ocio y casa de campo. Aunque no se tengan pruebas arqueológicas de ello, lo sugiere su uso sistemático por las reinas de la primera dinastía portuguesa. En los siglos XV y XVI se hicieron grandes obras de adaptación palatina, por lo que el gusto *morisco* domina todo un conjunto de volúmenes enlazados y yuxtapuestos, síntesis arquitectónica de rara armonía. Pequeños patios de aguas murmurantes y la policromía suave de los azulejos hacen del interior una de las más bellas ensoñaciones del arte *mudéjar* y de toda la arquitectura portuguesa.

en.name: Console
description: From a base with four round feet springs the console resembling two vine branches, intertwined with vine-leaves and grapes. The carving is powerful as the volumes are full and in the round. The wood is gilded with silver leaf. The table is painted to look like a dark green false marble, with pale green veins. Formerly thought to be a nineteenth-century remake from a Tuscan workshop, today this console is considered an original piece dating to the eighteenth-century. The original provenance is unknown, but it was likely made in Tuscany. The console is part of the furniture of the baroque apartment, on the first floor of the building which was made between 1736 and 1738 for the wedding of Francesco Tozzoni and Carlotta Beroaldi.

This piece of furniture is very original; the base is made of vine-shoots and grapes realistically intertwined with a strongly naturalistic carving. We don’t know its original provenance. The console is housed in the red living room of the baroque apartment on the first floor of Palazzo Tozzoni, built between 1736 and 1738 for the marriage of Francesco Tozzoni and Carlotta Beroaldi.
dates: First half of the eighteenth century
keywords: Console; Woodwork; furnishing; wood carving; grape design; vine tendris decoration; workpshop
materials: Wood carved, painted as marble and covered with a silver leaf

it.name: Console
description: Su un basamento con quattro piedini tondi è innestato il fusto della console che finge due rami di vite, intrecciati con pampini e grappoli. Lo stile dell'intaglio è potente e i volumi sono pieni, a tutto tondo, ad ottenere un effetto di potente plasticità. Il legno è ricoperto da una doratura a mecca a gradevole battitura metallica che non indulge alla modulazione morbida e piena dell'oro come è consuetudine di questo tipo di mobilia, con effetto di grande originalità. Il piano d'appoggio sagomato è in legno marmorizzato, con fondo vede scuro, percorso da venature più chiare. Una prima valutazione critica proponeva di collocarne l'esecuzione a metà Ottocento, a carico di una bottega toscana, secondo la moda del rifacimento neobarocco del periodo; più recenti valutazioni critiche e tecniche, propendono, invece, per una datazione settecentesca. A tale ipotesi concorre anche l'effetto di forte realismo dei tralci di vite che costituiscono il fusto. Non ne conosciamo la provenienza ma l'ipotesi di una realizzazione ina rea toscana appare possibile anche se espressa dubitativamente. La console si trova nell'appartamento barocchetto, situato al piano nobile del palazzo e realizzato tra 1736 e 1738 per le nozze di Francesco Tozzoni con Carlotta Beroaldi.

Il mobile ha caratteristiche di grande originalità; il fusto è caratterizzato dall’intreccio di tralci di vite arricchiti da foglie e grappoli, alla ricerca di un effetto naturalistico, realizzato con un intaglio di grande forza. Non ne conosciamo la provenienza La console arreda il salotto rosso dell’appartamento barocchetto, situato al pino nobile del palazzo e costuito tra 1736 e 1738 per le nozze di Francesco Tozzoni con Carlotta Beroaldi.
keywords: console; arredo intagliato; grappolo d'uva; decorazione a tralci di vite; bottega

en.name: Rekord II als Luftfracht in die VAR, Mediterranean Airways Trans, Libanon, DC4
description: This photograph by German photographer Heinz Woost captures a DC-4 aircraft of the Lebanon-based Trans-Mediterranean Airways during cargo loading operations. Taken at a time when goods were being transported to the United Arab Republic (UAR), the political union of Egypt and Syria from 1958 to 1971, the image reflects both the logistics of mid-20th century air transport and the UAR’s pursuit of modernization and international connectivity.
keywords: Aviation; Transportation; Airways; Lebanon; Photography

en.name: São Julião (Parish Church)
description:
The Church was altered and enlarged in 1515 by order of D. Manuel I, when there was a considerable increase in population and the monarch was keen to enhance the town with suitably majestic buildings. João Favacho, who almost certainly worked on the Mosteiro dos Jerónimos, carried out the work between 1516 and 1519.  
Various earthquakes affected the city, mainly that of 1755, which destroyed almost all the Manueline work, leaving only two portals and the bell tower. The North Door is extraordinarily exuberant, combining naturalist elements with others based on silver and fabric designs. The axial door is simpler but also heavily naturalist, with twisted arches ending in canopies.

en.name: Cock
description:
It was difficult to make and fire large ceramic figures like this one and the sphinx (Isl 56) with the technology of the day. They easily crackled or simply collapsed. The manganese, turquoise and blue glazes as well as the carved decoration are typical of laqabi ware, but while the glazes on a horizontal surface are kept in place by the carved decoration, this is not the case on an upright object like this one.  
  
Although both animals must be considered mythical creatures, the artist managed to depict the watchful and aggressive cock with all of this animal’s natural characteristics.
dates: AH 2nd half of the 6th / AD 2nd half of 12th century
keywords: Water; sphinx; ceramics; sculpture; fritware; Ayyubids; Zangids
materials: Cast, modeled and carved fritware, painted in blue, turquoise, and manganese under a transparent glaze
tags: Cast, modeled and carved fritware, painted in blue, turquoise, and manganese under a transparent glaze

ar.name: دار حسين.
description:
يفضي المدخل الرئيسي للقصر إلى ساحة تؤدي أيضاً إلى جامع القصر. يتم الوصول إلى وسط الدار من خلال الدريبة (دهليز)، التي تغطيها سلسلة من القبوات المتعامدة المبنية بالآجر المرصوص من جانب حرفه.  
وقد تم فتح بوابتين على جانبي الدريبة، تفضيان بالممر إلى سقيفة تؤدي إلى الفناء الداخلي. يحيط بهذا الأخير رواق بديع يتميز بالاستعمال الكثيف للرخام الإيطالي في تلبيس فتحات الأبواب والأعمدة و وتبليط الأرضيات .  
كما تتباين ألواح زليج القلالين المزيَّنة بالمحاريب والغنية بألوانها مع لوحات الرخام ذات الزخارف الزهرية الإيطالية الهيئة، وإفريز الجبس الذي يعلوها، مشكلاً سلسلة من الأقواس، ومذكراً بالتقليد الفني الأندلسي. نلاحظ أيضاً حوضاً بديعاً في كوّة الجدار الشرقي.  
يؤدي الفناء الداخلي إلى الشقق الخاصة وإلى قاعة الاحتفالات. تتشكل الأجنحة الثلاث الخاصة من فضاء على شكل حرف التاء اللاتيني "T"، وتزخر بزخارف متجانسة. يتواجد في القسم الذي ينفتح على الجانب الجنوبي بيت الديوان، وهو عبارة عن قاعة بديعة للاستقبالات، شُيّدت على عهد يوسف صاحب الطابع. وقد تمّت المحفاظة على التوزيع على شكل حرف التاء اللاتيني مع القباب الثلاث؛ وتُبْرز القبة التي تغطي القاعة بشكل جلي التأثيرين الأندلسي والتركي على السواء.  
يشكل الطابق العلوي من الدار إضافة ألحقت في القرن 13 هجري/ 19 ميلادي. تنفتح على الجهة الشرقية قاعة ذات مقاييس جميلة كانت تستعمل كمقر لاجتماعات المجلس البلدي؛ وقد تأثر طرازها بالنمط الإيطالي ويختلف عن الطراز المستعمل في بقية الدار.  
الفناء المتواجد في الطابق العلوي أقلّ اتساعا من فناء الطابق الأرضي، ولكنه أكثر ابتكاراً. في الماضي، كان الفناء عبارة عن فضاء مكشوف، يضمّ باحة معمّدة من الطراز الإيطالي العائد إلى القرن التاسع عشر.  
وفي نهاية الأروقة الأربعة الخارجة عن الباحة المعمّدة تتوزّع أربعة أجنحة خاصة مزينة بلوحات من الزليج، جلب بعض مربعاتها من بلدان أجنبية. ويمثّل الإفريز الجبسي المنحوت الذي يعلوها موضوعات زهريّة ذات أسلوب تقليدي.  
وبالإضافة إلى الغرف الخاصّة وقاعات الاحتفال والباحات الداخليّة، تضمّ دار حسين قسما للخدمات وحمّاما ومستودعات وإسطبلات. وأخيراً، تضيف حديقة جميلة لمسة من الذوق الرفيع إلى هذا القصر البديع.

استعملت هذه المعلمة التي تعتبر قصرا من أجمل القصور بالمدينة العتيقة، على التوالي كإقامة للأمراء، والدايات والبايات. وفي عام 1858، احتضنت الدار أول مجلس بلدي لمدينة تونس. سكن الجنرال حسين، رئيس المجلس البلدي، القصر الذي يحمل منذئذ اسمه. وبعد تحوله إلى مقر لقيادة جنود الاحتلال الفرنسي (1882)، خصص القصر منذ الاستقلال، عام 1957، إلى المعهد الوطني للآثار والفن الذي أصبح لاحقا المعهد الوطني للتراث.  
تعكس دار حسين مختلف وأهم فترات العمارة التونسية، منذ الفترة الحسينية وحتى الفترات الأندلسية والتركية والاستعمارية.
artist: إسماعيل كاهية، وزير وصهر علي باي.
history: سكن عبد المؤمن بن علي، مؤسّس الدولة الموحّدية، هذه الدار عام 555 هجري/ 1159 ميلادي، ثم سكنها أبو زكريّا الأوّل، وأجرى عليها بعض التعديلات لتصبح الدار قصراً للضيافة. استقرّ بها، في بداية العهد العثماني، عثمان داي عام 1003-1019 هجري/ 1594-1611 ميلادي. في القرن 12 هجري/ 18 ميلادي، تحوّلت ملكيّتها إلى الوزير إسماعيل كاهية، صهر علي باي الثاني، وكان ذلك بين عامي 1169-1190 هجري/ 1775-   1777 ميلادي. لاحقا، قام الوزير يوسف صاحب الطابع بشراء الدار، وسمحت له ثروته بتوسيع وتزيين هذا القصر الذي أصبح عام 1275 هجري/ 1858 ميلادي أوّل مقرّ لبلديّة مدينة تونس. ثمّ سكن القصر القائد حسين، أحد كبار المصلحين، إضافةً إلى توليه منصب رئيس المجلس البلدي، فحمل القصر اسمه منذ ذلك الوقت. وأخيراً، وبعد أن تحوّل المكان إلى مقرّ القيادة العليا لقوّات الاحتلال في عهد الاستعمار 1882، ومنذ عام 1957 أصبح القصر مقرّاً للمعهد الوطني للآثار والفنون الذي تحوّل عام 1992 إلى المعهد الوطني للتراث.
keywords: تأثير تركي؛ تأثير أندلسي؛ تأثير إيطالي؛ زخرفة زهريّة؛ زخرفة هندسيّة؛ زليج؛ عمارة بلاطيّة؛ قاشاني.
partner: Ministry of Culture, National Institute of Cultural Heritage

en.name: Dar Husayn.
description:
The main entrance of the palace overlooks the square, alongside which also stands the Qasar Mosque. One gains access to the centre of the house through the *driba* or hallway. This area is roofed with a series of groined vaults in which the bricks are set on edge.  
Through two coach doors, one on either side of the *driba*, one comes into a *sqifa* or antechamber, which leads in turn to the internal courtyard. This space is surrounded by a magnificent portico. Italian marble has been used abundantly to pave the floors and to face the doorways and colonnades. The rich, multicoloured Quallaline ceramic panels with their *mihrab*\-style features make a stunning contrast to the marble slabs with their Italianate floral decoration and to the stucco frieze above them. This last has a succession of arches reminiscent of the Andalusian tradition. Within a niche in the east wall stands a superb cistern.  
One enters the apartments and the robing room from the courtyard. Similar in their ornamentation, the three apartments are arranged in a T-shape. Opening towards the south side is a *bayt al-diwan*, an amazing reception room, built by Yussef Sahib el-Taba'a also on a T-shaped plan. There are three alcoves. The building carries a dome which shows both Andalusian and Turkish influences.  
The upper floor of the house was added in the AH 13th / AD 19th century. The well-proportioned room on the east side was the meeting place for the municipal council. Though Italianate in style, its decoration differs from that of the rest of the house.  
The courtyard on the first floor is smaller but more unusual than that of the ground floor. Originally it was open to the skies, but now it has a typically 19th-century Italianate peristyle. On the four galleries of this peristyle are four apartments. They have fired-clay frescoes in which some of the tiles are of foreign provenance. Over these appear carved plaster friezes with traditional floral motifs.  
Dar Husayn also has offices and servants' quarters, a Turkish bath, storehouses and stables. The final touch of refinement added to this fabulous palace was the beautiful garden.

This monument, one of the most beautiful palaces in the *medina*, was inhabited by successive *dey* and *bey* princes. In 1858, it hosted the first council for the city of Tunis. General Husayn, chairman of the city council, lived in the palace, which has since borne his name. The palace was used as the command headquarters for occupying French troops (1882) before being given over to the National Institute of Art and Archaeology, now the National Heritage Institute, following independence in 1957.
artist: Isma‘il Kahiya, minister and son-in-law of ‘Ali Bey.
history: ‘Abd al Mumin ibn ‘Ali, founder of the Almohad state, lived in this great house in 555 / 1159. Abu Zakariya I lived there himself and carried out some modifications. After his departure Dar Husayn became the 'guest's palace'. At the beginning of the Ottoman period, Othman *dey* resided there (1003–19 / 1594–1611). From 1169 to 1190 (1755–77) the house was the property of the minister Isma'il Kahiya, son-in-law of ‘Ali Bey II. After this the minister Yusuf Sahib al-Taba'a bought the palace and his great wealth allowed him to enlarge and embellish it; then, in 1275 (1858), the palace became the headquarters of the municipality of Tunis. General Husayn, the great reformer and president of the municipal council, then occupied the palace, which ever since has borne his name. It served as high command headquarters for the occupying army during the Colonial era (1882). Since 1957, the palace has been the headquarters of the National Institute of Archaeology and Art, which became the National Institute of the Patrimony in 1992.
keywords: Palatine architecture; floral decoration; Italian influence; geometric decoration; Andalusian influence; Turkish influence
partner: Ministry of Culture, National Institute of Cultural Heritage

es.name: Dar Husayn.
description:
La entrada principal del palacio da a una plaza desde la cual también se accede a la mezquita al-Qsar. La entrada al centro de la residencia se hace a través de la *driba* (vestíbulo), cubierta por una serie de bóvedas de arista con aparejo de ladrillo a panderete.  
Dos puertas cocheras, situadas a ambos lados de la *driba*, dan acceso a una *sqifa* (antesala) que conduce al patio interior. Éste está rodeado de un magnífico pórtico, marcado por la abundante utilización de mármol de Italia en los marcos de los vanos, las columnas y el enlosado del suelo. Los paneles de cerámica de Qallalin, con decoración de propia de un *mihrab* y rica policromía, contrastan con los paneles de mármol, por su decoración floral italianizante y el friso de estuco que los corona, una sucesión de arcos que recuerda la tradición andalusí. Una magnífica cisterna está encajada en el muro este.  
Desde el patio se entra en los apartamentos y la sala ceremonial. Los tres apartamentos configuran un espacio en forma de T con una decoración homogénea. Hacia el lado sur se abre *bayt al-diwan*, una magnífica sala de recepción construida bajo Yusuf Sahib al-Tabaa, cuya planta también adopta la disposición de T invertida, con tres alcobas. La cúpula que la cubre refleja influencias andalusíes y turcas.  
La planta superior de la morada fue añadida en el siglo XIII / XIX. En el lado este se abre una sala que albergaba las reuniones del Consejo Municipal. Por su estilo italianizante, difiere del resto de la casa.  
El patio de la planta superior es menos amplio que el de la planta baja, pero más original. Antaño a cielo abierto, está dotado de un peristilo típico del estilo italianizante del siglo XIII / XIX. A lo largo de las cuatro galerías se distribuyen cuatro apartamentos adornados con frescos de cerámica, cuyos azulejos son de origen extranjero. El friso de yeso esculpido que los corona presenta temas florales de estilo tradicional.  
Además de los apartamentos, las salas de recepción y los patios, Dar Husayn comprende zonas comunes, un *hammam*, almacenes y establos. Finalmente, un bonito jardín añadía un toque de refinamiento a este magnífico palacio.

Este monumento, uno de los más bellos palacios de la medina, sirvió sucesivamente de residencia a los príncipes, a los deyes y a los beyes. En 1858 acogió el primer Consejo Municipal de la ciudad de Túnez. El general Husayn, presidente del Consejo Municipal, habitó el palacio, que desde entonces lleva su nombre. Sede de la comandancia de las tropas del ejército francés desde la ocupación (1882), el edificio se destinó a partir de la independencia, en 1957, al Instituto Nacional de Arqueología y Arte, convertido en Instituto Nacional del Patrimonio.  
Dar Husayn refleja los diferentes e importantes periodos de la arquitectura tunecina, desde la época andalusí hasta la husayní, la turca y la colonial.
artist: Ismail Kahiya, ministro y yerno de Ali Bey.
history: Abd al-Muman ibn Ali, fundador del Estado almohade, vivió en esta gran morada en el año 555 / 1159. Abu Zakariya I, después de habitarla, efectuó algunas modificaciones y Dar Husayn se convirtió entonces en el palacio de los huéspedes. Al principio de la época otomana, Ozman Dey se instaló en esta residencia (1003-1019 / 1594-1611), y en el siglo XII / XVIII fue propiedad del ministro Ismael Kahiya, yerno de Ali Bey, entre 1169 / 1755 y 1190 / 1777. Luego, el ministro Yusuf Sahib al-Tabaa la compró, y su fortuna le permitió ampliar y embellecer este palacio. En 1275 / 1858 se convirtió en la primera sede de la municipalidad de la ciudad de Túnez. El general Husayn, gran reformador y presidente del Consejo Municipal, habitó este palacio, que desde entonces lleva su nombre. Después de haber sido sede de la comandancia superior de las tropas de la ocupación en la época colonial (1882), el palacio alberga, desde 1957, el Instituto Nacional de Arqueología y Arte, Instituto Nacional del Patrimonio desde 1992.
keywords: arquitectura palatina; decoración floral; influencia italiana; decoración geométrica; influencias andalusíes; influencias turcas
partner: Ministry of Culture, National Institute of Cultural Heritage

fr.name: Dar Hussein.
description:
L'entrée principale du palais donne sur une place qui dessert également la mosquée al-Qsar. L'accès au centre de la demeure se fait par la *driba* (vestibule) recouverte d'une série de voûtes d'arêtes en briques posées de chant.  
  
Deux portes cochères sont placées de part et d'autre de la *driba* desservant l'accès à une *skifa* (anti-chambre) conduisant à la cour intérieure. Cette dernière est entourée d'un magnifique portique marqué par l'utilisation abondante du marbre d'Italie dans le placage des ouvertures des portes, la colonnade et le dallage du sol. Les panneaux de céramique de Qallaline à décor de *mihrab* et riche polychromie contrastent avec les panneaux de marbre à décor floral italianisant et avec la frise de stuc qui les surmonte – une succession d'arceaux rappelant la tradition andalouse. Une magnifique citerne est nichée dans le mur est.  
  
La cour permet d'accéder aux appartements et à la salle d'apparat. Les trois appartements sont formés par un espace en T à l'ornementation homogène. Ouvrant sur le côté sud se trouve *bayt ad-diwan*, une magnifique salle de réception édifiée sous Youssef Sahib el-Tabaa et dont le plan conserve la disposition en T avec les 3 alcôves. La coupole qui la surplombe traduit bien les influences andalouses et turques.  
  
L'étage supérieur de la demeure est une adjonction du XIIIe siècle H (XIXe siècle J.-C.). Sur le côté est ouvre une salle aux belles proportions qui a abrité les réunions du Conseil municipal. Son style italianisant diffère de celui du reste de la demeure.  
  
La cour de l'étage est moins vaste que celle du rez-de-chaussée, mais plus originale. Autrefois à ciel ouvert, la cour est dotée d'un péristyle typique du style italianisant du XIXe. Sur les quatre galeries du péristyle sont distribués quatre appartements ornés de fresques de faïences dont certains carreaux sont d'origine étrangère. La frise de plâtre sculpté qui les surmonte présente des thèmes floraux de style traditionnel.  
  
Outre les appartements, les salles d'apparat et les patios, Dar Hussein comporte des communs, un hammam, des réserves et des écuries. Enfin, un beau jardin ajoutait une touche de raffinement à ce magnifique palais.

Ce monument, l'un des plus beaux palais de la médina, servit successivement de résidence aux princes, aux deys et aux beys. En 1858, il abrita le premier conseil municipal de la ville de Tunis. Le général Hussein, président du conseil municipal, habita le palais qui porte depuis son nom. Siège du commandement des troupes d'occupation française (1882), le palais est affecté depuis l'indépendance, en 1957, à l'Institut national d'archéologie et d'art devenu l'Institut national du patrimoine.  
Dar Hussein reflète les différentes et importantes époques de l'architecture tunisienne, de l'époque husseinite aux périodes andalouse, turque et coloniale.
artist: Ismaïl Kahia, ministre et gendre de Ali Bey.
history: Abdelmoumen ibn Ali, fondateur de l'état almohade, a habité cette grande demeure en 555 H / 1159 J.-C. Abou Zakariya Ier, après y avoir habité, effectua quelques modifications, et Dar Hussein devint alors le palais des invités. Au début de l'époque ottomane, Othman Dey s'y fixa (1003-1019 H / 1594-1611 J.-C.). Au XIIe siècle H (XVIIIe siècle J.-C.), la demeure propriété du ministre Ismaïl Kahia, gendre de Ali Bey II, de 1169 à 1190 H / 1755-1777 J.-C. Par la suite, le ministre Youssef Sahib el-Tabaa acheta la demeure, sa fortune lui permit d'agrandir et d'embellir ce palais. Il devint en 1275 H / 1858 J.-C. le premier siège de la municipalité de Tunis. Le général Hussein, grand réformateur et président du conseil municipal, habita alors le palais qui porte depuis son nom. Après avoir été le siège du commandement supérieur des troupes d'occupation à l'époque coloniale (1882), le palais est, depuis 1957, le siège de l'Institut national d'archéologie et d'art, devenu depuis 1992 l'Institut national du patrimoine.
keywords: Architecture palatine; décoration florale; influences italiennes; décoration géométrique; influences andalouses; influences turques.
partner: Ministry of Culture, National Institute of Cultural Heritage

en.name: Chancel
description: The chancel is completely covered with gilded and carved woodwork. In the centre of the altar stands the miraculous image of Our Lord of Matosinhos flanked by Late Renaissance stone figures.
place: Interior, Sanctuary of Bom Jesus de Matosinhos
artist: Portuguese woodcarvers: Luís Pereira da Costa (active 1724–?), Domingos Martins Moreira (active 1746–1750)

en.name: Imaret
short_description: *Imaret* was an educational and charitable foundation, donated by Mohammed ‘Ali, founder of modern Egypt, to his hometown. The complex included an elementary school and two higher level colleges dedicated to the instruction of the traditional Islamic curriculum, modern sciences and mathematics. It is one of the earliest examples of western style technical school providing secular education in the Ottoman Empire and reflects Mohammed ‘Ali’s program of modernization. The complex had 61 rooms for up to 300 boarding students, two study halls, a library, a printing press and a soup kitchen to feed students, travellers and the poor, regardless of religion. To meet the religious and hygiene needs of its occupants, the complex also contained a place for prayer, fountains for ablutions and a hammam. Cisterns underneath the structure guaranteed a continuous source of water.
holder: IMARET – Institute Mohammed Ali for the Research of the Eastern Tradition (under contract with the Egyptian Waqf Organization)
history: With the passage of time, the charitable and educational purposes of the foundation declined. According to surviving records, the School continued to function as late as 1902, and the Soup Kitchen as late as 1923. After the Lausanne Treaty and the exchange of populations between Greece and Turkey, the complex housed Greek refugees from Asia Minor (1927–1960). In 1954, Imaret was listed as a protected historical monument by the Greek Government. A series of (never realized) agreements between Greece and Egypt to restore the monument followed. In August 2001, a contract was signed between the Egyptian Waqf Organization and the Missirian family, who undertook the demanding task of restoring the two monuments and attributing them to new uses.
keywords: 19th century Ottoman baroque; Waqf; educational and charitable foundation; Mohammed Ali; Egypt; secular education in the Ottoman Empire
partner: IMARET – Institute Mohammed Ali for the Research of the Eastern Tradition

The interiors of the tiles are not identical, but each has scrolling arabesque forms. All of the star tiles are cut in half vertically.

en.name: Lithographed Qur’an, originally written by Shukr Zadeh (d. AH 1166 / AD 1753)
short_description: This Qur'an, originally caligraphed by the famous Ottoman calligrapher Shukr Zadeh is the first Qur'an to be printed in an Islamic country by way of lithograpy. It was produced around 1850 AD.While printing had begun in Europe many centuries ago, the Islamic world continued to favour handwritten books, and most certainly as regards copies of the Holy Qur’an. In 1834, the first edition of Gustav Fluegel’s printed Qur’an was published, while in the Ottoman Empire, the printing of Qur’ans began only in the second half of the 19th century, both in Egypt and in Istanbul. Most were lithographed, as they had the look and feel of manuscripts. Most importantly, all the required recitational signs could be rendered accurately.
holder: Sharjah Museum of Islamic Civilisation / Sharjah Museums Department
artist: Original calligraphed by Shukr Zadeh (d. AH 1166 / AD 1753)
keywords: naskhi; sura

en.name: Panel from a door or *minbar*
description: This carved pine panel is composed of two boards flanking alternating square and rectangular panels. The vine scrolls, particularly those carved in high relief in the central panels, exhibit close affinities with their Late Antique prototypes. A nearly identical panel in the Benaki Museum in Athens suggests that together these may have formed a two-panelled door.
dates: Hegira 2nd–first half 3rd century / AD late 8th–first half 9th century

de.name: Kath. Wallfahrtskirche Heiligkreuz
description: Das zurückhaltende Äußere der Kirche mit einem Schweifgiebel an der Frontseite verrät wenig vom Reichtum des Inneren, jedoch wird hier bereits die Baugestalt ablesbar, ein Kreuz mit zentraler Kuppelvierung und drei gleich gestalteten Armen, deren Ecken ausgerundet sind, ergänzt durch einen weiteren Kreuzarm, ein queroblonge Eingangshalle im Norden. Im Inneren beherrschen die nach römischem Muster mit abgeschrägten Pilasterpfeilern angelegte Vierung und die darüber aufragende Kuppel mit großer Laterne den Raumeindruck. Die symbolische Form des Kreuzes prägt die Baugestalt und wird in ihrer ikonologischen Bedeutung als Zeichen des Heils im Freskenzyklus Christoph Anton Mayrs auch zur bildlichen Anschauung gebracht.

Der einzige echte Zentralbau des großen Tiroler Kirchenbaumeisters Franz de Paula Penz wurde über der Grundform eines griechischen Kreuzes errichtet, die das hier verehrte Kruzifix symbolisiert. Das Innere dominiert die Kuppelvierung mit den Hauptszenen der in kräftigen Farben gehaltenen Ausmalung zur Kreuzeslegende. So ergibt sich eine überschaubare Einheit von Aussage und Form, wie sie gerade für kleinere Zentralbauten im Spätbarock typisch ist und hier in besonders hohem Grad erreicht wird.
artist:
Architektur (Entwürfe): Franz de Paula Penz (1707-1772)  
Bauleitung: Johann Michael Umhaus(er) (um 1710-1784; zugeschrieben)  
Deckenfresken: Christoph Anton Mayr (um 1720-1771)  
Bildhauerarbeiten: Gregor Fritz (1693-1774; zugeschrieben)
history: Die Verehrung des hl. Kreuzes von Pill geht auf ein Ereignis im Spanischen Erbfolgekrieg zurück, als bayerische Truppen in Tirol eingerückt waren. Bei den Kämpfen wurde die Zirler Innbrücke am 25. Juli 1703 abgebrannt, wobei das Brückenkreuz in den Inn fiel. Unterhalb von Pill, beim Heiligkreuzstollen, wurde es unversehrt geborgen. Bald galt das Kreuz als wundertätig und wurde in einer provisorischen Holzkapelle aufgestellt. Die zunehmende Wallfahrt veranlasste den Kurat Bernhard Kiechl 1764 zum Bau einer gemauerten Kirche, die am 25. Juli 1766 vom Brixener Bischof Leopold Graf Spaur eingeweiht werden konnte. Anlässlich der letzten Renovierung 1981-85 wurde der Bau um fünf Meter von der vorbeiführenden Bundesstrasse zurückversetzt.
keywords: Wallfahrtskirche; Zentralbau; Kreuzeslegende; Deckenfresken

en.name: Catholic Pilgrimage Church of the Holy Cross
description: The church’s modest exterior with a tail gable on the front side betrays little of its rich interior, although the building design is already apparent: a cross with central-crossing cupola and three uniformly designed arms, supplemented by a transverse oblong vestibule to the north. The spatial impression of the interior is dominated by the crossing with slanting pilaster piers according to the Roman design, surmounted by the cupola with its large skylight turret. The symbolism of the cross informs the building design and is also present in pictorial form as a symbol of salvation in Christoph Anton Mayr’s cycle of frescos.

The only genuine centralised building of the great Tyrolean master church-builder Franz de Paula Penz was built on the ground plan of a Greek cross, here symbolising the crucifix. The interior is dominated by the crossing cupola with its main scenes of the Legend of the Cross in bold colours. The clear unity of form and expression, as typical for smaller Late Baroque centralised buildings, has reached a high degree of perfection here.
artist: Architecture, plans: Franz de Paula Penz (1707–1772); building supervision, attributed to: Johann Michael Umhaus(er) (c. 1710–1784); ceiling frescos: Christoph Anton Mayr (c. 1720–1771); sculptural work, attributed to: Gregor Fritz (1693–1774)
history: The veneration of the holy cross of Pill dates back to the time of the War of the Spanish Succession as Bavarian troops invaded Tyrol. On 25 July 1703, during fighting, the bridge over the Inn at Zirl burnt down and the bridge cross fell into the river. It was recovered undamaged downstream from Pill, was soon held to be miraculous and was erected in a provisional wooden chapel. Increasing numbers of pilgrims occasioned curate Bernhard Kiechl to build the church in 1764, consecrated by the Bishop of Brixen Leopold Graf Spau on 25 July 1766. During the last renovation of 1981–5 it was moved five metres back from the main road passing directly in front of it.
keywords: Pilgrimage church; centralised building; ceiling frescoes

en.name: Engraved rock
description:
This engraved rock bears an inscription of a poem consisting of 12 verses composed by Khalfan bin Rashid. The prose documents the completion of a well in the Wilayat of al-Hamra for the Governor Saif bin Muhammad ibn Sayyar in AH 1177 / AD 1763, during the reign of Imam Ahmad bin Said al-Busaidi, the founder of the al-Busaid Household.  
  
The poem reads as follows:  
  
The Almighty granted the efforts with success  
The well has been built with mold and rocks.  
Its omens were like a magic,  
The area around seems heavenly, a garden full of trees bearing fruits.  
What a garden that burying sadness, with its flourishing beauty  
Blessed be its owner, the builder and those who dwelled in it.  
  
He , who had been freehanded to build the well, is Saif, son of Mohammad ibn Sayyar,  
And is the wise Wali of Oman, and the best leader.  
( )  
May the Almighty Allah protect him from the enviers, and those who are disloyal  
The best we conclude is by prayers upon the prophet Mohammad (Peace be Upon Him) as much of rainy clouds and more.  
In AH 20 Safar 1177, was written by (), Khalfan bin Rashid, ().
place: Local acquisition – Purchased 2020 from Badar bin Mohammed bin Hamed al-Sinani
artist: Author of the inscribed poem: Khalfan bin Rashid
keywords: Water; gravestone; al-Busaid

en.name: City Centre
description:
To understand the layout of the historic centre one must remember the ancient route of the Appian Way for those coming from Rome. From Albano you descended into the Ariccia valley, and starting at least from medieval times, you climbed up to the Roman Gate, crossed the whole town and came out from the Neapolitan Gate heading towards the steep slope of the Catena and Colle Pardo towards Genzano.  
The current Corso was therefore, until the construction of the Monumental Bridge, the main road axis of the town.  
  
The splendour that the city of *Aricia* had known in Roman times was followed by an inexorable decline as a consequence of the barbarian invasions that made the Appia route unsafe. After that, travellers started taking the route of the Via della Faiola (current Via dei Laghi) to reach southern Latium. Without the great economic flywheel represented by the Appia *Regina Viarum* (Queen of Roads), the city had gradually became depopulated until it was almost erased from the maps of the inhabited centres, especially after the disastrous Saracen raids that followed one after the other between 846 and 916 and especially due to the changed road layout.  
  
In 1473 when the Savellis acquired the territory of Ariccia from the monks of Grottaferrata, their efforts focused on rebuilding the uninhabitable ruins scattered through the abandoned territory and making them habitable. The current Old Town in its oldest housing units date to this first period of rebirth, although since it occupies part of the ancient acropolis of *Aricia* , it also hosts millenary vestiges. The urban rearrangements carried out in the 17th century by Gian Lorenzo Bernini gave new prestige to the town not only through the splendidly scenographic Court Square (Piazza di Corte) but also through the new layout of the main road axis with the arrangement of the mighty southern bastions, the Roman Gate, the Complex of Saint Nicholas and finally the Neapolitan Gate.  
Starting from the end of the 16th century, the Corso, now Corso Garibaldi, never ceased to be enriched with noble palaces as in the case of the Palazzo Primoli (Piazza della Repubblica n. 4-10), formerly known as Casino Kaisermann, purchased in the first half of the 19th century by Carlo Luciano Bonaparte prince of Canino and brother of Napoleon, and that was later inherited by the Conti Primoli family. A typical neoclassical building, between the nineteenth and the twentieth century it hosted leading figures in the artistic and cultural panorama such as Marcel Prevòst, Gabriele D'Annunzio, Eleonora Duse, Matilde Serao and Aristide Sartorio.  
Towards the Roman Gate the Corso ends in the panoramic Mazzini Square which offers a wonderful view over Vallericcia and the Roman countryside till the sea, overlooking the Berninian Southern Bastion. Built by Bernini in 1666 to support the outcrop on which the town stands, the monumental bastion is crowned by a large bull-shaped cornice in peperino stone, and it incorporates walls from the Age of Sulla (beginning of 1st century BCE).

it.name: Centro Storico
description:
Per cogliere la disposizione del Centro Storico è utile ricordare il percorso dell'Appia Antica per chi proveniva da Roma. Da Albano si scendeva nel vallone di Ariccia, e a partire almeno da epoche medioevali, ci si inerpicava fino a Porta Romana, si attraversava tutto il borgo e si sboccava da Porta Napoletana dirigendosi alla volta dell'erta della Catena e del Colle Pardo verso Genzano.  
   
L'attuale Corso di Ariccia quindi, fino alla costruzione del Ponte Monumentale è stato l'asse viario principale dell'abitato.  
   
Ai fasti che la città di Aricia aveva conosciuto nell'antichità, era seguita un'inesorabile decadenza, conseguenza delle invasioni barbariche che avevano reso insicuro il percorso dell'Appia facendo preferire quello della Via della Faiola (attuale Via dei Laghi) per gli spostamenti verso il Lazio meridionale. Priva del grande volano economico rappresentato dall'Appia la *Regina Viarum*, la città era andata man mano spopolandosi fino a quasi essere cancellata dalle mappe dei centri abitati in seguito alle disatrose incursioni saracene che si susseguirono a più riprese fra l'846 e il 916 e soprattutto alla cambiata disposizione viaria.  
   
Nel 1473 quando i Savelli acquisirono per permuta dai monaci di Grottaferrata, il territorio di Ariccia, si impegnarono a ricostruire e rendere abitabili, ruderi inagibili in un territorio pressoché abbandonato. L'attuale Centro Storico nelle sue unità abitative più antiche risale a questo periodo di rinascita, per quanto occupi parte dell'antica acropoli di Aricia e quindi sicuramente testimone di vestigia millenarie. Le risistemazioni seicentesche grazie al disegno urbanistico berniniano, diedero lustro all'abitato oltre che nei suoi aspetti più splendidamente scenografici della Piazza di Corte anche nell'assetto dell'asse viario principale con la sistemazione dei possenti bastioni meridionali e della Porta Romana, del Complesso di San Nicola di Bari e infine della Porta Napoletana.  
Il Corso, attuale Corso Garibaldi, non ha mai smesso dalla fine del '500 in poi di arricchirsi di palazzi signorili, come nel caso del Palazzo Primoli (piazza della Repubblica nn. 4-10),  già Casino Kaisermann, acquistato nella prima metà dell'800 da Carlo Luciano Bonaparte principe di Canino, fratello di Napoleone che  pervenne per eredità ai Conti Primoli. Tipico edificio di gusto neoclassico, ospitò a cavallo dell'Otto-Novecento, personaggi di primo piano nel panorama artistico e culturale come Marcel Prevòst, Gabriele D'Annunzio, Eleonora Duse, Matilde Serao e Aristide Sartorio.  
   
Il Corso sbocca verso Porta Romana nella panoramica Piazza Mazzini che offre un meraviglioso belvedere con veduta su Vallericcia e la campagna romana fino al mare, dominando il berniniano Bastione Meridionale. Bernini costruì il monumentale bastione nel 1666 a sostegno dello sperone su cui sorge l'abitato, l'opera coronata da un grosso cornicione a toro in peperino, ingloba murature di età sillana.
