en.name: Septum Nose Ring
description:
This is a nose ring worn through the nasal septum, known as an *arawak* or *arabek*. Such nose rings serve as a marker of ethnic identity and marital status among elderly Arabic women in the settlement of Jeynau. According to Jeynau residents, this type of jewellery distinguishes them from other Central Asian ethnicities. The section of the ring that passes through the septum is made of flattened silver wire that forms a crescent shape, resembling a bow. One end of the septum section is left unattached, and this open end is inscribed with cuneiform carvings and notches. The other end of the septum section is soldered to a length of silver wire that forms the base of the ring. Rather than connecting to the open end of the septum section, the wire curves back upwards and twists around the septum section to form a loop. Within this loop of wire, beads decorate the ring. First, there is a large bead made of a cobalt-coloured semi-precious stone. In nose rings of this kind, the largest blue or green bead is called *latwa tash* (“the guarding stone”), as the nose ring is traditionally understood to be a guarding amulet. Working outwards from the *latwa tash*, there is also a spiral of silver wire, a smaller bead made of a coral-like stone, and another spiral of silver wire. Typically, the septum nose ring can be used to secure a face veil. Some Jeynau women instead wear a chain connecting their nose ring to their temple pendant as a symbolic replacement of the face veil; veils are not widespread in Bedouin communities.  
Arab settlers brought the tradition of the septum nose ring to Central Asia. Due to the Arab conquests, Arab tribes established settlements in northwest Arabia, along the Great Silk Road, and ultimately in the region now known as Uzbekistan by the 10th/16th century. These tribes can be traced back to modern-day Afghanistan, specifically the cities of Aghan Balkh, Shibarghan, and Andkhoy. A close parallel to Jeynau septum nose rings was recorded in the Dhofar Governorate (the Sultanate of Oman). The Dhofar septum nose ring is called a *khasafa* or *khasama*, and it indicated girls’ marital status; at puberty a girl's nasal septum was pierced for the nose ring she would wear once wed.

en.name: *Patrona Hungariae sending St. Michael to Fight Against the Turks*
description:
In 1739, the Catholic convent in Sopron commissioned Martino Altomonte – a first-generation member of the Austrian High Baroque – to paint a picture for the high altar in St. Michael's Church. He passed the commission onto his son and collaborator, Bartolomeo. The Altomontes, who specialised in large church paintings, historical and triumphal compositions and frescoes, worked in the Italian Baroque tradition. Martino, although of Tyrolean stock, was born in Naples. He used an Italian version of his real name, Hohenberg, and first used his assumed name at the Polish court, where he painted compositions about the hereditary rulers. Later he was active in Vienna. His son, Bartolomeo, was a pupil of Solimena in Naples for two years.  
The vast altarpiece for Sopron echoes one of Francesco Solimena's (d. 1747) most popular creations, the fresco he painted in the San Domenico Maggiore in Naples in 1709. Bartolomeo continued to make use of details from Solimena's repertoire in his other works representing the Holy Trinity, St. Dominic with other saints, and the defeated heretics.  
In this picture, he adapted the subject to meet the wishes of his employers. The Virgin is represented as the patron saint of Hungary (indicated by the Hungarian coat of arms below her right hand), and the defeated are depicted as Turks wearing clothes and arms painted with pedantic accuracy. The impressive multi-coloured altarpiece, painted in the last years of the so-called Balkan campaign, illustrated for the faithful their release from Turkish rule – by then gradually becoming a reality – a notion suggested in the lower part of the picture by a battle scene, in the upper part by celestial rejoicing.

Although this large altarpiece borrows motifs from Bartolomeo's teacher, Francesco Solimena's, painting in Naples the subject matter has a Hungarian actuality.

en.name: Ruins of Cerro da Vila
description:
This archaeological site has been known since the last century, and its systematic excavation began little more than 30 years ago, when the building of the great Vilamoura tourist complex was first started. Since then, a substantial part of a Roman villa has been unearthed, which clearly remained inhabited until the period of the *Caliph*s (4th/10th-5th/11th centuries).  
The mosaics and the remnants of what were once imposing Roman baths are the most visible aspects of this carefully preserved archaeological site. Islamic influence is seen in the artefacts collected from various trenches and ditches, which are currently on display at the Loulé Archaeological Museum, as well as at the Vilamoura Archaeological Centre. Cerro da Vila is also a beacon site for Islamic archaeology in Portugal. It was here, initially, that attention was directed to the evidence of mediaeval occupation at a Roman site. Also it was here that the first systematic study was made of a collection of Islamic ceramics, which, besides a number of luxurious green and manganese and *cuerda seca* pieces, also contains popular locally made pieces. Amongst the latter pieces, artefacts from the archaic tradition predominate, decorated with a reticulated geometrical pattern with a white or red *engobe* or slip. A special mention should also be made of the glazed bowls, which are thought to be 4th/10th and 5th/11th-century pieces and a most significant part of this collection.  
The ruins of Cerro da Vila have been classified as a Site of Public Interest since 1977.

es.name: Ruinas del Cerro da Vila
description:
Yacimiento arqueológico conocido desde el siglo pasado, su excavación sistemática comenzó hace poco más de 30 años, al tiempo de la puesta en marcha del gran complejo turístico de Vilamoura. Desde entonces se ha sacado a la luz una parte sustancial de una *villa* romana que estuvo habitada de manera continuada hasta la época califal (siglos IV/X-V/XI).  
Los mosaicos y los restos de una imponente estructura balnearia son los aspectos de mayor efecto visual en este bien cuidado yacimiento arqueológico. El Islam está presente, a su vez, en los utensilios recogidos en varios silos y fosas, que actualmente se exponen en el Museo Arqueológico de Loulé y en el propio Centro Arqueológico de Vilamoura. El Cerro da Vila es, también, un lugar emblemático para la arqueología islámica en Portugal. Por primera vez se prestó atención a la ocupación medieval en un sitio romano y se procedió al estudio sistemático de una colección de cerámica islámica donde surgen por igual lujosas piezas en *verde y manganeso*, y en *cuerda seca* y materiales de origen popular, de fabricación local. Entre estos predominan los utensilios de tradición arcaica, decorados con un apretado reticulado geometrizante trazado con engobe blanco o rojo. Hay que hacer referencia también a los cuencos vidriados, atribuibles a los siglos IV/X y V/XI, y que constituyen la parte más significativa de esta colección.  
Las ruinas del Cerro da Vila están catalogadas como Inmueble de Interés Público desde 1977.

ar.name: ألبوم مينتو
description: إن ألبوم مينتو هو مجموعة من أربعين صفحة هي الآن متفرقة ومقسمة بين مكتبة تشيستر بيتي ( تسعة عشر صقحة) ومتحف فيكتوريا  وألبرت في لندن (إحدى وعشرين). وهي تتضمن بعض أجمل اللوحات المغولية المنتجة قط وتتألف بشكل أساسي من بورتريهات في وضعية الوقوف لأباطرة وأشخاص آخرين مهمين في البلاط . واللوحات المشمولة هنا هي لجانجير ( حكم خلال 1605 – 27) وهو يحمل كرة وشاه جهان ( حكم خلال 1627 – 58) في ثوب برتقالي ومرشد روحي للمغول وعالم دين معرّف بنقش كتابي باسم محمد رضا كشميري. والحدود المزهرة الرائعة التي تحيط بكل لوحة هي أخاذة مثل اللوحات نفسها.

en.name: Minto Album
description: The Minto Album is a collection of forty, now loose folios, divided between the Chester Beatty Library (nineteen) and the Victoria and Albert Museum, London (twenty-one). It includes some of the finest Mughal paintings ever produced and consists mainly of standing portraits of emperors and other individuals important at court. The paintings included here depict Jahangir (r. 1605–27) holding a globe, Shah Jahan (r. 1627–58) in an orange robe, Shah Jahan and his sons, Mu‘in al-Din Chisti, spiritual guide of the Mughals, and a religious scholar identified by inscription as Muhammad Riza Kashmiri. The magnificent floral borders that surround each painting are as impressive as the paintings themselves.

ar.name: موقد محمول.
description: موقد يتألف من حجرة عليا أو حجرة النار، ومن حاجز مشبك، ومن حجرة دنيا أو مرمدة. حافة الحجرة العليا عمودية مع مرقد أو بروز يمكن تعليب آنية أخرى في داخله؛ كما أن للموقد فوهة مستديرة وجسم أسطواني له بدن مرتفع، وفتحات لتأمين الهواء للنار، وقبضتان عموديتان على شكل شريطة تعلوها زائدة مخروطية الشكل. المشواة محدبة مع فتحات دائرية تؤمن الاتصال مابين الحجرة العليا والمرمدة التي تأخذ شكلاً شبه أسطواني. وللموقد فتحة بيضوية وقاعدة مسطحة؛ وهو مزين بحبل ظفري الشكل في منطقة البدن، وبثلاثة سطور متوازية محزوزة ومتموجة؛ وبدهان أبيض على أرضية محمرّة يرسم خطوطاً متموجة عمودية وأفقية متداخلة. كما تبدو على القطعة آثار عديدة للنار تعود لاستخدامها كفرن صغير أو كموقد منقول يفيد في الطبخ أو في تدفئة مكان ما. قطعة مرمّمة.

آنية مطبخ ترجع إلى الفترة الموحدية؛ ومن المحتمل أن تكون نتاجا محليا.  
موقد مكون من حجرة علوية أو حجرة النار، ومن حاجز مشبك ومن حجرة سفلية (أو مرمدة)، وهو صنف استعمل حتى أيامنا هذه في هذه الجهة.
dynasty: الفترة الموحدية، العقود الأولى من القرن 7 الهجري / القرن 13 الميلادي
keywords: حياة يومية؛ نار.
materials: فخار عادي من عجينة تميل إلى الأحمر نصف مرصوصة، مقولبة بدورة دولاب سريعة، ومشوية في وسط متناوب أكسدة / تخفيض.
tags: فخار عادي من عجينة تميل إلى الأحمر نصف مرصوصة، مقولبة بدورة دولاب سريعة، ومشوية في وسط متناوب أكسدة / تخفيض.

en.name: Portable stove.
description: A portable stove consisting of an upper or fire chamber, a grate and a lower chamber or ash collector. The upper chamber has a vertical rim or moulding into which another object is fitted, a circular mouth, a cylindrical body with sharp carination, holes to ventilate the fire and two vertical strap handles with a conical protuberance at the top. The grate is convex with circular openings between the upper chamber and the ash collector, which is almost cylindrical with an oval opening and flat base. It is decorated with a cord of impressed fingernail marks at the point of carination, three parallel wavy incised lines and white paint on a reddish background which traces interlacing vertical and horizontal lines. The object has many fire marks from its use as a portable stove for cooking or heating. The object has been restored.

Kitchen utensil from the Almohad era, probably produced locally. The stove consists of an upper (or fire) chamber, a grill and a lower (or ash) chamber. This type of item has been used up to the present day in this region.
dates: Hegira early 7th century / AD early 13th century.
keywords: fire; daily life; kitchenware; domestic vessels; furnishing
materials: Common ceramic made from moderately fine reddish paste, modelled on a potter’s wheel and fired in an alternating oxidising and reducing atmosphere.
tags: Common ceramic made from moderately fine reddish paste, modelled on a potter’s wheel and fired in an alternating oxidising and reducing atmosphere.
partner: Archaeological Area and Museum of Mertola

es.name: Anafe.
description: Anafe compuesto por una cámara superior o cámara de fuego, una rejilla y una cámara inferior o cenicero. La cámara superior presenta borde vertical con una cama o moldura en donde encajar otro objeto, boca circular, cuerpo cilíndrico con carena alta, orificios para airear la lumbre y dos asas verticales de cinta con apéndice cónico superior. La parrilla es convexa con orificios circulares que comunican la cámara superior con el cenicero que es casi cilíndrico con una abertura ovalada y base plana. Está ornamentado con un cordón ungulado en la carena, tres líneas incisas onduladas paralelas y pintura blanca sobre fondo rojizo que dibuja trazos ondulados verticales y horizontales entrecruzados. La pieza presenta abundantes marcas de fuego dejadas por su uso como anafe u hornillo portátil para cocinar o caldear ambientes. Pieza restaurada.

Utensilio de cocina de probable fabricación local. Está formado por una cámara superior o cámara de fuego, una rejilla y una cámara inferior o cenicero. Se trata de un tipo de pieza empleado hasta nuestros días en esta región.
dates: Primeras décadas del silgo VII H. / XIII d. C.
keywords: anafe; Mértola; almohades; fuego; vida cotidiana
materials: Cerámica común de pasta rojiza semicompacta, modelada a torno rápido, y cocida en atmósfera que alternó la oxidación y la reducción.
tags: Cerámica común de pasta rojiza semicompacta, modelada a torno rápido, y cocida en atmósfera que alternó la oxidación y la reducción.
partner: Área Arqueológica y Museo de Mértola

fr.name: Fourneau portatif.
description: Fourneau composé d'une chambre supérieure ou chambre à feu, d'une petite grille et d'une chambre inférieure ou cendrier. La chambre supérieure présente un bord vertical avec un lit ou moulure dans laquelle on peut emboîter un autre objet, une bouche circulaire, un corps cylindrique à carène haute, des orifices pour fournir de l'air au feu et deux anses verticales en ruban surmontées d'un appendice conique. Le gril est convexe, avec des orifices circulaires qui font communiquer la chambre supérieure avec le cendrier presque cylindrique ; il possède une ouverture en ovale et une base plate. Le fourneau est orné d'un cordon ongulé dans la carène, de trois lignes parallèles incisées et ondulées, et d'une peinture blanche sur fond rougeâtre qui dessine des traits ondulés verticaux et horizontaux entrecroisés. La pièce présente de nombreuses traces de feu dues à son utilisation comme petit four ou réchaud portable pour cuisiner ou réchauffer un endroit. Pièce restaurée.

Ustensile de cuisine de la période almohade, probablement de production locale. Fourneau composé d'une chambre supérieure ou chambre à feu, d'une petite grille et d'une chambre inférieure (ou à cendres). Ce type d'article a été utilisé jusqu'à nos jours dans cette région.
dates: Premières décennies du VIIe siècle H (du XIIIe siècle J.-C.).
keywords: vie quotidienne ; feu
materials: Céramique commune en pâte rougeâtre mi-compacte, modelée au tour rapide ; cuisson en atmosphère alternée oxydation/réduction.
tags: Céramique commune en pâte rougeâtre mi-compacte, modelée au tour rapide

pt.name: Fogareiro.
description: Fogareiro composto por uma câmara superior ou câmara de fogo, uma grade e uma câmara inferior ou cinzeiro. A câmara superior apresenta bordo vertical com uma moldura onde se encaixava outro objecto, boca circular, corpo cilíndrico com carena alta, orificios para arejar o lume e duas asas verticais com apêndice cónico superior. A grade é convexa com orificios circulares que comunicam a câmara superior com o cinzeiro, que é quase cilíndrico com uma abertura ovalada e base plana. Está ornamentado con um cordão na carena, três linhas incisas onduladas paralelas e pintura branca sobre fundo avermelhado com traços ondulados verticais e horizontais entrecruzados. A peça apresenta abundantes marcas de fogo deixadas pelo seu uso como fogareiro ou pequeno forno portátil para cozinhar ou aquecer ambientes. Peça restaurada.

Utensílio de cozinha do período almóada (primeiras décadas do século VII AH/ XIII AD), de provável fabrico local. O fogareiro é composto por uma câmara superior ou câmara de fogo, por uma grade e por uma câmara inferior ou cinzeiro. Trata-se de um tipo de peça usado até aos nossos dias nesta região.
dates: Primeiras décadas do VII AH / primeras décadas do XIII AD.
keywords: fogo; vida quotidiana
materials: Cerâmica comum de pasta avermelhada semi-compacta, modelada em torno rápido, e cozida em atmosfera que alternou a oxidação e a redução.
tags: Cerâmica comum de pasta avermelhada semi-compacta, modelada em torno rápido, e cozida em atmosfera que alternou a oxidação e a redução.

de.name: Kanzel
description: Die frei über einen Holzkern stuckierte Kanzel zählt zu den bemerkenswertesten Rokokokanzeln im ganzen süddeutschen Sprachraum. Vor allem der aufragende Schalldeckel mit seinen frei wie Wellen emporschlagenden Rocaillen, ist ein außergewöhnliches Meisterstück der Stuckateurskunst. In die Rocaillen des Deckels fügen sich die Symbole für die Predigt – Gesetzestafeln, Flammenschwert und Geisttaube – ein, während der Kanzelkorb rein ornamental gestaltet ist.

en.name: Pulpit
description: The pulpit, with its wooden core freely ornamented with stucco is one of the most remarkable Rococo pulpits in the entire south German-speaking region. An exemplary feature is the towering baldachin with its rocaille work ascending freely like waves, a masterpiece of the stucco mason’s art. The rocaille work of the baldachin contains symbols of the sermon – Tablets of the Law, flaming sword and the holy spirit in the form of a dove – while the pulpit itself has a purely ornamental design.
place: East side of the nave, central pillar

en.name: St Justa's lift
short_description:
This revivalist example of the 1900 iron architecture for transportation foregrounds amidst Lisbon Downtown skyline. The 45 m high lift includes a gangway with Neo-gothic decoration 2 towers with 7 floors, each one with a cabin for 24 passengers. Inside they are covered with wood and mirrors while each floor has its own decoration. The balance between the cabins is provided by a steel cable and was initially water moved.  
Foreseen since 1874 it aimed to overcome the 25 metres gap between Ouro and Carmo Streets thus easing the pedestrian’ traffic between the hills of the Lisbon centre. The inauguration of the gangway by King Carlos I was held in 1901 and the lift itself started to be fully operational in 1902 and electrified in 1907.  
It is classified as a national monument.
artist: Engineer Raul Mesnier du Ponsard (1849–1914 Porto/Inhambane); master builder and Foreman of the building sites: Manuel Cardoso (n.d.)
history: Built between 1890–1892 it will be inaugurated still unfinished by Royal Prince Afonso of Braganza (1865–1920) on the 18th August 1892.
keywords: Lisbon; Urban innovation; transportation; Urban iron architecture

en.name: Le Boulevard El-Nassr, Damas (El-Nassr Boulevard, Damascus)
description: Al Nasr Street in Damascus, previously known as Jamal Pasha Street, was renamed Al Nasr (Arabic: "Victory") in 1919. The street extends between the commercial centre near Suq al-Hamidiyya and the Hijaz Railway Station. Although an earlier route existed on the site, it was widened and monumentalized during the First World War under Jamal Pasha, the Military Governor of Ottoman Syria. The project formed part of a broader programme of urban transformation in the Ottoman provinces. The printed caption reads “Damas. — Le Boulevard El-Nassr un jour de fête,” ("Damascus—A Day of Celebration on El-Nassr Boulevard") and names the Damascus publishers Soubhi S. et Munir Aita. During this celebration, the street functioned as a gathering place on a scale that would have been difficult to accommodate within the narrow streets of Damascus's historic urban fabric. Soubhi and Munir Aita were photographers and imprint publishers active in Damascus, particularly during the 1920s.
keywords: Syria; Route; Travel; festival

holder: Digital Library of Periodicals, Lisbon Municipality
keywords: Tourism; Pena Palace; 19th century; Sintra

ar.name: لوحة مكونة من تسع بلاطات
description: تظهر اللوحة المقطع العرضي ذو الطراز الخاص للمسجد النبوي في المدينة. وأسفل الصف العلوي يوجد قوس مركزي ثنائي وقوسين جانبيين محمولين على أربعة أعمدة حلزونية جميلة ومتوجة بواسطة هلال. ويوجد ثلاثة مصابيح مسجد معلقة بشكل متوافق مع المركز لقناطر الأقواس. وفي الوسط يوجد لفة/درجة مركزية التي تحمل نقش ""العزة لله"".
dates: القرن الحادي عشر هجري / القرن السابع عشر الميلادي
