en.name: Small Octagonal Pavilion Tent
description:
A tent comprising eight contiguous panels, each measuring 211cm x 135cm, and an octagonal canopy of eight triangular pieces. The plain-weave cotton exterior is embroidered with silk and metallic yarns, and the interior is lined with woven silk panels.  
The exterior of the tent is a plain-weave cotton, which is resistant to sunlight and less likely to be damaged by rain, while the interior is lined with more fragile and luxurious silk fabric. The form of this small pavilion tent inevitably recalls the shape of medieval Iranian octagonal tomb structures or gunbad, whose decorative brickwork frequently includes corner columns or "tent poles."  
One of the eight wall panels is designed to open as an entrance, and the central part of each wall panel is embellished by a fabric "grille" that clearly imitates Persian wooden or metal grille-work. The design provides plenty of shade and privacy coupled with maximum air circulation, and the door panel could be closed for additional privacy.
dates: Hegira Mid 12th to early 13th century / AD late 19th century
keywords: Octagonal; Pavillion; Tent; Textile; Silk; Cotton; Metallic; Yarn; Rasht; Persia; Iran; Asia; Persian

cs.name: Mešní kalich a konvičky
description: Vedle kalichu, zdobeného na emailu malovanými polopostavami řádových světců a konviček opata Zircla vznikly pro korunovaci v augsburské dílně ještě dva další kalichy pro asistující kněze s výjevy ze života a mučení sv. Jana Nepomuckého a pašijí.

en.name: Mass Chalice and Jugs
description: Apart from the chalice decorated with half-figures of the order’s saints painted on enamel, and jugs for Abbot Zirckl, there were two other chalices for assisting priests, with scenes from the Lfe and Torment of St. John of Nepomuk and the Passion, created in the Augsburg workshop for the coronation.

de.name: Sommerhaus, Inneres, Festsaal
description: Der vom Haller Stadtbaumeister Simon Gremblich 1715/16 im Stiftsgarten errichtete Bau diente den Stiftsdamen als Sommerresidenz. Im Zentrum befindet sich der über sieben Fensterachsen reichende Festsaal mit den bedeutenden Wand- und Deckenfresken von der Hand Kaspar Waldmanns. Der Maler wirkte hier gewissermaßen als Architekt und Bildhauer, indem er die gesamten Wände in wuchtigen hochbarocken Bauformen illusionistisch gliederte. Diese bilden einen Rahmen für das theologische Bildprogramm mit biblischen Frauenfiguren, Vorbilder für die Stiftsdamen, während im Deckenfeld die Stifterin selbst, Erzherzogin Magdalena, vor der hl. Dreifaltigkeit erscheint.

en.name: Summerhouse, interior, festive hall
description: The building erected in the convent garden by Hall’s master builder Simon Gremblich in 1715/16, served the ladies of the endowment as a summer residence. At its centre is located the festive hall extending across seven window axes with its important wall and ceiling frescos from the hand of Kaspar Waldmann. Here the painter operated, in a manner of speaking, as both architect and sculptor, structuring all the walls in illusionistic depictions of High Baroque architectural forms. These form a framework for the theological programme of images of female biblical figures – role models for the ladies of the endowment – while in the ceiling panel, the benefactress herself, Archduchess Magdalena appears before the Holy Trinity.

de.name: Allerheiligenkapelle
description: Ein stuckierter, von Engeln aufgezogener Baldachin gibt den Blick frei auf einen Reliquienaltar, der seitlich in vier Schaukästen die Skelette der als heilig verehrten Äbte Wigpertus, Nidgarius, Adalbero und Thosso präsentiert. Über das zentrale Kreuzigungsbild werden diese in die Nachfolge Christi gestellt.
artist: Stuck: Matthias Lotter; Deckenfresko: Johann Georg Knappich (1637-1704); Altar: Johann Georg Schmierer

en.name: Chapel of All Saints
description: Under a stuccoed baldachin, lifted by angels, the altar of relics is presented to the believers. To its sides, the skeletons of the Four Holy Abbots: Wigpertus, Nidgarius, Adalbero and Thosse are presented in showcases. The connection of their dead bodies with an image of the Crucifixion suggests their successful emulation of Christ.
artist: Matthias Lotter [n.d.]; Johann Georg Knappich (1637–1704); Johann Georg Schmierer [n.d.]
partner: University of Munich, Institute of Art History

en.name: *Nosocomium* \[Latin: Hospital\]
short_description: Silvio Rotta was introduced to painting by his father and, in his early years, produced mainly watercolours, genre compositions inspired by Venetian popular customs. In 1887, after an illness, the production of the artist underwent a radical change ad began to show social realism through the depiction of the insane. *Nosocomium* represents a psychiatric hospital where poor and sick were hosted and nursed. The scale of the canvas is accentuated by the diagonal of the benches and the path. The painting won awards at the 1895 Biennale of Venice and is now recognised as one of the most important works by Rotta. The scene’s realism offers a merciless analysis and public complaint about the patients’ living conditions. Caring of poor and sick was an important issue during the 19th century and a law to control hospitals and mental institution was discussed in those years.
keywords: Italian painters; city; urban space; segregation; medicine; disease; poverty; illness; life expectancy; psychiatry; social changes; scientific development; social topics; post-unitarian Italian society; Positivism; celebration of science; exposition
partner: MIBACT | National Gallery of Modern Art (GNAM)

en.name: Jordan National Gallery of Fine Arts Park
names: Previously known as the *Jabal al-Luweibdeh* Park
description:
The park covers an area of approximately 7500 square metres and provides a pleasant green space surrounded by residences in what was once one of Amman's most elegant neighbourhoods. Following the rehabilitation programme of the early 2000s, the park incorporates the domain of the Jordan National Gallery of Fine Arts, presenting different areas of the garden that have been fully reinterpreted in terms of sustainability and contemporary landscape architecture.  
  
The new public installations include outdoor sculpture displays, children's play areas, a performance/exhibition space, a café/restaurant and model educational gardens demonstrating water-conservation landscape practices. It also includes a Japanese garden, elaborated in partnership with the Japanese Embassy in Amman, and an Andalusian fountain, also a fruit of the collaboration with the Spanish Embassy in Amman.  
  
The park also includes a 160 cubic metre reservoir that harvests rainwater for use in a drip irrigation system. All existing trees and mature ornamental plants were carefully preserved and incorporated into the new landscape design. To enhance the park’s vegetation, a diverse selection of drought-tolerant trees, ornamental species and ground covers were introduced to complement the original greenery. Additionally, a specialised variety of turf grass (Bermuda grass) has been introduced in select areas to further reduce water usage.  
  
Radiating from the platform, the pathways retrace the layout of the park’s original circulation routes. The irregular stone paving panels from the former design have been preserved to maintain a visual and tactile connection to the park’s historic character.
history: Originally known as *Jabal al-Luweibdeh* Park, the National Gallery of Fine Arts Park was established in AH 1371 / AD 1953 as one of the first public parks in Amman. Situated in one of the city’s oldest neighbourhoods, it became a cherished meeting place and an early example of civic planning in Jordan’s growing capital. However, over time, neglect and insufficient maintenance led to its deterioration. In AH 1423 / AD 2002, the Center for the Study of the Built Environment (CSBE) proposed comprehensive rehabilitation works. In collaboration with the Greater Amman Municipality, work began in the spring of AH 1424 / AD 2004 and was completed in AH Rabi 1426 / AD May 2005. The park was officially renamed to emphasise its integration with the Jordan National Gallery of Fine Arts, linking the original gallery building and its new extension. The entire complex was inaugurated under the royal patronage of Their Majesties King Abdullah and Queen Rania, restoring the park as both a public amenity and a model of sustainable landscape design. In AH 1437 / AD 2016, the park won a Global Gold award by Green World Organisation in "Sustainability".
keywords: Park; Amma; Jordan; National Gallery; Sustentability; Water; Rehabilitation
partner: Jordan National Gallery of Fine Arts

en.name: *Muhammad 'Ali Pasha*
short_description: Muhammad 'Ali Pasha, founder of Modern Egypt and Wali of Egypt in 1805. He was the head of the Alawiyya Dynasty that ruled Egypt from 1805 to 1952, and founder of modern Egypt. He came to Egypt in 1799 as part of a military unit to fight with the Turks – and the help of the British – to drive the French out of Egypt. However, the Turkish forces were defeated in 1799 in the Battle of Abu Qir.
keywords: Ruling Family; Rulers of Egypt; The Alawiyya Dynasty; Turks; The Ruling Elite

short_description: L'apprentissage de l'écriture dans les écoles coraniques se fait grâce à des tablettes sur lesquelles on copie des versets du Coran, que l'on effacera ensuite avec précaution.

en.name: Funduq of the Blacksmiths
description:
The term *funduq*, which signifies an establishment whose character is mainly economic, was at first shared by both the Muslim East and the Muslim West, but in the Muslim East it was eclipsed in the 4th/10th century by the terms *khan* and *wikala*.  
*Funduq, khan, wikala* – although they possess certain architectural differences, their plans are those of a *caravanserai* composed essentially of a huge courtyard surrounded by buildings and with an inn. Caravans would stop there. Funduqs appeared in Sfax early on. Ibn Hawqal, in the 4th/10th century, is the first to have notified us of their existence in this town.  
Situated inside the *medina*, near Bab al-Jibli and the caravan station, the Funduq of the Blacksmiths derives its name from the *suq* in which it is located. Its name has become more significant since the municipality moved blacksmiths and coppersmiths (boil-ermakers) there.  
Dilapidated during the Hafsid era, and rebuilt and restored in the 12th/18th century, it stands as the only remaining reminder of the neighbourhood of the *funduq*s, *Humat al-Fanadiq*, which was made up of similar establishments and was very active during the 12th/18th century.  
The form taken by the Funduq of the Blacksmiths is a classic one. A narrow hallway-corridor, *sqifa*, leads to a vast courtyard surrounded by porticoes, under which sit shops. Staircases, situated in this same hallway, lead to a first floor of 25 rooms or *ghorfa*s. The ground floor was reserved for the travellers’ animals and their goods, whilst the upper floor served as an inn.  
The *funduq* is built along the lines of traditional masonry based on time-honoured techniques, using local materials. The conchitic sandstone imported from the Mahdia region is used in bulk for the construction of door frames, arches and pillars. Having calculated the available materials, the width of the spaces required to be covered, and the best means of maximising thermal regulation, the roof coverings are made in the form of groined vaults for the *sqifa*, in thuja-wood joists for the staircases and in a light timber framework for the porticoes. As such, the *funduq* represents every kind of roofing material used previously in Sfax.  
In the Funduq of the Blacksmiths, as in other historic Sfaxian monuments, the freestone, the arches, the diagonally ribbed ceilings and the visible joists are all structural elements; they are also, within this type of monument, the only decorative elements capable of attracting attention. Compared to the *khans* of the East, the Funduq of the Blacksmiths appears modest, lacking in all ornamentation, and is located closer to *suq*s and to *qaysariya*s than to other monuments.

es.name: Funduq de los Herreros
description:
El término *funduq* designa un establecimiento más bien económico y en principio era utilizado tanto en Oriente como en Occidente. Sin embargo en Oriente, a partir del siglo IV/X, se empezaron a utilizar los términos *jan* y *wukala*.  
*Funduq*, *jan* y *wukala*, aunque mantienen algunas diferencias arquitectónicas, designan una parada de caravanas compuesta esencialmente de un amplio patio rodeado  
de edificios y de una hostería. Los *funduq*s aparecen desde muy pronto en Sfax, y es Ibn Hawqal, en el siglo IV/X, el primero que nos señala su existencia.  
Situado en el interior de la *medina*, próximo a la Bab el-Yibli y a la estación caravanera, el *funduq* de los Herreros toma su nombre del zoco en el que se encuentra. Su apelación se ha convertido en algo significativo desde que el Ayuntamiento instaló en él a los forjadores y a los caldereros.  
Muy deteriorado en época hafsí, reconstruido y restaurado en el siglo XII/XVIII, es el único testigo que nos queda del barrio de los funduqs (*humat el-fanadiq*), formado por varios establecimientos similares y muy activos durante el siglo XII/XVIII.  
La forma del *funduq* de los herreros es clásica. Un vestíbulo o *sqifa* en un corredor conduce hasta un amplio patio rodeado con pórticos, sobre los cuales se abren los almacenes. Las escaleras, situadas en el propio vestíbulo, conducen a un primer piso formado por 25 habitaciones: las *gurfa*s. El piso bajo estaba reservado a los animales de carga de los viajeros y a sus mercancías; el primer piso hacía la función de hotel.  
El *funduq* está construido según los procedimientos de la albañilería tradicional, basada en técnicas seculares en las que se utilizan materiales locales. El gres conchífero, importado de la región de Mahdia, se utiliza en grandes bloques para los marcos de puertas, arcos y pilares. Teniendo en cuenta los materiales utilizados, la amplitud de los espacios que deben cubrirse y la necesidad de obtener una regulación térmica adecuada, las cubiertas han sido realizadas con bóvedas de aristas en la *sqifa*, con vigas de tuya en las escaleras y con un armazón de madera ligera en los pórticos. De esta forma, este *funduq* presenta todos los tipos de cubiertas utilizados antaño en Sfax.  
En el *funduq* de los Herreros, como en el resto de los monumentos históricos de  
Sfax, las sillerías, los arcos, las cubiertas y las vigas son también elementos esenciales de la estructura. En este tipo de  
monumentos constituyen los únicos elementos decorativos. Si se compara con los janes orientales, el *funduq* de los Herreros parece algo modesto, puesto que está desprovisto de toda ornamentación, de forma que parece más próximo a los zocos y a las *qaysariya*s que a otro tipo de monumento.

fr.name: Fondouk des Forgerons
description:
Le terme fondouk, qui désigne un établissement à caractère plutôt économique, d’abord partagé entre l’Orient et l’Occident musulman, fut éclipsé de l’Orient à partir du IVe/Xe siècle par l’utilisation des termes *khan* et *oukala*.  
Fondouk, *khan*, *oukala*, quoique ayant quelques différences architecturales, désignent le caravansérail composé essentiellement d’une vaste cour entourée de bâtiments et d’une hôtellerie. Les caravanes y faisaient halte. Les fondouks apparaissent très tôt à Sfax. Ibn Hawqal, au IVe/Xe siècle, est le premier à nous signaler leur existence dans cette ville.  
Situé à l’intérieur de la médina, à proximité de Bab el-Jibli et de la station caravanière, le fondouk des Forgerons tire son nom du souk où il se trouve. Son appellation est devenue plus significative depuis que la municipalité y a installé des forgerons et des chaudronniers.  
Délabré à l’époque hafside, réaménagé et restauré au XIIe/XVIIIe siècle, il reste le seul témoin du quartier des fondouks, Houma el-Fanadiq, formé d’établissements semblables et très actifs au cours du XIIe/XVIIIe.  
La forme du fondouk des Forgerons est classique. Un vestibule, ou *sqifa*, en couloir conduit à une vaste cour entourée de portiques sous lesquels ouvrent des magasins. Des escaliers, situés dans ce même vestibule, conduisent au premier étage formé de 25 chambres, les *ghorfa*s. Le rezde- chaussée était réservé aux animaux des voyageurs et à leurs marchandises, le premier étage jouait le rôle d’hôtellerie. Le fondouk est construit selon les procédés de la maçonnerie traditionnelle basés sur des techniques séculaires, utilisant les matériaux locaux. Le grès coquiller importé de la région de Mahdia est utilisé en gros appareil pour réaliser des encadrements de portes, des arcs et des piliers. Compte tenu des matériaux disponibles, de la largeur des espaces à couvrir, de la façon d’aboutir à une meilleure régulation thermique, les couvertures sont réalisées en voûtes d’arêtes dans la *sqifa*, en solive de thuya pour les escaliers ou en charpente de bois léger pour les portiques. Ainsi, ce fondouk présente tous les types de couverture utilisés autrefois à Sfax.  
Au fondouk des Forgerons, comme dans le reste des monuments historiques sfaxiens, les pierres de taille, les arcs, les couvertures en ogives et les solives apparentes sont des éléments de la structure; ils sont aussi, dans ce type de monuments, les seuls éléments décoratifs capables d’attirer l’attention. Comparativement aux *khan*s orientaux, le fondouk des Forgerons apparaît modeste, dépouillé de toute ornementation, plus proche des souks et des *qaysariya*s que des autres monuments.

ar.name: سجادة أسبانية.
description:
تنتمي هذه السجادة الكبيرة والمحفوظة في أجزاء منها، إلى مجموعة من السجاد الأسباني في القرن الخامس عشر الذي كان مزوّداً بشعار عائلة إنريكس. إذ تدل المناظر المستخدمة والألوان والمظهر العام على انتماء هذه السجادة لهذه المجموعة. ويعتقد أن هذا النوع من السجاد كان يصنع في المدينة الأسبانية ليتور في النصف الثاني من القرن الخامس عشر. ويميز هذه السجادة، والسجاد الأسباني عامة، العقدة الأسبانية المستخدمة.  
كان يظن بداية أن هذا النوع من السجاد، الذي يسمى سجاد المدجَّن في أسبانيا، من عمل حرفيين شرقيين لأشخاص أسبانيين. ولكن هذه السجادات الأسبانية تتميز بتغييرات بالغة في المبدأ الذي يعتمد عليه تقسيم نماذج الرسوم عما هو معروف عن سجاد الدول الإسلامية، بحيث لا يمكن افتراض علاقة مباشرة بين النوعين.  
تتكون رسوم الحقل الداخلي من منظر واحد متكرر ومستمر يتكون من نجمة سداسية على أرضية زرقاء مسدّسة الأضلاع. وتتناوب رسوم العصافير مع الورود في الحقول ذات الأشكال المعيّنة التي تنشأ نتيجة هذا التكرار. ويحيط بالحقل الداخلي أربع حواشٍ مختلفة العرض، فالحاشية الداخلية عبارة عن تعاريج تليها نجوم مضفرة ومتراصفة في الحاشية التالية، ثم أزهار متراصة في الحاشية الثالثة، تليها الحاشية الخارجية المكونة من مناظر تقارب الكتابة بالخط الكوفي على أرضية زرقاء. وتتناوب أحرف طويلة عليها عقفات مع مثلثات تظهر فيما بينها مناظر حيوانية مشكلة على نمط الشعارات (طواوييس وبط وأسود وحيوانات أخرى) بالإضافة إلى رسوم هندسية ومعينات مملوءة بالعقفات.  
كذلك في البلدان الإسلامية فإن الشعارات المنسوجة على شكل عقدي تدل على أن هذا السجاد تم بناء على طلب خاص. وهناك سجادة عثمانية محفوظة في السويد عليها شعار أحد القساوسة، كما هناك سجادات عثمانية أخرى تحمل شعارات عائلات من جنوة. وهذا دليل هام على التجارة الواسعة والمتشعبة في بلاد حوض البحر المتوسط كلها.

من قبل كانت هذه السجّادة بطول خمسة أمتار. باحتها الداخلية مُزيَّنة بقالب نجمي صغير. أما المحيط الخارجي، الذي يُذكِّر بالنقوش الكوفية، فزاخر برسوم حيوانية، مثل الأسود وطيور البط، مما يجعلها نقيضة ذات شأن للسجاجيد المملوكية والعثمانية.
dates: النصف الثاني من القرن التاسع/ النصف الثاني من القرن الخامس عشر؟
keywords: سجادة أسبانية؛ سجادة يدوية.
partner: متحف الفن الإسلامي في متحف بيرغامون ، المتاحف الحكومية

de.name: Spanischer Teppich.
description: Der große, fragmentarische Teppich gehört zu einer Gruppe von spanischen Teppichen des 15. Jh., die mit Wappen der Familie Enriquez versehen sind. Sowohl die verwendeten Motive als auch die Farbigkeit und die Gesamterscheinung zeigen, dass dieser Teppich zu dieser Gruppe gehört. Sie wurde wahrscheinlich in der spanischen Stadt Letur in der zweiten Hälfte des 15. Jh. geknüpft. Charakteristisch für diesen wie auch für andere spanische Teppiche ist die Knüpfung mit dem spanischen Knoten. Es wurde vermutet, dass Teppiche dieser Art, die als Mudejar-Teppiche bezeichnet wurden, Arbeiten orientalischer Handwerker für spanische Auftraggeber waren. Allerdings zeigen diese spanischen Teppiche bereits weitgehende Veränderungen der Prinzipien der Musterglierderung wie sie von Teppichen aus islamischen Ländern bekannt sind, so dass keine direkte Verbindung mehr anzunehmen ist. Das Muster des Innenfeldes besteht aus der fortlaufenden Reihung eines einzigen Motives: Ein sechsstrahliger Stern in einem blaugrundigem Sechseck wird kontinuierlich wiederholt. In den entstehenden Rauten wechseln Vögel mit Rosetten. Vier unterschiedlich breite Bordüren rahmen das Innenfeld. Von Innen nach Außen sind dies eine Zickzackbordüre, aneinandergereihte Flechtsterne, gereihte Blüten, und schließlich in der äußeren Bordüre auf blauem Grund Motive, die Schriftzeichen im Kufi-Duktus angenähert sind. Lange Buchstaben sind mit Haken besetzt und alternieren mit spitzen Dreiecken und in deren Zwischenräumen sowohl Tiermotive in heraldischer Stilisierung (Pfauen, Enten, Löwen etc.) als auch geometrische Motive wie hakenbesetzte Rauten vorkommen. Eingeknüpfte Wappen sind auch in islamischen Ländern ein Merkmal für eine Auftragsarbeit. So trägt ein in Schweden aufbewahrter osmanischer Teppich das Wappen eines Bischofs oder andere osmanische Teppiche tragen Wappen Genueser Familien. Sie sind ein wichtiges Indiz für den weitverzweigten Mittelmeerhandel.

Dieser Teppich war ursprünglich mehr als fünf Meter lang. Im inneren Feld findet sich ein Muster mit kleinen Sternen. Der Rahmen, der an Kufi-Inschriften erinnert, ist mit Tiermotiven – u.a. Löwen, Enten – ausgefüllt und bildet so einen deutlichen Kontrast zu mamlukischen oder osmanischen Teppichen.
keywords: Spanische Teppiche; Knüpfteppiche
partner: Museum für Islamische Kunst, Pergamon Museum

en.name: Spanish carpet.
description:
This large fragmented carpet belongs to a group of Spanish carpets from the AH 9th / AD 15th century that feature the coats of arms of the Enriquez family. The motifs used in the carpet, as well as its colours and entire appearance, indicate that it belongs to this group. They were probably made in the Spanish town of Letur in the second half of the AH 9th / AD 15th century. The Spanish knots in the weave are a typical characteristic of Spanish carpets, including this one.  
It was thought that carpets of this kind, known as Mudéjar carpets, were made by Oriental craftsmen for Spanish patrons. However, no further direct link can be made, as these Spanish carpets show big changes to the structural principles of carpet patterns in Islamic countries.  
The pattern within the central area is composed of consecutive rows of a single motif: a six-pointed star within a blue hexagon, repeated continuously. Birds and rosettes alternately occupy the diamond-shaped spaces in between. Four borders of different widths frame the central area. Starting from the inner border and moving outwards, the borders are composed of zigzags, interlinked plaited stars, rows of blossoms and, finally, an outer border of motifs recalling *kufic* script on a blue background. Long letters, embellished with hooks, alternate with pointed triangles. Animal motifs in a heraldic style (peacocks, ducks, lions. etc.) and geometrical motifs, such as diamonds decorated with hooks, fill the spaces in between.  
In Islamic countries, coats of arms knotted into carpets indicate that the carpet was commissioned. The coat of arms belonging to a bishop can be seen in an Ottoman carpet that was preserved in Sweden; other Ottoman carpets show the coats of arms of Genoese families. They are an important testimony to the widespread extent of Mediterranean trade.

This carpet was once over five metres long. Its inner field has a small star pattern. The outer border, reminiscent of *kufic* inscriptions, is filled with animal motifs including lions and ducks, and is therefore a considerable contrast to Mamluk or Ottoman carpets.
holder: Museum of Islamic Art at the Pergamon Museum
Museum of Arts and Crafts, Berlin.
dates: Hegira second half of 9th century / AD second half of 15th century.
keywords: Spanish carpets; knot-carpets; kufic; six-pointed star; geometric patterns
partner: Museum of Islamic Art at the Pergamon Museum, State Museums

es.name: Alfombra española.
description:
Fragmento de una gran alfombra perteneciente al grupo de alfombras españolas del siglo IX / XV con el escudo de armas de la familia Enríquez. Los motivos decorativos, los colores y su apariencia en conjunto hacen clasificarla entre las alfombras de ese grupo, probablemente producidas en Letur (Albacete) con el característico anudado español. Se cree que esta clase de alfombras, conocidas como "alfombras mudéjares", fueron tejidas por artesanos orientales para clientes españoles, aunque no puede llevarse más allá la hipótesis, pues muestran muchos cambios respecto a los patrones de alfombras de los países islámicos.  
El diseño del campo central consiste en filas consecutivas de estrellas de seis puntas dentro de un hexágono azul y separadas por espacios romboidales en que alternan aves y rosetas. La decoración de los bordes se compone, de dentro a fuera, de cenefas de zigzags, estrellas de lacería, flores y una inscripción cúfica sobre fondo azul, de altos caracteres adornados con ganchos y triángulos de forma alterna. Los espacios entre caracteres se han rellenado con motivos geométricos (cuadrangulares, romboidales, etc.) y animales heráldicos (pavos reales, patos, leones, etc.).  
En países islámicos, la presencia de escudos de armas en las alfombras indica que se tejieron por encargo. Se conservan alfombras otomanas con escudos de familias genovesas, e incluso una, hoy en Suecia, con el escudo de un obispo, lo cual da una idea del alcance del comercio en el Mediterráneo.

Esta alfombra mediría originalmente cinco metros. El campo central está decorado con un dibujo de pequeñas estrellas repetidas, mientras que el borde parece una reminiscencia de inscripción cúfica, entre cuyos caracteres se han tejido animales como patos o leones. Contrasta considerablemente con alfombras islámicas como las mamelucas y otomanas.
holder: Museo de Arte Islámico del Museo Pergamon
keywords: alfombras españolas; alfombras de nudo
partner: Museo de Arte Islámico en el Museo de Pérgamo, Museos Estatales

fr.name: Tapis espagnol.
description:
Ce grand tapis fragmentaire fait partie d'un groupe de tapis espagnols du IXe siècle H (XVe siècle J.-C.) portant les armoiries de la famille Enriquez. Cette attribution est justifiée par les motifs employés, la polychromie, l'aspect général. Ce tapis a probablement été fabriqué dans la ville espagnole de Letur durant la seconde moitié du IXe siècle H (XVe siècle J.-C.). Tous ces tapis sont caractérisés par l'emploi du nœud espagnol.  
On a pensé jadis que les tapis de cette catégorie, appelés tapis mudéjars, avaient été réalisés par des artisans orientaux pour des commanditaires espagnols. Toutefois, ils présentent déjà de telles divergences d'avec les principes de structuration du motif observés dans les pays islamiques que l'on ne peut légitimement admettre de filiation directe.  
Le champ principal est constitué de la répétition continue d'un même motif : une étoile à six branches dans un octogone à fond bleu. Dans les losanges intercalaires alternent des oiseaux et des rosettes. Quatre bordures de différentes largeurs encadrent le champ : en partant de l'intérieur, une bordure avec motifs en zigzag, une frise d'étoiles d'entrelacs, une frise de fleurs, et enfin, sur la bordure externe, des motifs sur fond bleu qui rappellent l'écriture coufique. De longues lettres se lèvent en crochets et alternent avec des triangles pointus ; les interstices sont garnis d'animaux traités dans une stylisation héraldique (paons, canards, lions, etc.) et de motifs géométriques comme les losanges remplis de crochets.  
Les armoiries insérées dans le tapis sont dans les pays islamiques aussi le signe distinctif d'un travail de commande. Un tapis ottoman conservé en Suède porte le blason d'un évêque, d'autres les armes d'une famille génoise, signe de l'importance du réseau commercial méditerranéen.

Ce tapis mesurait autrefois plus de cinq mètres de long. Son champ intérieur présente un motif de petite étoile. La bordure externe, qui rappelle l'écriture coufique, est remplie de motifs animaliers incluant des lions et des canards, ce qui crée un contraste considérable avec les tapis mamelouks ou ottomans.
dates: seconde moitié du IXe siècle de l’Hégire (seconde moitié du XVe siècle J.-C.).
keywords: tapis espagnols ; tapis à points noués
partner: Musée d’art islamique du Pergamon Museum (Museum für Islamische Kunst)

ar.name: جذاذة من أسطوانة (السنطوانة): كتب عليها آيات قرآنية.
description:
يقع جامع بهلاء بالقرب من قلعة بهلاء، ويرجع البعض تأريخ إنشائه إلى عهد الخليفة عمر بن الخطاب (رضي الله عنه) (13–24هـ/634–644م)، إلا أن أقدم تأريخ مكتوب كشف عنه حتى الآن في إحدى الأسطوانات، وهو يحمل تأريخ (528هـ/33–1134م).  
  
يتكون جامع بهلاء من أسطوانات عديدة، تترابط بعقود طينية، ووظيفتها الأساسية حمل السقف، بالإضافة إلى إضفاء البعد الجمالي، ولها مع الجدران الداخلية للجامع بعدا تاريخيا، وثقافيا، واجتماعيا؛ بما تملؤه من كتابات؛ إذ إنها بمثابة مدونات تأريخية توثق تواريخ مهمة لحوادث جرت في مدينة بهلاء خصوصا، وفي عمان عموما، وتحمل تواريخ العديد من الغزوات، وتواريخ التنصيب، والتأبين لأعيان البلاد، وأسماء الأئمة، والعلماء، والفقهاء، الذين عاشوا في البلاد، أو اشتغلوا بالتدريس في حلقات الجامع، أو الذين زاروا مدينة بهلاء من الساسة، والعلماء، والأدباء.

en.name: Stucco Fragments with Inscription
description: Bahla Grand Mosque, with a construction date attributed to the reign of Caliph Omar bin al-Khattab (13-24 AH / 634-644 AD) is located near Bahla Fort. The mosque has many cylinders connected with mud joints which act as pillars to support the ceiling in addition to their decorative function. The inscriptions on the cylinders and on the inner walls of the mosque have historic, cultural and social importance. They are considered historic registers as they document important events of Bahla and of Oman, including the dates of battles, the elections and deaths of local dignitaries and the names of imams, scientists and scholars who lived in the country, taught at the mosque or visited the town. The oldest written inscription revealed so far on one of the cylinders is marked with the date, 528 AH / 1133–34 AD.

en.name: Turbe al-Bey
description:
Islamic funerary customs, particularly of the Malikite sect, recommends simplicity to its believers, as can be seen by the anonymity of the tombs. The Hanafite Turks had introduced the habit of building elaborate monuments in honour of the dead, which were known as *turbe*s or *turbet*s. The Turbe al-Bey, built during the reign of ‘Ali Pasha II (1171/1758–1195/1781), houses the burial place of the Princely Husaynite family. It has a imposing ochre sandstone facade from which pilasters, as well as Italian-styled stone entablatures sculpted in low-relief floral motifs, branch out.  
It is interesting to compare this facade to that of Turbe al-Fellari which is situated in the opposite corner. Dating from the 12th/18th century, this monument subscribes to local tradition. Each of its three facades is furnished with a blind arcature, and the median arch is punctured by a saddle-barred window which is surmounted by an epitaph.  
Leading on from a straight-lined entrance, Turbe al-Bey is composed of a complex succession of rooms, a result of successive extensions done according to various needs and at the expense of bordering buildings. Next to the tombs of the sovereigns and their families, the monument retains tombs belonging to a certain number of their ministers or of privileged faithful servants.  
Within this complex, it is the square room which houses the tombs of the “*bey*s of the throne”, in other words the tombs of those who actually reigned, that is the most attention-grabbing. It is a miniature replica of Ottoman mosques which themselves derived from Agia Sofia. Four fat pillars support a central dome which is buttressed by semi-domes on each of its four sides. Four smaller domes (cupolas) finish the roof, covering each of the room’s four corners. The interior decoration combines the Italian-style, polychrome marble inlaid work with the sculpted plaster perfectly.  
The tombs dug out of the earth are covered with marble chests which are abundant with low-relief motif ornamentation, above which rise prismatic columns engraved with epitaphs, which are surmounted by a hat when the deceased is a male. The turban or Fez-form sculpted in stone corresponds to the change of fashion within official costumes. The tombs of women are indicated by two marble plaques, and that which lies on the end where the head is placed is engraved with an epitaph.

es.name: Turbet el-Bey
description:
Las costumbres funerarias islámicas en general, y malikíes en particular, recomiendan a los creyentes la simplicidad y el anonimato de las tumbas. Los turcos hanafíes introdujeron, sin embargo, la costumbre de construir suntuosos monumentos a los muertos, llamados *turbé*s o *turbet*s. El Turbet el-Bey, elevado bajo el reinado de Alí Pachá II (1171/1758-1195/ 1781) alberga las sepulturas de la familia principesca husseiní. Presenta una imponente fachada, en gres ocre, en la que aparecen pilastras y entablados en piedra esculpida con motivos florales en bajorrelieve de estilo italianizante.  
Es interesante comparar esta fachada con la del Turbet el-Fellari, que ocupa el ángulo opuesto. Este monumento, que data del siglo XII/XVIII, debe inscribirse en la más pura tradición local. Cada una de las tres fachadas aparece adornada con una arquería ciega, y el arco central está horadado mediante una ventana con barrotes coronados por un epitafio.  
Después de una entrada recta, el monumento consiste, en realidad, en una sucesión compleja de salas, resultado de sucesivas ampliaciones, llevadas a cabo con los gastos de las construcciones limítrofes, a medida que se iban necesitando. Al lado de las tumbas de los soberanos y sus familias, el monumento guarda las de algunos de sus ministros y de sus fieles y privilegiados servidores.  
En este conjunto, llama especialmente la atención la sala cuadrada que cierra la tumba de los “beyes del trono”, es decir, la de aquellos que efectivamente reinaron. Se trata de una réplica en miniatura de las mezquitas otomanas, que estaban también inspiradas en la de Santa Sofía. Cuatro gruesos pilares sostienen una cúpula central apuntalada por varias semicúpulas sobre sus cuatro lados. En los ángulos de la sala, cuatro pequeñas cúpulas terminan la cubierta. La decoración interior alía perfectamente el revestimiento de mármol policromado, al gusto italiano, con los estucos.  
Las tumbas están excavadas en el suelo y cubiertas con sepulcros de mármol abundantemente adornados con bajorrelieves, debajo de los cuales se sitúan las columnas prismáticas, grabadas con epitafios y cubiertas con una toca, cuando el difunto era del sexo masculino. La forma en turbante o *tarbuch* esculpido en la piedra corresponde al cambio en la moda de los vestidos oficiales. Las tumbas de las mujeres están señaladas mediante dos placas de mármol; la que corresponde a la cabeza lleva un epitafio.

fr.name: Tourbet el-Bey
description:
Les coutumes funéraires musulmanes en général et malékites en particulier recommandent aux croyants la simplicité, voire l’anonymat des tombes. Les Turcs hanéfites avaient introduit l’habitude de construire de somptueux monuments aux morts, appelés *turbé*s ou *tourbet*s. Le Tourbet el-Bey, élevé sous le règne de Ali Pacha II (1171/1758-1195/1781), abrite les sépultures de la famille princière husseinite. Il présente une imposante façade en grès ocre d’où se détachent des pilastres et des entablements en pierre sculptés de motifs floraux en bas-relief de style italianisant.  
Il est intéressant de comparer cette façade à celle du Tourbet el-Fellari qui occupe l’angle opposé. Datant du XIIe/XVIIIe, ce monument s’inscrit dans la tradition locale. Chacune des trois façades est meublée d’une arcature aveugle, l’arc médian est creusé d’une fenêtre barreaudée que surmonte une épitaphe.  
Après une entrée droite, Tourbet el-Bey se compose d’une succession complexe de salles, résultant d’agrandissements successifs opérés aux dépens de bâtiments limitrophes, au fur et à mesure des besoins. Le monument garde, à côté des tombes des souverains et de leur famille, celle d’un certain nombre de leurs ministres ou de leurs serviteurs fidèles privilégiés.  
Parmi cet ensemble, la salle carrée renfermant les tombes des “*bey*s du trône”, c’est-à-dire ceux qui ont effectivement régné, retient l’attention. C’est une réplique en miniature des mosquées ottomanes, elles-mêmes dérivées de Sainte- Sophie. Quatre gros piliers soutiennent une coupole centrale contrebutée par demi-coupoles sur les quatre côtés. Aux angles de la salle, quatre coupolettes achèvent la couverture. La décoration intérieure allie parfaitement la marqueterie de marbre polychrome au goût italianisant, à la sculpture sur plâtre.  
Les tombes creusées dans le sol sont recouvertes de coffres de marbre, abondamment ornés de motifs en bas-relief, au-dessus desquels se dressent des colonnes prismatiques, gravées d’épitaphes et surmontées d’un couvre-chef, lorsque le défunt était de sexe masculin. La forme en turban ou en tarbouch sculpté dans la pierre correspond au changement de mode dans le costume officiel. Les tombes des femmes sont signalisées par deux plaques de marbre, celle qui est du côté de la tête est gravée d’une épitaphe.

ar.name: ابريق
description:
زخارف هندسية وزخارف نباتية من الذهب الأحمر والسائل تزين هذا الإبريق المصنوع من البورسلين الأبيض من تركيا العثمانية. يذكرنا الجسم على شكل طائر بقطع مماثلة من الدولة الأموية. كانت هذه الأنواع من الأواني تصب الماء ، المعطر غالبًا ، لأغراض الوضوء أو لتنظيف أيدي الضيوف قبل العيد.  
  
أثناء استعارة عناصر مثل الزهور وأوراق البيزلي والفاكهة من فن إزنيق ، من المحتمل أن يكون الحرفي قد صمم الإبريق للسوق المجري. مع تزايد الاهتمام بالخزف الآسيوي والعثماني في أوروبا في القرن التاسع عشر ، حاول الحرفيون من إيطاليا وفرنسا والمجر تقليد فخار إزنيق. في غضون ذلك ، أراد الحرفيون الأتراك أن يتناسبوا مع الذوق الأوروبي ، حيث صمموا الإنتاج العثماني النموذجي.  
  
يجسد هذا الإبريق الاتجاه العثماني الفخم لمزج التأثيرات من الصين وعصر النهضة في إيطاليا ومنطقة البلقان وأسلوب إزنيق. من هذا التقليد للفن من خلال الإعجاب المتبادل ، تظهر مجموعة من الأشياء التي تمت دراسة تفاعلها الفريد من نوعه حتى اليوم.

partner: متحف الشيخ فيصل بن قاسم ال ثاني

en.name: Ablution Ewer
description:
Geometric patterns and floral motifs in red and liquid gold adorn this white porcelain ewer from Ottoman Turkey. The bird-shaped body is reminiscent of similar pieces from the Umayyad dynasty. These types of vessels would pour water, often scented, for ablution purposes or to clean guests’ hands before a feast.  
  
While borrowing elements such as flowers, the paisley leaf and fruit from the Iznik art, a craftsman likely designed the ewer for the Hungarian market. With growing interest in Asian and Ottoman ceramics in 19th century Europe, craftsmen from Italy, France and Hungary attempted to imitate Iznik pottery. Meanwhile, Turkish artisans wished to suit the European palate, tailoring the typical Ottoman production.  
  
This ewer embodies the lavish Ottoman trend of blending influences from China, the Italian Renaissance, the Balkans and Iznik style. From this imitation of art through mutual admiration, new objects were created. Their unique interplay of styles is studied until today.
holder: Sheikh Faisal Bin Qassim Al Thani
keywords: Turkey; Ewer; Ablution; Porcelain
partner: Sheikh Faisal Bin Qassim Al Thani Museum (FBQ Museums)

en.name: Sanctuary of Our Lady of Cape Espichel
names: Santuário de Nossa Senhora do Cabo; Santuário de Nossa Senhora da Pedra Mua
description:
The sanctuary is located at the top of Cape Espichel. It has a U-shaped floor plan due to the pilgrim's lodging houses which formed a square. The houses are decked with continuous arcades and are very simply built, typical of the traditional architecture of the Lisbon and Setúbal Peninsulas. Centred at the far west-end of the square is Our Lady of the Cape Church.  
The church has a single, clear nave with two pulpits in the middle of it. Due to the design it can be attributed to João Antunes, architect of the Casa do Infantado nearby. The church was likely to have been commissioned by the Infant Francisco, King João V's brother and head of the brotherhood of Our Lady of the Cape. There is a large cross at the opposite end of the church, on the axis of the square. Continuing along this axis, the aqueduct meets the water house to supply the sanctuary with water. The water house is a hexagonal-shaped building with one door. It is equipped with an undulating dome and crowned with a lantern. Its construction dates to 1770, and was the initiative of King José I after he had stayed at the court of the sanctuary. At the same time, between 1760 and 1770, the sanctuary's infrastructure was improved with the construction of kitchens, an oven and wood store, stables, a water tank and an “opera house” – a small theatre with dressing rooms and a backstage area, which today is completely dilapidated.  
Separate from this group of buildings, is the Memory Hermitage, found near to where the sanctuary was founded. The building is cubic in form with a smooth reverse ogee dome. Despite not knowing the date of its construction it was probably rebuilt in the 17th century. It is decorated with 18th-century *azulejos,* depicting the legend of the Miraculous Finding of the Image of Our Lady at the site.

The origins of the cult date to the 15th century; most of the buildings date to the 17th and 18th centuries. A pilgrimage sanctuary with a U-shaped floor plan, it was created around pilgrim’s lodging houses that formed a square. The respective church, to which the lodging houses belonged, was at the far end of the square.
artist: King João I of Portugal (1357–1433; r. 1385–1433); Brotherhood of Nossa Senhora do Cabo Espichel (17th century–present); Casa do Infantado; King José I (1714–1777; r. 1750–1777)
Attributed to the architect João Antunes (1642–1712); painter: Lourenço da Cunha (active 1740–1743)
history:
The origins of the cult performed at the Sanctuary of Our Lady of Cape Espichel dates to the 15th century. Most of the buildings centre about the sanctuary, except for the Memory Hermitage, also known as Nossa Senhora da Pedra Mua Hermitage. The sanctuary and its associated buildings date to the 17th and 18th centuries, a period of pilgrimage which received royal attention and protection, especially during the reign of King José I.  
The origins of the sanctuary are connected to a legend, which relates that two elderly people – one from Caparica (on the south bank of the River Tagus) and another from Alcabideche (near Cascais) – dreamed about Our Lady appearing on top of the cliffs of Cape Pedra Mua riding a gigantic she-mule. Inspired by their dream they followed their calling and met at the top of the promontory where they found the miraculous image of Our Lady. The footprints of the she-mule left on the stones of the promontory continue to bear witness to the veracity of the legend, although in reality these are footprints of two types of dinosaur (one being the largest footprint of this type).
keywords: Sanctuary, miracle, legend, pilgrimage, *azulejos*, Sesimbra, Cape Espichel
tags: Sanctuary, miracle, legend, pilgrimage, azulejos, Sesimbra, Cape Espichel
partner: Institute for the Administration of Architectural and Archaeological Heritage -  IGESPAR

pt.name: *Santuário do Cabo Espichel*
names: Santuário de Nossa Senhora do Cabo; Santuário de Nossa Senhora da Pedra Mua
description: Santuário situado na ponta do promontório do cabo Espichel. Possui planta em U, gerada pelos edifícios de hospedagem dos romeiros, formando uma praça. Os edifícios de hospedagem, providos de uma arcaria contínua, são muito singelos e remetem para a arquitectura tradicional da região “saloia” (Penínsulas de Lisboa e de Setúbal). No extremo poente da praça, devidamente centrada, encontra-se a Igreja de Nossa Senhora do Cabo. É de nave única desimpedida e púlpito a meio da nave. Pode ser atribuída, pelo desenho, a João Antunes, na altura arquitecto da Casa do Infantado, e a quem poderá ter sido endereçada a encomenda, quase certamente, pelo infante D. Francisco, irmão de D. João V de Portugal e provedor da Irmandade de Nossa Senhora do Cabo. No eixo da praça, no lado oposto ao da igreja, encontra-se um cruzeiro. Na continuação deste eixo, numa colina, encontra-se a Casa da Água, ponto de chegada do aqueduto que servia o santuário. A Casa de Água é uma construção de planta hexagonal, com uma só porta, provida de uma cúpula ondeada de seis panos, coroada por um lanternim. A sua construção, em 1770, foi iniciativa de D. José I, na sequência da estada da corte, que se hospedou no Santuário. Nessa altura, entre 1760 e 1770, foi reforçado o equipamento “social” do santuário, com a edificação de cozinhas, casa do forno e da lenha, cavalariças, cisterna e uma “*casa da ópera*” – um pequeno teatro com camarins e bastidores, hoje completamente arruinado. À parte, separada deste conjunto, no lugar onde se terá dado a aparição, encontra-se a Ermida da Memória, edifício paralelepipédico com cúpula lisa contracurvada, de datação incerta, eventualmente reconstruído no século XVII e decorado de azulejos com a narrativa do milagre.

As origens do culto recuam até ao século XV, mas a maior parte dos edifícios é dos séculos XVII e XVIII. Santuário de peregrinação com planta em U, formado pelas hospedarias dos romeiros, com a respectiva igreja centrada num dos extremos da praça.
dates: Entre os séculos XV e XVIII
artist: Rei D. João I de Portugal (1357–1433; r. 1385–1433); Irmandade de Nossa Senhora do Cabo Espichel (séculos XVII-XXI); Casa do Infantado; rei D. José I de Portugal (1714–1777; r. 1750–1777).
Atribuído ao arquitecto João Antunes (1642–1712); pintor Lourenço da Cunha (activo 1740–1743).
history: A origem do culto que se presta no Santuário do Cabo Espichel remonta à Idade Média, com maior incidência a partir do século XV, embora a maioria dos edifícios que ali se encontra, exceptuando a Ermida da Memória, ou Ermida de Santa Maria da Pedra da Mua, seja já dos séculos XVII e XVIII, período que é também o de maior afluência de peregrinos, bem como o de maior atenção e protecção régias, especialmente no reinado de D. José I. A origem do Santuário deve-se a uma lenda segundo a qual uma velha de Caparica (margem Sul do Tejo) e um velho de Alcabideche (perto de Cascais) tiveram, ambos, o mesmo sonho, no qual aparecia a imagem de Nossa Senhora montada num burrico no cimo das pedras do Cabo da Pedra da Mua. Pondo-se a caminho, inspirados pelo sonho, encontraram-se no cimo do promontório e testemunharam a aparição que lhes tinha sido anunciada. As pegadas das patas do burrico ainda hoje atestam a veracidade do facto, marcadas nas pedras do promontório (na realidade, pegadas de dois tipos de dinossáurios, naquele que é um dos mais extensos trilhos deste tipo).
keywords: Santuário, milagre, lenda, peregrinação, azulejos, Sesimbra, Cabo Espichel.
tags: Santuário, milagre, lenda, peregrinação, azulejos, Sesimbra, Cabo Espichel.

en.name: Revolver
description: This is a solid-frame revolver with 9-chamber cylinder and 8 mm calibre. The ejector and the screw for attaching the cylinder to the frame are missing. This revolver is fitted with two grip silver plates, highly decorated with checking and with a lion under a palm tree on both sides. The screw to attach the plates is installed with the grip plated diamond shape. The base of the barrel is octagonal in shape and the barrel had an inverted lip at its end. On the crown, “R”, a star and “E” are the only visible markings on the right side of the barrel. Right under the screw of the ejector, the number 16 is engraved. Only the last digit “3” of the serial number is visible and most of it is under the museum's inventory number.
holder: Jordan Museum for Costumes and Jewellery, Department of Antiquities
keywords: Revolver; solid frame; 9-chamber cylinder; ejector; grip silver plates; checking; barrel; arms; armours; metalwork; war; warfare; military objects

en.name: Anatolian Railways
short_description: During the 19th century, new technologies radically transformed both travel and communications. The first railway in Anatolia was constructed between Izmir and Aydin. Ottoman railways were mainly built during the period of Abdülhamid II. The first railway in the Republic of Turkey was part of the İzmir-Aydın line, founded by a British company in 1860. The İzmir-Kasaba line was built in 1865, the Rumeli line in 1869-77, the Anatolia-Baghdad line in 1872 and the Mudanya-Bursa line in 1892.
holder: Istanbul University, Nadir Eserler Kütüphanesi (Rare Books Library)
keywords: Yıldız Album; II. Abdulhamid Han; Photograph Anatolian Railways
partner: Ministry of Culture and Tourism (General Directorate for Cultural Heritage and Museums)

en.name: Views of Syria
description: Collection of aerial views of historical monuments and cities of present-day Lebanon and Syria, taken approximately between 1925 and 1932 by the Jesuit missionary, explorer, and archaeologist Antoine Poidebard (1878–1955) and military pilots of the French Air Force. Considered the pioneer of aerial archaeology in the Middle East, Poidebard settled in Beirut in 1925 and was charged with mapping missions by the French mandatory authorities. With the logistical support of the French Air Force, he clocked up thousands of flying hours mainly above Lebanon and Syria, but also along the Mediterranean coast as far as Algeria and Tunisia. A highly talented amateur, he developed innovative technical processes and camera prototypes, paving the way for aerial archaeology as a scientific method.

en.name: Beirut Port before expansion
short_description: This photograph shows the Beirut port before its expansion. The dam was built under the command of Ibrahim Pasha. This old port underwent several important changes in the late 19th century, including the construction of a commercial tribunal and expansion of the port. This expansion involved the enlargement of existing buildings and filling areas of sea with rock brought in along the Nahr al-Kalb railway.

de.name: Katholische Zunftkirche St. Josef
description: Die Kirche ist zweistöckig angelegt. Während die Unterkirche aus zwei achteckigen Gruftkapellen gebildet wird, eine Vereinfachung gegenüber Herkomers Planung eines hl. Grabes, besteht das Obergeschoss aus zwei einfachen quadratischen Raumteilen für Langhaus und Chor. Die Zentralgestalt wird jeweils durch Eckausrundungen noch unterstrichen, und eine kräftige Arkade über Pilasterpfeilern trennt beide Raumteile deutlich. In der Perspektive fügt sich beides aber wieder zusammen: die raumhinterlegte Arkade wird zum Hauptmotiv, zum Würdezeichen des Hochaltars, der seinerseits an der Chorstirnwand nochmals von einer Arkade im Wandrelief hinterlegt ist. Schwung, aufgerichtete Proportionen und kräftige Akzente zeichnen diese Architektur aus und verleihen ihr einen Anspruch, der über eine einfache Landkapelle deutlich hinaus geht.

St. Josef in Bichlbach ist die einzige erhaltene Zunftkirche Österreichs. Darin, weniger in den durchaus beachtlichen baulichen und künstlerischen Qualitäten, liegt ihre eigentliche Bedeutung. Das Äußere der auf einem Hügel oberhalb des Dorfes gelegenen Kirche ist sehr schlicht, aber in der Raumanlage des zentralisierten Saalbaus mit leicht abgeschrägten Ecken und dem anschließendem Chor zeigt sich einiger baukünstlerischer Anspruch und Reiz. Die Raumwirkung wird indessen ganz durch den mächtigen Hochaltar beherrscht, wogegen die übrige Ausstattung zurücktritt.
artist: Pfarrer Lukas Egger/Zunft der Maurer- und Zimmerleute
history: Die Entstehung von St. Josef hängt unmittelbar mit den sozialen Verhältnissen des Außerfern zusammen, denn die Handwerker fanden hier im Sommer kaum Arbeit und mussten auf Wanderschaft gehen. Ihre Gottesdienste zum Abschied und zur Wiederkehr feierten sie gemeinsam in der Zunftkirche. Die Bruderschaft unter dem Patronat des hl. Josef, dem Schutzheiligen der Handwerker, gründete der umtriebige Pfarrer Lukas Egger 1690 (durch Kaiser Leopold I. 1694 bestätigt). Die Gründungsurkunde enthält bereits eine erste Planung des Kirchenbaus von der Hand des Füssener Baumeisters Herkomer, doch verzögerte sich die Ausführung. Nach neuen Plänen wurde der Bau schließlich 1710 begonnen und war nach ca. zwei Jahren weitgehend fertiggestellt. Die Weihe erfolgte indessen erst 1726.

en.name: Catholic Guild Church of St. Joseph
names: Church of the Brotherhood of Jesus, Mary, and Joseph for Craftsmen
description: The church is composed of two storeys. While the crypt is formed of two octagonal crypt chapels – a simplification of Herkomer’s plan for a holy sepulchre – the upper storey is composed of two simple quadratic spatial components for nave and choir. The centralised design is underlined by rounded corners. The powerfully built arcade-above-pilaster piers clearly divide the two sections, while reuniting the two in the overall prospect. Sweeping, erect proportions and bold accents lend the building qualities that clearly extend beyond that of a country chapel.

St. Joseph’s in Bichlbach is the only surviving guild church in Austria. This is its primary significance, as opposed to its architectural and artistic qualities. The exterior of the church located on a hill above the village is plain, but however the interior of the centralised hall building with lightly slanted corners and adjoining choir, displays architectural ambition and charm. Here the spatial impression is completely dominated by the mighty high altar.
artist: Parish Priest Lukas Egger/Guild of Masons and Carpenters

Architecture, first plan: Johann Jakob Herkomer (1652–1717); re-planning and construction work: Andreas Hafenegger (1666–1745); superstructure: Johann Georg Pauer [n.d.]; altar paintings, attributed to: Johannes Heel (1686–1749) or Paul Zeiller (1658–1738); crucifix: attributed to Andreas Thamasch (1639–1697)
history: The origin of St. Joseph’s is directly connected to the social conditions in Außerfern. In summer there was virtually no work for the craftsmen who were thus forced to take to the road as journeymen. Church services, held on their departure and return, were celebrated together in the guild church. The brotherhood under the patronage of St. Joseph, the patron saint of craftsmen, was founded by the parish priest Lukas Egger in 1690 (certified by Emperor Leopold I in 1694). The founding charter already contained initial plans for the church building drawn up by Herkomer, master builder of Füssen, however their execution was delayed. The building was finally begun in 1710 according to new plans and was largely completed in the space of two years. The consecration did not take place until 1726.

en.name: *St. Gertrude*
description:
St. Gertrude (626–659) was the daughter of Pepin I of Landen, the Prefect of the Palace of the Merovingian King Dagobert I of Austrasia. She was abbess of the Monastery of Nivelles (today in Belgium) founded by her mother Saint Itta of Aquitania. St. Gertrude is presented as a noble and independent woman who refused to marry because she wanted to be a nun. She devoted her life to the study of the Holy Scriptures and collaborated with the Irish saints Foillan and Ultan to assist the needy and promote Evangelisation.  
The Monastery of Arouca commissioned Jacinto Vieira to make a set of limestone sculptures of male Benedictine saints for the nave and a set of female saints for the choir, all of which were particularly venerated by the Cistercian Order. Almost unknown, Jacinto Vieira belonged to a group of Northern Portuguese sculptors, who, during the reign of King João V, sought to combine the national Portuguese aesthetics typical of the 17th century with the Italian aesthetic peculiar to the erudite Roman Baroque. Mainly an expert in sculpture in wood, Vieira managed to adapt his mastery in wood, acquired in the saint-making workshops, to stone sculpture.  
This image of St. Gertrude depicts her with an abbess' crosier and a medallion surrounded by a *gloria luminosa* filled with an inflamed heart with Baby Jesus, following the iconographic canons of the day and the austerity of the Cistercians. St. Gertrude stands out due to the elegance of her gesture, her contemplative facial expression and her mystical aura over the other nuns, all of them dressed with delicate pleated garments and habits with enormous sleeves, which are the main features of this set of sculptures.

St. Gertrude was canonised in 1677 and is an emblematic character both of the Benedictine and Cistercian orders. *St. Gertrude* is one of a set of stone sculptures from the Monastery of Arouca depicting the saints worshipped by the Cistercian Order to enhance their role in promoting the Teachings of Christ according to the Counter-Reformation.
holder: Real Irmandade da Rainha Santa Mafalda de Arouca, Museu de Arte Sacra de Arouca
place: Saint Mary’s Cistercian Monastery of Arouca
keywords: Sculpture; Counter-Reformation; Cistercian order; Benedictine order

pt.name: *Santa Gertrudes*
description:
Santa Gertrudes (626-659), filha de Pepino I de Landen, prefeito do palácio de Dagoberto I, rei merovíngio da Austrásia, foi abadessa do Mosteiro de Nivelles (actualmente na Bélgica), fundado por sua mãe, Santa Itta da Aquitânia. Desde cedo, manifestou forte vocação para a vida religiosa, rejeitando todos os pretendentes que a sua condição aristocrática lhe proporcionava e estudando com afinco as Sagradas Escrituras. Apoiada pelos irlandeses Santo Foillian e Santo Ultan, promoveu a evangelização e ajudou os mais carenciados.  
O Mosteiro de Arouca encomendou a Jacinto Vieira um conjunto de esculturas em pedra de Ançã, para a igreja, representando, na nave, santos beneditinos e, no coro, santas, todos especialmente venerados pela Ordem de Cister. Com um percurso de vida pouco conhecido, este artista pertence ao grupo de escultores nortenhos que, no reinado de D. João V, combinou a estética nacional seiscentista com os padrões da estética italiana do Barroco romano erudito. Sobretudo habituado a trabalhar em madeira, Jacinto Vieira transpôs para o calcário, sem dificuldade, toda a mestria adquirida, provavelmente, nas oficinas de santeiros.  
Esta imagem da santa, representada com o báculo de abadessa e um coração inflamado, com o Menino Jesus dentro de um medalhão, envolto por uma *glória* luminosa, segue os ditames do cânone iconográfico e da austeridade cisterciense. Tal como as outras monjas, trajadas a rigor, com vestes de pregueado finíssimo e enormes mangas do hábito, elementos escultóricos essenciais destas peças, Santa Gertrudes destaca-se pela elegância da pose e pela expressão contemplativa do olhar, bem como pela aura mística que irradia da sua figura.

Santa Gertrudes, canonizada em 1677 e muito popular na época barroca, é uma figura emblemática para as ordens beneditina e cisterciense. Integrada no conjunto de estátuas de pedra de santos do Mosteiro de Arouca, reafirma, no contexto da Contra-Reforma, a importância dos mosteiros cistercienses como difusores dos ensinamentos de Cristo.

en.name: Madrasa al-Taziyya
description:
Although the inscription on the southern façade above the main window commemorates the death of the *amir* Taz in 763/1362, it does not refer to the date of the construction of the building or the founding of its *waqf*. However, by relying on architectural evidence, the mausoleum that has been used in the past as a *madrasa*, was probably built in 762/1361.  
Its founder was the Amir Taz who was a Mamluk slave of Sultan al-Nasir Muhammad Ibn Qalawun. He held various significant posts during the Mamluk Dynasty such as that of the sultan’s butler (*saqi*), which was a very delicate post during this period. The emblem of the butler was a chalice, which explains the existence of one amidst the above-mentioned inscription plaque. After he had attained the post of Governor of Aleppo, his luck declined; he was arrested and later exiled to Jerusalem where he resided and established Madrasa al-Taziyya. Many historical references mention him, his relatives, and others whom he freed from bondage in Jerusalem.  
Despite the fact that the foundation inscription refers to the edifice as a mausoleum, reality and documents reveal it had various functions. Salaries were paid to its jurists, readers and tutors; these were covered by its *waqf*, which comprised the village of al-Miniya, which lay northwest of Lake Tiberias.  
The Taziyya has one western façade that is divided into two parts, lower and upper. The lower part has a simple door that leads into the interior. To the west of the entrance is a rectangular window that is surrounded by a deep-set frame and covered by Mamluk-style metal grills. On top of it is a lintel upon which a foundation inscription was engraved. Above it is another lintel of beautiful joggled inlay. The stones of this part have been constructed in the *ablaq* style. The upper part of the façade, on the other hand, has well-arranged courses and a wooden *mashrabiyya* dating back to the 13th/19th century, and three windows above it.  
The building consists of two floors. The first floor has two parts; the southern part has an entrance, stairs and two halls, each of which is covered by a cross vault. The northern part of the first floor also has two large halls that are reached through a corridor that lies to the east of the halls in the southern part. There is also an *iwan* that leads to a large, cross-vaulted hall and which overlooks the main road from the south. Some residential quarters are found to the north, most of which were rebuilt during the Ottoman period, and some of which have been covered by a small, shallow vault.

es.name: Madrasa al-Taziyya
description:
Aunque existe una inscripción en la fachada sur, sobre la ventana principal, que hace referencia a la muerte del *emir* Taz en 763/1362, no aparece ninguna fecha concreta en relación con el momento de creación del *waqf* o la construcción del edificio. Sin embargo, las características arquitectónicas del mausoleo, que fue utilizado como *madrasa*, permiten situar su edificación alrededor de 762/1361.  
El fundador de este monumento fue el *emir* Taz, un esclavo mameluco del sultán al-Nasir Muhammad Ibn Qalawun. Taz ocupó diversos cargos importantes en el Estado mameluco; el primero fue el de copero (*saqi*), un cargo delicado en la época, lo que explica la presencia de un cáliz en su escudo de armas, como se vio anteriormente.  
Tras ser ascendido al cargo de gobernador de Alepo, su estrella comenzó a declinar, fue detenido y posteriormente exiliado a Jerusalén, donde vivió y fundó la *madrasa* al-Taziyya. En las fuentes históricas hay alusiones al emir Taz, sus familiares y algunos de sus libertos que vivieron en Jerusalén.  
Aunque la inscripción fundacional identifica el edificio como mausoleo, la realidad y los documentos confirman que el edificio tenía diversos usos. En él desempeñaban sus ocupaciones alfaquíes, recitadores, maestros y otras personas que recibían sus salarios del *waqf* del edificio que incluía el pueblo de al-Minya, al noroeste del lago Tiberíades. Al-Taziyya tiene una única fachada, al oeste, dividida horizontalmente en dos partes. En la parte inferior, una puerta sencilla conduce al interior; al oeste de la entrada hay una ventana rectangular, protegida por rejas de estilo mameluco. Sobre la ventana aparece un primer dintel, en el que se ha tallado la inscripción fundacional, y luego un segundo dintel delicadamente aparejado. Las piedras con las que está construida esta parte están dispuestas según la técnica *ablaq*. La parte superior de la fachada se distingue por la disposición simétrica de las hileras de piedra; las tres ventanas en saledizo están realizadas con *machrabiyya*s que se remontan al siglo XIII/XIX.  
La *madrasa* dispone de dos niveles. La planta baja tiene dos partes; la sección sur consta de una entrada, una escalera y dos grandes salas, cubiertas por sendas bóvedas por arista. La parte norte también consta de dos grandes salas, a las que se accede a través de un pasillo que se encuentra al este de la parte sur, y de un *iwan* que conduce a una gran bóveda por arista que da a la calle principal, al sur. En el flanco norte, distintas estancias, la mayoría reconstruidas en la época otomana, se utilizan como viviendas. Algunas fueron cubiertas por una pequeña bóveda rebajada.

fr.name: Madrasa al-Taziyya
description:
Si la date de la mort de l’émir Taz est fournie par l’inscription (763/1362) dominant la fenêtre principale de la façade sud, nous ne disposons pas de renseignements explicites sur la date de construction du bâtiment ou de constitution des *waqfs* dont il relevait. Toutefois, les caractéristiques architecturales du mausolée, qui dans le passé a servi de *madrasa*, permettent d’en situer la construction autour de 762/1361.  
La fondation de l’établissement est due à l’émir Taz, un esclave mamelouk du sultan al-Nasir Muhammad Ibn Qalawun. Parmi nombre de fonctions éminentes dans la dynastie mamelouke, il exerça notamment celle d’échanson (*saqi*) – une charge sensible à l’époque –, ce qui explique la présence d’un calice dans ses armoiries, comme on l’a vu plus haut.  
Une fois parvenu au poste de gouverneur d’Alep, sa chance commença à tourner; après son arrestation, il fut envoyé en exil à Jérusalem où il finit par s’installer et fonder la *madrasa* al-Taziyya. Le personnage de Taz, sa famille et certains de ses affranchis qui vivaient à Jérusalem nous sont connus par de nombreuses sources historiques.  
Bien que l’inscription fondatrice l’évoque comme un mausolée, la réalité aussi bien que les documents prouvent que l’édifice remplissait plusieurs fonctions. Y étaient rétribués des oulémas, des lecteurs et des répétiteurs, dont les salaires étaient payés grâce au *waqf* du bâtiment, qui comprenait le village de al-Minya, au nord-ouest du lac de Tibériade. La Taziyya possède une seule façade, à l’ouest, divisée horizontalement en deux parties. La partie inférieure est percée d’une simple porte conduisant à l’intérieur. À l’ouest de l’entrée s’ouvre une fenêtre rectangulaire ceinte d’un profond encadrement et protégée par des grilles métalliques de style mamelouk. La fenêtre est surmontée d’un premier linteau sur lequel est gravée l’inscription fondatrice, puis d’un second linteau délicatement appareillé. Les pierres de cette zone sont montées selon la technique *ablaq*. Quant à la partie supérieure de la façade, elle se distingue par ses assises bien coordonnées; trois fenêtres sont surmontées d’encorbellements en *machrabiyya* du XIIIe/XIXe siècle.  
La *madrasa* est un bâtiment à deux niveaux. Le rez-de-chaussée comprend deux parties; la section méridionale présente une entrée, un escalier et deux grandes salles, chacune d’elles étant couverte par une voûte d’arêtes. La partie septentrionale de ce même niveau comporte elle aussi deux grandes salles que l’on atteint par un couloir situé à l’est des pièces de la partie méridionale, ainsi qu’un *iwan* conduisant à une grande voûte d’arêtes donnant sur la rue principale au sud. Sur le flanc nord, un certain nombre de pièces, pour la plupart reconstruites à l’époque ottomane, servent de logements. Certaines ont été couvertes d’une petite voûte surbaissée.

en.name: Las palabras las lleva el viento
description:
Alberto Gambale was born in Ferrara. He trained at the Academia de Bellas Artes de Bolonia, before embarking on an immense search and experience within the pictorial and sculptural field, discovering glass as the core material for his work. He perfected his work by way of many other courses with significant artists within the contemporary glass field, such as: Detleft Tonz, specialist in Tiffany glass; Gil Reinolds, German-American Bullseye Artist; Elimer Preder; the great, internationally renowned Italian-American artist, Narcissus Quagliata and S&K Higuchi, Japanese experts in molten glass.  
In 1992, he participated in the Polariscope programme, that took place at the Fundación Centro Nacional del Vidrio, in which glassworkers of various nationalities were involved. They all created a piece inspired by a common topic: water. Since, Alberto Gambale has maintained contact with the Escuela del Vidrio at the Foundation, providing several monographic courses, both in stained glass and alternative techniques.  
He currently works in his workshop in Ferrara, experimenting in the field of molten glass, as we can observe in this piece, in addition to teaching classes in different Glass Schools, such as the Escuela de Vidrio de Bolzano and the Escuela de Vidrio de la Real Fábrica de Cristales.
holder: Technological Glass Museum. Royal Factory of Glass and Crystal of La Granja
keywords: Italy; Glass sculpture; kiln casting; Gambale
partner: Technological Glass Museum. Royal Factory of Glass and Crystal of La Granja

es.name: Las palabras las lleva el viento
description:
Alberto Gambale nació en Ferrara. Se formó en la Academia de Bellas Artes de Bolonia, siguiendo posteriormente con una inmensa búsqueda y experiencia en el campo pictórico y escultórico, encontrando en el vidrio la materia principal para su trabajo. Se perfeccionó en muchos otros cursos con artistas de gran importancia en el campo del vidrio contemporáneo como: Detleft Tonz, especialista en vidrio Tiffany; Gil Reinolds, artista alemán-americano de la Bullseye Art; Elimer Preder; el gran artista italo-americano conocido mundialmente Narcissus Quagliata y los expertos en pasta de vidrio japoneses S&K Higuchi.  
En 1992 participó en el programa *Polariscopio* que tuvo lugar en la Fundación Centro Nacional del Vidrio, en el que intervinieron vidrieros de distintas nacionalidades. Todos crearon una pieza inspirada en un tema común: el agua. Desde entonces, Alberto Gambale ha mantenido contacto con la Escuela del Vidrio de la Fundación, impartiendo varios cursos monográficos tanto en vidrieras como en técnicas alternativas.  
Actualmente trabaja en su taller de Ferrara experimentando en el campo de la pasta de vidrio, como vemos en esta pieza y ha colaborado impartiendo clases  
en diferentes Escuelas de Vidrio como son la Escuela de Vidrio de Bolzano y la Escuela del Vidrio de la Real Fábrica de Cristales.

en.name: *Panoramic View of Makkah - Arabia (West Asia). Panoramic View of Makkah during the Celebration of the Pilgrimage of the Muslims to the Kaaba, where the religious treasure is guarded*
names: *Vista Panoramica de la Meca - Arabia (Asia Occidental). Vista Panoramica de la Meca Al Celebrarse una Peregrinacion de los Mahometos á la Kaaba Donde se custodia el tesoro religioso*
short_description: This coloured print, perhaps from a late 19th-century, Spanish newspaper or magazine, shows a birds-eye view of the city of Makkah with the Holy Mosque and Ka'bah at the centre. The view was recorded from one of the rugged mountains surrounding the city. Hundreds of pilgrims are seen to approach from afar and converge on the city gates. that lead to the sanctuary. The print shows close compositional similarities to an early 19th century drawing by the English officer and artist Charles Hamilton Smith (1776-1859). Smith, although not known to have visited the Arabian peninsula, produced an album of drawings - possibly in turn taken from older engravings - with views from Syria, Persia and Arabia sometime between 1818 and 1846.
holder: Sharjah Museum of Islamic Civilisation / Sharjah Museums Authority
keywords: Ka'bah

en.name: Dish with stylised bird.
description: A deep dish with curved sides and a flat base, decorated with a large figure of a stylised bird with filiform, almost plant-like, long wings. The body is rendered using a series of rectangular panels filled with thick zigzag lines. The base of the dish is mostly decorated with large flowering bushes, palmettes and clusters of small dots within a frame consisting of a fringed motif that runs below a brim painted in solid lustre.
The decoration of this deep dish is typical of late Valencian production, characterised by flowering bushes, large birds and red lustre.
holder: Museum of Civilisations | Museum of Oriental Art “Giuseppe Tucci”
dates: Hegira end of 12th century / AD end of 18th century.
keywords: Dish; lustre; Mudéjar art; floral decoration; figurative decoration
partner: Museum of Civilisations | Museum of Oriental Art

es.name: Plato con ave estilizada.
description: Plato hondo de paredes curvas y base plana, decorado con una gran ave estilizada de alas alargadas y filiformes, de aspecto casi vegetal, mientras que el cuerpo consiste en una serie de rectángulos rellenos de trazos gruesos en zigzag. La superficie del fondo del plato está decorada, en gran parte, con frondosos arbustos en flor, palmetas y conjuntos de puntitos, rodeados por un motivo de flecos que recorre las paredes por debajo del borde pintado en reflejo metálico compacto.
Pieza que presenta en su decoración elementos muy típicos de los productos valencianos de la época más tardía.
holder: Museo de Civilizaciones | Museo de Arte Oriental “Giuseppe Tucci”
dates: Finales del siglo XVIII d. C.

partner: Museo de Civilizaciones | Museo de Arte Oriental

fr.name: Plat avec figure d’oiseau stylisé.
description: Ce plat creux à marli bombé sur base plate est orné d'une grande figure d'oiseau stylisé aux ailes longues et aux plumes filiformes, d'aspect presque végétal ; le corps est rendu avec une série de petits panneaux rectangulaires constitués de traits épais et sinueux. Le fond est essentiellement orné de rameaux fleuris, de palmettes, de groupes de pointillés, à l'intérieur d'un cadre formé d'un motif frangé qui se développe sous le bord peint en lustre compact.
Cet objet présente, dans son décor, des éléments très typiques des produits de Valence (Espagne) d'époque plus tardive.

it.name: Piatto con figura di uccello stilizzato.
description: Il piatto fondo a parete ricurva su base piana è decorato con una grande figura di uccello stilizzato dalle ali lunghe e filiformi, di aspetto quasi vegetale, mentre il corpo è reso con una serie di pannellature rettangolari campite da grossi tratti a serpentina. La superficie del fondo risulta per lo più ornata con grossi cespugli fioriti, palmette, gruppi di piccoli punti, entro una cornice formata da un motivo frangiato, che corre al di sotto dell'orlo dipinto a lustro compatto.
L'esemplare mostra, nella decorazione, elementi assai tipici dei prodotti valenzani di epoca più tarda.

de.name: Inneres nach Osten
description: Das von der frühbarocken Ausstattung dominierte Raumbild teilt sich in zwei horizontale Zonen, einer unteren mit Seitenkapellen und Altären und einer oberen mit Emporen und Gewölbezone, die durch den kräftigen, schweren Stuck und die buntfarbigen Freskenfelder bestimmt wird. Die Altäre folgen dem strengen frühbarocken Ädikula-Schema und sind alle in Schwarz und Gold gefasst. Der Hochaltar mit seinem triumphal inszenierten Auszug bildet die Verbindung zwischen beiden Zonen. Der indirekte Lichteinfall über Kapellen und Emporen trägt wesentlich dazu bei, den Kirchenraum als Sakraltheater wirken zu lassen.
artist: Christoph Gumpp; Bernardo Pasquale; Kaspar Waldmann

en.name: Interior, facing east
description: The spatial image, dominated by the Early Baroque fittings, is divided into two zones, a lower with side chapels and altars and an upper with choir lofts and vault, which are characterised by the bold, heavy stucco and the colourful fresco panels. The altars are arranged according to the strict Early Baroque aedicula scheme and are all framed in black and gold. The high altar with its triumphal altar crown forms the connection between the two zones. The indirect light falling on chapels and choir lofts plays a decisive role in generating the atmosphere of a scared theatre.
place: Catholic Collegiate Church of St. Lawrence and St. Stephen
artist: Christoph Gumpp the younger (1600–1672); Bernardo Pasquale [n.d.]; Kaspar Waldmann (1657–1720)

en.name: Little Sicily
short_description: Pictured here is an area, near the port of Tunis, where many immigrants from southern Italy had settled. Between 1865 and 1900, hundreds of small one or two-bedroom houses were built in the lower part of the Avenue Jules Ferry (today Avenue Habib-Bouguiba). The layout of the port allowed for the a rapid increase in the number of residents; a great many (mostly Sicilian) workers settled around the warehouses and workshops. Little Sicily therefore became both the home of the European working classes and the centre of the city's industrial activity. As Gaston Loth described it in 1905, "It's still Sicily, the children live in the streets, speak Arabic but also French, it's a like a swarm of lewd, barely dressed sparrows."
holder: Institut Supérieur d’Histoire Contemporaine de la Tunisie
keywords: Italians in Tunisia; La Goulette
partner: Higher Institute for the Study of Contemporary History of Tunisia, University of Manouba

fr.name: La petite Sicile
short_description: Agglomération à proximité du port de Tunis où s’étaient entassés les immigrants de l’Italie méridionale. Entre 1865 et 1900, des centaines de maisonnettes d’une ou deux pièces couvrirent la partie basse de l’avenue Jules-Ferry, actuelle avenue Habib-Bouguiba. L’aménagement du port fit accroître le phénomène d’occupation du sol ; beaucoup d’ouvriers essentiellement siciliens s’installèrent autour des entrepôts et des ateliers. La petite Sicile devint à la fois le lieu de résidence du prolétariat européen et celui des activités industrielles de la ville. Gaston Loth le décrit en ces termes en 1905 : “C’est encore la Sicile, les enfants vivent dans la rue, parlent l’arabe mais aussi le français, c’est une nuée de moineaux paillards à peine vêtus.”
holder: Institut supérieur d’Histoire contemporaine de la Tunisie
keywords: Italiens en Tunisie; La Goulette
partner: Institut Supérieur d’histoire contemporaine de la Tunisie, Université de la Manouba

en.name: Tourists climbing the Great Pyramid of Giza, Egypt
